# Moving an ASE script to rgmin.optimize

The maturin package `python/` provides `rgmin.optimize`. Replace

```python
from ase.optimize import BFGS, LBFGS, FIRE
```

with

```python
from rgmin.optimize import BFGS, LBFGS, FIRE
```

`LBFGSLineSearch`, `FIRE2`, and `GPMin` match those ASE names (see
@@rst::doc:`gpmin`@@ for GPMin hyperparameters and step-cap behavior).
The other gradient methods of `Session` are `SR1`, `SR2`, `SteepestDescent`,
`BarzilaiBorwein`, `Adam`, the nonlinear CG family, `EonCG`, `NewtonCG`
and `NewtonPCG`.
Importing `rgmin` does not import ASE. The classes do, when they are constructed.

Each class is an `ase.optimize.optimize.Optimizer`. `run`, `irun`, `attach`,
`trajectory` and `logfile` are ASE's. The step reads and writes
`self.optimizable`, so `FixAtoms`, `FixedLine`, `FixCartesian`, `FixedPlane`
and the cell filters work.

`LBFGS` uses ASE's length control unless `eon_cap=True`. `Adam` takes
`learning_rate` (default 0.02) as the session step scale. On this line the
session normalizes Adam's direction to unit per-atom length before that
scale, and `maxstep` still caps the longest atom. `BFGS` and `FIRE` on a
cell filter reach the same minimum as ASE; their iterates are not ASE's,
because the 0.6.0 session rescales the first BFGS step and integrates FIRE
on its own schedule. `LBFGS` on the same filters keeps ASE's iterates.

A restart file replays the recorded evaluations into a fresh session and
refuses a file written by another class or with parameters that no longer
match. The nanobind classes live in `rgmin.ase` and are a separate binding.

`rgmin.ase.BFGSLineSearch` is also exported as `QuasiNewton`.
`rgmin.ase.LBFGSLineSearch` subclasses `rgmin.ase.LBFGS`. Both match the
ASE 3.29.0 constructors
([BFGSLineSearch](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.29.0/ase/optimize/bfgslinesearch.py),
[LBFGSLineSearch](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.29.0/ase/optimize/lbfgs.py),
[QuasiNewton](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.29.0/ase/optimize/__init__.py)).
`c1=0.23`, `c2=0.46`, `alpha`, `stpmax=50`, `memory=100`, and `maxstep`
are the ASE values. `alpha` is the fixed inverse-Hessian scale `1/alpha`
on the Rust BFGS or L-BFGS session. The session runs a port of ASE's
[LineSearch](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.29.0/ase/utils/linesearch.py).
The first trial is the full quasi-Newton step and `stpmax` bounds the
step multiplier. `maxstep` limits how far an atom moves from one trial
to the next, so one step can move an atom further than `maxstep`. A
failed search leaves the atoms where they were and raises
`RuntimeError("LineSearch failed!")`, as ASE does. An opening step above
`stpmax`, so any `stpmax` below 1, fails that way. ASE 3.29 ends a
search successfully on its warnings, including a trial at `stpmax`, and
so does rgmin. `damping` is stored and, as in ASE, does not scale a
line-search step.

Five differences remain. The search stops after `linesearch_maxiter`
trials, 20 by default, where ASE has no limit; running out raises the
same `RuntimeError`. A `maxstep` of zero is a safety stop: ASE scales a
later zero increment by 0/0 and the search does not finish, while rgmin
keeps the first trial at the start and stops before the oracle sees a
non-finite coordinate. The BFGS update skips a pair when ASE does, on
`no_update`, a nonpositive step length, or a directional derivative
whose magnitude did not fall, and it still declines a pair with
nonpositive curvature. ASE's unconditional L-BFGS pair is not
reproduced. A `maxmove` is refused, because it would cap the step
outside ASE's search. `restart` replays the rgmin
evaluation log; it does not read ASE's Hessian JSON, and
`replay_trajectory` is not ASE's Hessian replay. The BFGS line-search
log adds ASE's force-call column. The L-BFGS line-search log keeps the
shared `Step`, `Time`, `Energy`, `fmax` columns.

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/bench-gate.org`

# Compare repeated runs

`bench/gate` reads the CSV written by `bench/atomistic` and decides
whether a candidate reached the same stationary point as a baseline in
fewer force calls. The comparison sits beside Goswami, AIP Adv. (2025),
doi:10.1063/5.0283639.

Install and run it with the pixi environment `gate` (numpy 2.2.6, scipy
1.15.3). Matplotlib is optional and is used only for `--plot`.

```bash
pixi run -e gate gate results.csv --pair lbfgs-exp`lbfgs-wolfe --pair fire-exp`fire --pair cg-exp=cg-wolfe
```

Exit 0 is a pass, 1 is a fail, 2 is undecided, and 3 is a contract or
argument error. The target is the win probability over the suite's
start distribution. A start is one `(system, seed)`.

## Contract

A file with no version marker, or `# rggate-csv 1` (minor numbers
allowed), is contract version 1. Any other major version is refused.

Required columns:

`system,method,seed,converged,iters,calls,energy,fmax,wall_s`

Optional: `pot_s`, `overhead_us_per_iter`, `endpoint`, `reference`,
`dim`, `threads`. `dim` is the free coordinate count, three times the
number of moving atoms. Frozen atoms are excluded, because `fmax` and
the energy bound cover only those atoms. `reference` is an energy, or
a path to an endpoint file. An endpoint file has optional `energy` and
`cell` lines, then `x y z`. A zero cell is a free cluster.

## Same stationary point

Precedence on one start: an explicit `reference`, then the baseline
endpoint from that start when the baseline converged, then the lowest
converged energy only with `--reference lowest`. Otherwise the two
runs are compared with each other.

A free cluster is Kabsch-rotated after centering. A periodic cell is
not rotated: after the minimum-image map only the mean displacement is
removed. The energy window is `--e-tol` (default 1e-4 eV) when the atom
count `N` is unknown, and `e_tol + N * max(fmax) * rmsd_tol` when `N`
is known from `dim / 3` or the endpoint. Each pair prints
`window_fallback`, the number of starts judged with the `e_tol`
window. An energy-only split with unknown `N` is an upper bound on a
real basin split. Without endpoints the summary says `energy-only`.

Per-method Kaplan-Meier curves and profiles count a converged run as a
success unless an explicit reference or `--reference lowest` is in
force. An unconverged run is right-censored at its call count. The
median interval is Brookmeyer-Crowley on the log-log Greenwood band
(Kaplan and Meier, JASA 53, 457, 1958,
doi:10.1080/01621459.1958.10501452).

## Profiles

Dolan-Moré at tau 1, 1.5, 2, 4 and 8 (Math. Program. 91, 201, 2002,
doi:10.1007/s101070100263). Moré-Wild at alpha 10, 50, 100, 500 and
1000 in force-call units, or `alpha (n + 1)` when `dim` is set (SIAM J.
Optim. 20, 172, 2009, doi:10.1137/080724083). Pairwise fractions when
more than two methods are present (Gould and Scott, ACM TOMS 43, 2016,
doi:10.1145/2950048).

## Calls and the walk

Both runs in the same basin form the BCa sample (Efron, JASA 82, 171,
1987, doi:10.1080/01621459.1987.10478410). The interval resamples
systems, then starts within each drawn system. It is printed when the
number of systems is at least `--min-clusters` (default 10). Below
that the cluster bounds are `na` and the i.i.d. interval is the
diagnostic. The geometric mean uses `math.fsum`. `n` is the number of
same-basin starts. `clusters` is the number of systems in that sample.

A basin split (both converged, different basins) is counted with a
Clopper-Pearson interval and is not a loss. Gehan scoring handles the
rest: a candidate that stops early without converging does not win.
Indeterminate starts are dropped from the walk and counted.

Systems are shuffled with Philox, starts are shuffled within a system,
and a round robin visits one start from each system. The seed is mixed
into Philox key word 1. Stream and pair index sit in counter words 2
and 3.

With `k` pairs each walk uses `alpha / k`. The header prints
`alpha_pair`. The default boundary is the normal mixture of Howard,
Ramdas, McAuliffe, and Sekhon, Ann. Stat. 49, 1055 (2021),
doi:10.1214/20-AOS1991, with `V_t = t/4`. `rho` minimises the width at
`--plan-n` (default 50) for `alpha_pair` and is printed. `decide_min`
is the first number of informative starts at which an all-wins or
all-losses walk can cross. Before that count the pair line says
`forced=yes`. At the default horizon and one pair, `decide_min` is 11.
The walk stops when the interval excludes `0.5 - --margin`. The
summary prints `starts_used` and the per-system win, loss,
indeterminate and split counts.

`--boundary agrapa` uses one signed approximate-GRAPA stake from
Waudby-Smith and Ramdas, J. R. Stat. Soc. B (2024),
doi:10.1093/jrsssb/qkad009, clipped at 3/4 of full Kelly. It is not the
hedged capital process. The time-uniform guarantee is the sequential
test of Wald, Ann. Math. Stat. 16, 117 (1945),
doi:10.1214/aoms/1177731118.

`--jobs` only splits the per-method Kaplan-Meier curves, then joins
them in method-name order. The bootstrap stays serial, and the summary
text is the same for `--jobs 1`, `2`, and `N`.

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/c-abi.org`

# C and C++ ABI

Solvers live in Rust. Geometry hosts that call one outer iteration at
a time hold an opaque `rgmin_solver_t`; scripts that want a one-shot
solve still call `rgmin_minimize`. Every vector is a dlpk
`DLManagedTensorVersioned` tensor.

## Install

```bash
cargo cinstall --prefix=/usr/local --features capi
```

`cargo cinstall` comes from cargo-c (@@rst::doc:`install`@@).
That installs the hand-written `include/rgmin.h`, the C++ wrappers
under `include/rgmin/` and `include/xts/`, and `dlpack/dlpack.h`.
The pkg-config file is `rgmin`. A C or C++ file includes `rgmin.h`
and links with `pkg-config --cflags --libs rgmin`. The crate version
macros are `RGMIN_H_MAJOR`, `RGMIN_H_MINOR`, and `RGMIN_H_PATCH`.
HiGHS `HighsInt` is not a type in this header. The constrained
setters take `int32_t` and the closed `rgmin_highs_*` enums.

Pass `--features capi`. The C symbols are compiled only with that
feature. `cbindgen` output is not installed.

## Start from the defaults

Every struct a caller fills in has an initializer that returns the Rust
defaults. A caller must start each struct from its initializer and
assign only the fields it changes.

| Struct                  | Initializer                     |
|-------------------------+---------------------------------|
| `rgmin_control_t`       | `rgmin_control_default()`       |
| `rgmin_exp_t`           | `rgmin_exp_default()`           |
| `rgmin_scg_params_t`    | `rgmin_scg_params_default()`    |
| `rgmin_scg_options_t`   | `rgmin_scg_options_default()`   |
| `rgmin_eigen_params_t`  | `rgmin_eigen_params_default()`  |
| `rgmin_eigen_options_t` | `rgmin_eigen_options_default()` |
| `rgmin_rcg_options_t`   | `rgmin_rcg_options_default()`   |
| `rgmin_precon_t`        | `rgmin_precon_init(&p, kind)`   |

A field that a later revision adds then holds its default without a
change to the caller. A struct declared without an initializer holds
stack bytes in the fields the caller does not set, and a brace or
designated initializer sets them to zero, which is not every field's
default. A stray positive `noise_eps` turns the noise-floor stop on, and
a session then stays at its start point. The `rgmin_*_default` functions
are `abi_minor` 46, and `xts.h` names them `xts_*_default`.
`rgmin_rcg_options_default` is `abi_minor` 65.

## Control layout

Layout revision 6 adds `require_convergence` to `rgmin_control_t`,
which grows from 56 to 64 bytes on a 64-bit target, and `converged` to
`rgmin_report_t`. A binary built against revision 5 passes the shorter
struct, so each exported entry that takes a `rgmin_control_t` reads
only the fields through `noise_c`, `require_convergence` keeps its
default 0, and the report is written only through `stop`. The exported
`rgmin_control_default` still returns the revision 5 struct.

`rgmin.h` turns those names into inline functions that pass
`sizeof(rgmin_control_t)` to a `_sized` symbol, such as
`rgmin_minimize_opts_sized` and `rgmin_solver_create_sized`, and
`rgmin_control_default` calls `rgmin_control_init(&c, sizeof c)`. A
program built against this header has every field read and the whole
report written without a source change. The size has the meaning of
`rgmin_precon_t.struct_size`: `RGMIN_CONTROL_REVISION5_SIZE` is the
revision 5 struct, a larger size than this build's struct leaves the
extra bytes unread, and any other size returns
`RGMIN_INVALID_PARAMETER` (a null session from
`rgmin_solver_create_sized`) without a read. A caller that resolves
symbols at run time calls the `_sized` names to have
`require_convergence` read.

Layout revision 7, at `abi_minor` 68, adds `noise_eps_f` after
`require_convergence`, and the struct grows from 64 to 72 bytes on a
64-bit target. `RGMIN_CONTROL_REVISION6_SIZE` is the revision 6 struct:
an entry told that size reads the fields through `require_convergence`,
writes the whole report, and leaves `noise_eps_f` at its default 0.
`rgmin_control_init` fills any of the three layouts.

`noise_eps_f` is the noise of the objective value, and a value that is
not positive leaves the test off. With `c` the factor `noise_c`, a line
search that finds no trial whose decrease clears `c * noise_eps_f`
stops with `RGMIN_STOP_NOISE_FLOOR`, and so does a Newton-CG run
(`rgmin_minimize_hvp`, `rgmin_minimize_hvp_precond`, `RGMIN_NEWTON_CG`,
`RGMIN_NEWTON_PCG`) when a trust region trial is refused while the
model predicts a reduction of at most `c * noise_eps_f`. The entry
returns `RGMIN_SUCCESS` and writes the last accepted point to `x`.
Without it, that Newton-CG run shrinks its radius to the floor and
returns `RGMIN_INVALID_PARAMETER` with "trust region collapsed" in
`rgmin_last_error`, and `x` stays at the start. Set it to a few units
in the last place of the objective value when the value is large
against the decrease a step can still make:

```c
rgmin_control_t ctrl = rgmin_control_default();
ctrl.gtol = 1e-10;
ctrl.noise_eps_f = 4.0 * DBL_EPSILON * fabs(value_at_start);
```

`report.converged` is 0 at that stop unless the gradient norm is below
`gtol`, and `require_convergence` still returns `RGMIN_NOT_CONVERGED`.

## Session (eOn / ASE `step`)

```c
#include "rgmin.h"

rgmin_control_t ctrl = rgmin_control_default();
ctrl.maxiter = 200;
ctrl.gtol = 1e-8;
ctrl.memory = 8;
rgmin_solver_t *s = rgmin_solver_create(RGMIN_LBFGS, &ctrl, n);
rgmin_report_t report;
while (!done) {
    rgmin_solver_set_maxmove(s, max_move);
    rgmin_solver_set_qn_step(s, RGMIN_QN_NEWTON); /* or RGMIN_QN_LBFGS + P as H0 */
    rgmin_solver_set_accept(s, RGMIN_ACCEPT_NONE);
    rgmin_solver_step_hess_fg(s, evalgrad, hess, user, x, &report);
}
rgmin_solver_free(s);
```

`rgmin_precon_init` and `rgmin_solver_set_precon` install Exp, Lindh,
the bonded metric, or the automatic choice. NaN `mu` estimates the
energy scale on the next step. L-BFGS uses the matrix as H0. FIRE and
nonlinear CG use it as a metric. `rgmin_solver_clear_precon` removes
it. Morse bonds and FF torsions are Rust-only.

`rgmin_solver_forget` drops pairs / conjugacy / moments. Newton and RFO
use `rgmin_solver_step_hess_fg` (fused energy and gradient, one host
potential call). Split `eval` / `grad` callbacks remain. `accept`
is `none` (take the clipped step), `energy`, `nonmonotone`, or `step`
(the clipped step with no line search, for a force that is not the
gradient of the energy). `rgmin_solver_create` opens with `energy`.
Callbacks are arguments of each step, not stored on the handle.

`rgmin_solver_set_exp` installs the exponential preconditioner.
`mu` NaN estimates the energy scale on the next step.
`rgmin_solver_exp_mu` returns that scale, or NaN when none is
installed. L-BFGS uses the factor as `H0`. FIRE and nonlinear CG
use it as the metric. `rgmin_solver_clear_exp` drops it.
`abi_minor` 28.

A HiGHS feasible set is `rgmin_solver_set_highs` plus
`rgmin_solver_set_box` (NULL side unbounded), optional
`rgmin_solver_set_trust`, and `rgmin_solver_add_equality`. Each
returns 0, or 1 when the build has no `highs` feature. Stamp
1.22.4.

A Cartesian session starts with a per-atom cap of 0.2.
`rgmin_solver_set_atom_maxmove` replaces it. A non-positive argument
clears it. A positive `maxmove` on `rgmin_control_t`, with no call to
that setter, is the Euclidean step limit and leaves the per-atom
default off. A negative `maxmove` leaves every step cap off, including
that default. Zero keeps the defaults. The cap is the largest per-atom
displacement. The C++ `OptimizeControl.maxmove` is 0, so `optimize`
keeps the per-atom default. ASE `Optimizer.defaults` `maxstep` is 0.2
at tag 3.29.0
(https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.29.0/ase/optimize/optimize.py).
eOn `max_move` is 0.2 Å
(https://henkelmanlab.org/eon/optimizer.html); the schema field
`OptimizerOptions.maxMove` is 0.2 at `4be157d4`
(https://github.com/TheochemUI/eOn/blob/4be157d43265af6b1140aaac0e52e42add62693f/schema/eon_params.capnp).

## One-shot

```c
#include "rgmin.h"

rgmin_control_t ctrl = rgmin_control_default();
ctrl.maxiter = 200;
ctrl.gtol = 1e-8;
ctrl.memory = 8;
rgmin_report_t report;
rgmin_status_t st = rgmin_minimize(eval, grad, user, x, &ctrl, RGMIN_LBFGS, &report);
```

A run that spends its budget, fails its line search, reaches line-search rounding, reaches machine
precision, leaves a backward polish unmet or spends the evaluation budget still returns
`RGMIN_SUCCESS`, with the stop in `rgmin_report_t.stop`. The one-shots
whose names end in `_opts` add `error_on_unmet` and `backward_polish`
before `out`. A
nonzero `error_on_unmet` writes `x` and `out` for those six stops and
then returns `RGMIN_UNMET_STOP`, so the host reads the report and still
sees the run as unmet. `rgmin_minimize_eindir_opts` is the same for an
`eindir_objective_t`:

```c
rgmin_status_t st = rgmin_minimize_eindir_opts(
    objective, &stamp, x, &ctrl, RGMIN_LBFGS, /* error_on_unmet */ 1,
    /* backward_polish */ 0, &report);
if (st == RGMIN_UNMET_STOP) {
    /* x holds the last iterate and report.stop names the unmet stop */
}
```

`rgmin_minimize_eindir` is that call with both flags off. An eindir
objective has no Hessian, so `backward_polish` does not change this
entry. Its errors name the symbol the host called, in
`rgmin_last_error`, from `abi_minor` 64. Check
`rgmin_abi_stamp().abi_minor >= 64` before you rely on that.

SCG takes the same one-shot shape.
Conjugacy is a field on `rgmin_scg_params_t`, not a different entry point.
Stamp is 1.69.7 (`xts_abi_compatible` still checks major and layout only).
`rgmin_lowest_eigenpair` takes a typed `rgmin_eigen_params_t` (closed `rgmin_eigen_kind_t`, no string).
Unlinked kinds return `RGMIN_UNAVAILABLE`.
`rgmin_lowest_eigenpairs` is the block LOBPCG solver for the k lowest pairs (Knyazev 2001).
`seed` and `modes_out` are row-major n-by-k.
`rgmin_lowest_eigenpairs` is `abi_minor` 39.
`rgmin_manifold_handle_t` is a Stiefel, SPD, rigid quotient or product manifold with column-major point buffers, `abi_minor` 41; see the manifold reference.
`rgmin_manifold_rigid_quotient` is `abi_minor` 56.
`rgmin_lowest_eigenpairs_ex` adds each residual and a converged flag, and an optional preconditioner (null is the identity).
It is `abi_minor` 42.
`rgmin_eigenpair_t` is unchanged.

```c
rgmin_scg_params_t params = rgmin_scg_params_default();
params.conjugacy = RGMIN_CONJUGACY_LIU_STOREY; /* gpr_optim RgminScg.inl */
rgmin_minimize_scg(eval, grad, curv, user, x, &ctrl, &params, &report);
/* params == NULL is rgmin_scg_params_default(): Netlab Polak-Ribiere +
   ScgParams::default + Restart::Never */
```

A non-CPU tensor returns `RGMIN_UNSUPPORTED_DEVICE`. The ABI does not
change when a CUDA path lands.

## L-BFGS direction with a caller `H0`

A host that keeps its own step and wants only the two-loop direction
holds an `rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_t`. The handle stores `(s, y)` pairs, oldest
first, and never evaluates an objective.

```c
rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_t *pairs = rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_create(n, 10);
int32_t stored = 0;
rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_push(pairs, s, y, n, &stored);          /* rho = 1 / (s . y) */
rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_push_rho(pairs, s, y, rho, n, &stored); /* the caller's rho */
rgmin_lbfgs_direction(pairs, grad, h0_diag, NULL, NULL, dir, n); /* dir = -H g */
rgmin_lbfgs_direction(pairs, grad, NULL, apply_h0, user, dir, n);
rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_free(pairs);
```

Pass the diagonal of `H0` or a callback, not both and not neither. A
diagonal whose entries are all `gamma` is `H0 = gamma I`. An empty
memory writes `-H0 g`. `apply_h0(user, v, out, n)` writes `H0 v` and
returns 0; any other value fails the call with
`RGMIN_INVALID_PARAMETER`. It runs once per direction, on the residual
of the backward loop that starts from `grad`, so the direction is
`-H g` when the map is linear. It must not call back into the handle.

`rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_push` declines a pair whose `s . y` is not finite or
is at most `1e-8 ||s|| ||y||`, the test `Lbfgs::record` applies. It
returns `RGMIN_SUCCESS` with `*stored` 0. `rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_push_rho`
applies the same test and also declines a `rho` that is not finite and
positive, so a pair with non-positive curvature never enters the
two-loop. A length other than the handle's `n` is
`RGMIN_INVALID_PARAMETER`, and `rgmin_last_error` names it.
`capacity` 0 keeps ten pairs; a full memory drops the oldest.

The direction is the Rust `LbfgsPairs::direction` and runs the
recursion of the session step. The pairs a capped L-BFGS session holds,
with a scalar `H0` equal to the session's, give that session's eOn step
bit for bit. `rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_push` and `rgmin_lbfgs_direction` are
`abi_minor` 38; `rgmin_lbfgs_pairs_push_rho` is `abi_minor` 43, so check
`rgmin_abi_stamp().abi_minor >= 43` before calling it. C++ wraps the
handle in `rgmin::LbfgsPairs` (`push`, `push_rho`, `direction_diagonal`,
`direction_apply`), `xts.h` aliases each entry as `xts_lbfgs_*`, and
Python takes `rgmin.LbfgsPairs.push(s, y, rho=None)`.

## Stopping rules

`rgmin_solver_set_etol(s, etol)` stops a session when the relative energy
change between accepted steps falls below `etol`, the LAMMPS
`minimize etol` test. `rgmin_solver_set_max_evals(s, n)` stops it after `n`
objective evaluations, line-search trials included, the LAMMPS `maxeval`
test. Both are off until set, and `rgmin_solver_clear_etol` and
`rgmin_solver_clear_max_evals` turn them off again. `rgmin_solver_evals(s)`
is the count the budget compares. The finished step reports
`RGMIN_STOP_ENERGY_TOLERANCE` or `RGMIN_STOP_EVAL_BUDGET` in
`rgmin_report_t.stop`. A negative or non-finite `etol`, a zero budget, a
null session and an `etol` on a particle swarm session return
`RGMIN_INVALID_PARAMETER`, leave the session as it was, and put the
reason in `rgmin_last_error`. These are `abi_minor` 50, so check
`rgmin_abi_stamp().abi_minor >= 50` first. `rgmin_control_t` keeps its
layout and the one-shot `rgmin_minimize` calls carry no stops.
@@rst::doc:`stopping`@@ has the formula and the SciPy and LAMMPS mapping.

## Cautious Riemannian L-BFGS

`rgmin_minimize_rlbfgs` runs Algorithm 2 of Huang, Absil, and Gallivan
([10.1137/17M1127582](https://doi.org/10.1137/17M1127582))
on a manifold token. Null `params` is `rgmin_rlbfgs_default`: memory 4,
cautious slope `10^{-4}`, Armijo `10^{-4}`, backtrack `1/2`, 48 trials,
and the relative gradient stop `10^{-6}`. The token uses the same
default shapes as `rgmin_solver_set_manifold`. A positive
`ctrl->maxmove` caps the ambient trial length. Zero leaves that cap
off. `xts_minimize_rlbfgs` and `xts_rlbfgs_default` are the aliases.
These are `abi_minor` 51. `rgmin_control_t` is unchanged, and the
default Euclidean L-BFGS step stays the eOn cap.

## Newton-CG under a caller preconditioner

ABI minor 66 adds `rgmin_vec_precond_fn` and `rgmin_minimize_hvp_precond`, with `rgmin_minimize_hvp_precond_sized` behind it.
Check `rgmin_abi_stamp().abi_minor >= 66` before using them.
No struct changes, so the layout revision stays 6.

`RGMIN_NEWTON_PCG` builds its own rank-16 Nystrom preconditioner at every outer step.
`rgmin_minimize_hvp_precond` runs the trust-region Newton-CG minimizer under a preconditioner that you supply: `precond` applies `P^-1` to one residual of length `n`, and a null `precond` is the identity.
The three callbacks are `evalgrad` (value and gradient in one call), `hvp` (the Hessian action, as `rgmin_minimize_hvp` takes it) and `precond`.
One `user` pointer reaches all three.
`P` takes no iterate and stays fixed for the solve, so it must be symmetric positive definite wherever the solve goes; keep any iterate-dependent state behind `user`.
CG under any such `P` reaches the same step as plain CG, in fewer Hessian actions when `P` approximates the Hessian.

```c
#include "rgmin.h"

rgmin_report_t report;
rgmin_status_t st = rgmin_minimize_hvp_precond(
    evalgrad, hvp, precond, user, x, &ctrl, 0, 0, &report);
```

`ctrl.istep` seeds the trust radius and `ctrl.maxmove` caps it.
A callback that returns a status other than `RGMIN_SUCCESS` aborts the solve.
Later callbacks do not run, `x` and `report` stay as they were, the entry returns that status, and `rgmin_last_error` names the callback.
Negative curvature is not a failure: the step follows it to the trust boundary.

The callback tensors point at solver storage and are valid for that call only.
One outer iteration allocates 10 arrays of length `n` and one inner CG iteration allocates 2, the Hessian action and the preconditioner application, because the Rust `HessianVector` and `Preconditioner` traits return owned arrays.
`xts_minimize_hvp_precond` and `xts_vec_precond_fn` are the aliases.

## Riemannian conjugate gradients

ABI minor 65 adds `RGMIN_RCG`, `rgmin_rcg_options_t`, `rgmin_rcg_options_default` and `rgmin_minimize_rcg`.
Check `rgmin_abi_stamp().abi_minor >= 65` before using them.
`rgmin_rcg_options_t` is a new struct and no existing struct changes, so the layout revision stays 6.

`RGMIN_RCG` is a `rgmin_method_t` token.
`rgmin_solver_create(RGMIN_RCG, &ctrl, n)` runs Riemannian CG as a session method, with PRP+ and the scaled transport, on the manifold that `rgmin_solver_set_manifold` selects.
`rgmin_minimize_rcg` is the one-shot run on Euclidean space, and its options record selects the other coefficients.

```c
#include "rgmin.h"

rgmin_rcg_options_t opts = rgmin_rcg_options_default();
opts.beta = 2;       /* Hager-Zhang */
opts.grad_tol = 1e-8;
rgmin_report_t report;
rgmin_status_t st = rgmin_minimize_rcg(eval, grad, user, x, &opts, &report);
```

| Field          | Meaning                                              | Default |
|----------------+------------------------------------------------------+---------|
| `beta`         | 0 Fletcher-Reeves, 1 PRP+, 2 Hager-Zhang             | 1       |
| `transport`    | 0 scaled, 1 identity                                 | 0       |
| `linesearch`   | 0 strong Wolfe, 1 Brent (`LineSearch::default`)      | 0       |
| `grad_tol`     | Riemannian gradient norm that stops the run          | `1e-5`  |
| `max_iter`     | Iteration cap                                        | 200     |
| `initial_step` | Length of the first trial displacement               | 1       |

`rgmin_rcg_options_default` returns the Rust `RcgOptions::default`, and a null `options` pointer selects the same record.
PRP+ replaces a negative Polak-Ribiere coefficient by zero.
The scaled transport shortens a transported vector that the transport made longer, back to its length before the transport.
The strong Wolfe search has `c1 = 1e-4`, `c2 = 0.1` and at most 20 trials.
`grad_tol` must be finite and not negative, and `initial_step` finite and positive.

`x` is updated in place, and `report` is written on success.
`report.converged` is nonzero when the final gradient norm is at most `grad_tol`, and `report.stop` is then `RGMIN_STOP_TOLERANCE`.
A run that ends before `max_iter` without meeting `grad_tol` reports `RGMIN_STOP_STEP_TOLERANCE`, and one that spends `max_iter` reports `RGMIN_STOP_BUDGET`.
A null `eval`, `grad`, `x` or `report`, an unknown tag, a tolerance or step that the record refuses, and a non-finite start return `RGMIN_INVALID_PARAMETER`.
So does a line-search trial whose retraction slope cannot be resolved, `Error::RcgSlope` in Rust, which refuses the slope rather than accept its curvature.
`x` is then left as it was, and `rgmin_last_error` names the reason.
A panic inside the run returns `RGMIN_INTERNAL_ERROR`, and `rgmin_last_error` names `rgmin_minimize_rcg`.

`xts.h` aliases the four names as `XTS_RCG`, `xts_rcg_options_t`, `xts_rcg_options_default` and `xts_minimize_rcg`.
The C++ wrapper names the method `rgmin::Method::Rcg`.

## Rigid quotient, trust region and projected modes

ABI minor 56 adds five entries.
Check `rgmin_abi_stamp().abi_minor >= 56` before calling them.
`rgmin_control_t` is unchanged.

`rgmin_manifold_rigid_quotient(n_atoms, periodic)` builds `R^{3N}/SE(3)` when `periodic` is 0 and `R^{3N}/T(3)` otherwise.
The packed length is `3 * n_atoms`.
Projection removes translations, and rotations as well when the quotient is `SE(3)`.
`xts_manifold_rigid_quotient` is the alias.

`rgmin_rtr_tcg_solve` is one Steihaug-Toint truncated CG step on the tangent space of any manifold handle, or in Euclidean space when the manifold pointer is null.
The gradient and the Hessian action are the Euclidean ones.
The model, the trust ball and the reported step length are in the metric of the manifold, so an SPD factor measures the step in its own metric.
It stops on negative curvature, on the trust boundary, on the residual test, on the iteration budget, or on a zero projected gradient.
A Hessian action that is not finite, or a failing callback, ends it at once with `RGMIN_INTERNAL_ERROR` and leaves the outputs alone.
`rgmin_rtr_tcg_result_t` reports the model decrease, the step length in that metric, the stop code and the iteration count.

`rgmin_rtr_radius_update` applies the Absil, Baker and Gallivan rule.
The step is accepted when the ratio of actual to predicted decrease is above 1/10. The radius shrinks by 1/4 when the ratio is below 1/4, and it doubles, never past the supplied maximum, when the ratio is above 3/4 and the step lies on the trust boundary.
A radius already above the maximum is clamped to it first.

`rgmin_lowest_eigenpair_on_manifold` and `rgmin_lowest_eigenpairs_projected` solve the tangent-projected operator.
Lanczos, Rayleigh-Ritz, Jacobi-Davidson, LOBPCG and the dimer project the seed, every operator and preconditioner action, and the returned mode; the block entry uses projected LOBPCG.
PRIMME, libkrylov and SLEPc cannot honor a projector.
With a non-null manifold they return `RGMIN_INVALID_PARAMETER` before any backend is called, whether or not it is linked, and a manifold that leaves no tangent direction returns the same status.
Neither output is written on failure.
A null manifold matches the unprojected entries.

## C++

```cpp
#include <rgmin/optimize.hpp>

rgmin::Control ctrl;
auto report = rgmin::minimize_fn(eval, grad, user, x, ctrl,
                                 rgmin::Method::Lbfgs);
```

`rgmin::Control` has its own defaults. The wrappers copy it over
`rgmin_control_default()`, so a C field it lacks keeps its default.
`<xts/optimize.hpp>` keeps the same names under `xts::optimize` for old hosts.
xtensor callers include `xts/xtensor.hpp`, which adapts `xt::xarray` to
the same `rgmin_minimize` entry. There is no solver in the header.

## Manifold

```c
rgmin_solver_set_manifold(s, RGMIN_MANIFOLD_SPHERE);
```

Tokens: `RGMIN_MANIFOLD_EUCLIDEAN` (default), `RIGID_QUOTIENT`
(`R^{3N}/SE(3)`, Sella Cartesian), `MW_RIGID` (Page–McIver /
Sella IRC Eckart), `SPHERE`, `SO3` (length 9), `STIEFEL`
(`St(n,1)`; `rgmin_solver_set_stiefel` for `p > 1`), `SE3`
(length 12), `OBLIQUE` (token 11), `MULTINOMIAL` (token 12),
`SYMMETRIC` (n² row-major), `SKEWSYMMETRIC` (token 15, n²
row-major, `n >= 2`), `EUCLIDEAN_COMPLEX` (token 16, interleaved
`(re, im)`, length `2 n`; `rgmin_solver_set_euclidean_complex`),
`CONSTANT` (token 17, singleton of length `n`;
`rgmin_solver_set_constant`), `MULTINOMIAL_DS` (token 18,
n² doubly-stochastic; `rgmin_solver_set_multinomial_ds`),
`MULTINOMIAL_SYM` (token 19, n² symmetric doubly-stochastic;
`rgmin_solver_set_multinomial_sym`), `SPHERE_COMPLEX` (token 20,
interleaved `(re, im)`, length `2 n`; `rgmin_solver_set_sphere_complex`),
`POSITIVE` (token 21, packed length `n`; `rgmin_solver_set_positive`),
`CENTERED_MATRIX` (token 22, packed `m n` row-major;
`rgmin_solver_set_centered_matrix`), `SPD` (token 7, row-major `n^2`),
`GRASSMANN` (token 8; `rgmin_solver_set_factor_shape`), `HYPERBOLIC`
(token 9), `POINCARE` (token 10) and `UNITARY` (token 23, interleaved
row-major `2 n^2`; `rgmin_solver_set_unitary`).
No token is reserved. See
@@rst::doc:`retract onto an embedded manifold <manifolds>`@@.
`rgmin_solver_set_masses` supplies N atomic masses for `MW_RIGID`.

`rgmin_solver_set_power(s, factor, block, count)` (`abi_minor` 44) selects `count` unit-weight copies of a token without shape parameters, each of packed length `block`, as manopt's `powermanifold` does.
It returns 1 and keeps the manifold for a null session, a token with shape parameters, a block the token cannot hold, or a count of zero.
`MW_RIGID` copies read `rgmin_solver_set_masses` as one molecule reused on every copy or as every copy's masses in order.
Weighted products of arbitrary factors are Rust only; @@rst::doc:`../reference/product-manifold`@@ lists them.

# Cite rgmin

This page gives a BibTeX entry for rgmin that names the version you ran.

## Get the entry

`CITATION.cff` at the top of the repository is the citation record, in the Citation File Format (CFF).
It names version 0.8.0, dated 22 November 2026.
cffconvert turns it into BibTeX.
Run it at the top of a checkout:

```bash
pip install cffconvert
cffconvert -f bibtex
```

cffconvert 2.0.0 prints:

#+begin_example
@misc{YourReferenceHere,
author = {Goswami, Rohit},
doi = {10.5281/zenodo.24437655},
month = {11},
title = {rgmin},
url = {https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgmin},
year = {2026}
}
#+end_example

The month and year come from the release date, and the entry has no version.
Its DOI is the Zenodo concept DOI, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24437655, which resolves to the latest release.
The record for 0.8.0 is https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24469714.
`codemeta.json` (CodeMeta 2.0) and `.zenodo.json` carry the same metadata for software indexes and for the Zenodo archive.
The "Cite this repository" button on GitHub reads the record on the default branch, `main`.

## Find the version you ran

In the project that depends on rgmin, run:

```bash
cargo tree -p rgmin --depth 0
```

With the release from crates.io, it prints:

#+begin_example
rgmin v0.8.0
#+end_example

With the `develop` branch, the short commit follows the `#`:

#+begin_example
rgmin v0.6.0 (https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgmin?branch=develop#113fb592)
#+end_example

The version in `Cargo.toml` on `develop` does not change with each commit, so on that route cite the commit.
`Cargo.lock` has the full commit:

```bash
grep -A2 '^name = "rgmin"' Cargo.lock
```

#+begin_example
name = "rgmin"
version = "0.6.0"
source ` "git+https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgmin?branch`develop#113fb592707406a6d621e4da6d8eea243abce968"
#+end_example

In the rgmin checkout that `Cargo.lock` names, `git rev-parse HEAD` prints the same full commit.

## Put the version in the entry

Give the entry a key, and add the version.
The `plain` style of BibTeX prints a `note` field, but it drops `version` and `url`, so put the version in `note`.
Braces around `rgmin` in the title stop a style from capitalizing the name.
For the 0.8.0 release:

```bibtex
@misc{rgmin,
author = {Goswami, Rohit},
title = {{rgmin}},
url = {https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgmin},
doi = {10.5281/zenodo.24469714},
note = {Version 0.8.0},
year = {2026}
}
```

On the `develop` route, the note names the full commit, such as `note = {Commit 113fb592707406a6d621e4da6d8eea243abce968 of the develop branch}`.

## Cite the published work too

The methods in rgmin come from published work.
The explanation pages name the book or paper that each derivation follows, and @@rst::doc:`../reference/bibliography`@@ lists the works that the docs cite.
Cite the sources of the methods you ran, along with rgmin.

# Configure a solver

Every public configuration type is `#[non_exhaustive]`. Outside this
crate it cannot be written as a struct literal. Start from
`default()` or a named constructor and chain `with_*` setters, one per
field. The fields stay public, so they can still be read.

```rust
use rgmin::{Control, EigenParams, EigensolverKind, Method, Solver, StopNorm};

let control = Control::default()
    .with_maxiter(500)
    .with_gtol(0.01)
    .with_stop_norm(StopNorm::MaxAtom)
    .with_maxmove(0.2);
assert_eq!(control.maxmove, Some(0.2));
let solver = Solver::new(Method::lbfgs_with_memory(8), control, 21);

let eigen = EigenParams::default()
    .with_kind(EigensolverKind::Lanczos)
    .with_krylov(8);
```

A setter for an `Option` field takes `impl Into<Option<T>>`:
`with_maxmove(0.2)` stores `Some(0.2)` and `with_maxmove(None)`
clears it. `Control` is `Clone` and not `Copy`, so a setter chain on a
control that is used again starts from `control.clone()`.

## Types built this way

| Type | Start from |
| `Control` | `Control::default()` |
| `NoiseFloor` | `NoiseFloor::new(eps_g)` |
| `EigenParams`, `SlepcParams`, `EigenExaParams`, `DlaFutureParams`, `ElpaParams` | `default()` |
| `ScgParams`, `ScgOptions`, `HighsOptions`, `HighsStep` | `default()` |
| `ExpParams`, `LindhParams`, `FfParams` | `default()` |
| `EonCg` | `EonCg::default()` |
| `QuickMinOptions` | `rgmin()`, `eon()`, `per_atom()` |
| `FireConfig` | `FireConfig::ase()` |
| `TrustRegion` | `TrustRegion::new(delta)` |
| `IrcTrust` | `IrcTrust::new(d1, sqrtm, dx)`, `from_atom_masses` |
| `RtrRadius` | `RtrRadius::new(radius_max)` |
| `LindhSpec` | `LindhSpec::new(z, c_stab, cell)` |
| `LineSearchOptions` | `default()`, `with_objective_roundoff` |
| `Report` | `Report::new(value, coords)`, for a host that writes its own |
| `DeflatedPair` | `DeflatedPair::new`, when supplying a pair to deflation |

Results (`LowestMode`, `Eigenpair`, `Eigenpairs`, `RestrictedStep`,
`TcgResult`, `RtrMin`, `EonCgReport`, `LineOutcome`, `NoiseEstimate`,
`ValueGradientNoise`, `Ode12rVerdict`, `ConstraintReport`,
`ElpaSpectrum`, `FireTrace`, `EonFeat`, `KantorovichBall`,
`AdjointFunctionalBar`, `MorseGap`, `TridiagEigh`,
`QuadratureEstimate`, `PcgResult`, `DeflatedPair`,
`ExtremePairsReport`, `SlqLogDetReport`, `GaussLegendre`,
`LobattoShapes`, `MagnusStep`, `Exponential`) are non-exhaustive too.
Read their fields; a destructuring pattern needs `..`.

## Methods and step rules

A variant that carries parameters is non-exhaustive. Build it with its
constructor and match it with `..`:

| Variant | Constructor |
| `Method::Lbfgs` | `Method::lbfgs()`, `Method::lbfgs_with_memory(m)` |
| `Method::Diis` | `Method::diis()`, `Method::diis_with_memory(m)` |
| `Method::Fire` | `Method::fire(kind)` |
| `Method::Newton` | `Method::newton(kind)` |
| `Method::Nlcg` | `Method::nlcg(c)`, `Method::nlcg_with_restart(c, r)` |
| `Method::Adam` | `Method::adam()`, `Method::adam_with(beta1, beta2, eps)` |
| `Method::Pso` | `Method::pso()`, `Method::pso_with(n, w, c1, c2)` |
| `LineSearch::Brent` ... `Wolfe` | `LineSearch::brent`, `backtracking`, `goldstein`, `wolfe` |
| `LbfgsStep::Capped`, `Scaled` | `LbfgsStep::capped(max_atom)`, `scaled(max_atom)` |
| `Restart::Njws`, `Powell` | `Restart::njws_at(t)`, `powell_at(t)` |
| `Conjugacy::Hybrid` | `Conjugacy::hybrid(a, b, take_max)` |

`LbfgsStep::default()` is still the eOn cap,
`LbfgsStep::capped(EON_MAX_MOVE)`.

```rust
use rgmin::Method;

let method = Method::lbfgs_with_memory(8);
let memory = match method {
    Method::Lbfgs { memory, .. } => memory,
    _ => 10,
};
assert_eq!(memory, 8);
```

## New knobs are additive

A field added to one of these types gets a default that keeps the
earlier behaviour, and a setter. A parameter added to a method variant
gets a default, and the constructors above keep their signatures. A
caller that builds through `default()`, constructors and setters, and
matches with `..`, compiles against the next minor release unchanged.

## Errors

Every fallible entry point returns `rgmin::Result<T>`, whose error is
`rgmin::Error`: the eigenpair calls (`lowest_eigenpair`, `lowest_mode`
and its backend arms, `lowest_eigenpairs`), the minimizers, FIRE 2.0
(`fire2_displacement` stalls with `Error::FireStalled`), the manifold
factories (`StiefelNp::new`, `Grassmann::new`, `Unitary::new` refuse a
shape with `Error::ManifoldShape`) and `Vector::try_on`
(`Error::UnsupportedDevice`). `Error` is non-exhaustive, so a `match`
on it needs a wildcard arm.

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/constraints.org`

# Keep bond lengths fixed while a session minimizes

A `DistanceConstraints` set fixes `|x_i - x_j| = d` for a list of atom pairs in packed `3 N` coordinates.
Install it on a `Solver` and every later step keeps each constraint to its tolerance.
Every method of the session runs on the set, under every `Accept` rule, except particle swarm.
The set can carry one mass per atom, and then every correction and projection uses the metric `M^{-1}`.
@@rst::doc:`../reference/constraints`@@ gives the equations, the derived tolerances and budgets, and how the solvers compare with GROMACS.

## Rust

The sample keeps a three-site water rigid, with real masses, while a harmonic pull moves it.

```rust
use ndarray::{ArrayView1, array};
use rgmin::{Accept, Control, DistanceConstraints, Method, Oracle, Solver};

// Oxygen, hydrogen, hydrogen.
let mut x = array![0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.9572, 0.0, 0.0, -0.24, 0.9266, 0.0];
let set = DistanceConstraints::at(vec![(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2)], x.view())?
    .with_masses(vec![15.999, 1.008, 1.008])?;
let target = array![0.1, 0.2, 0.0, 1.2, 0.1, 0.0, 0.0, 1.1, 0.3];
let obj = Oracle::unbounded(9, move |p: ArrayView1<f64>| {
    let d = &p - &target;
    (0.5 * d.dot(&d), d)
});
let control = Control::default().with_maxiter(200).with_gtol(1e-8);
let mut solver = Solver::new(Method::lbfgs(), control, 9);
solver.set_accept(Accept::Energy);
solver.set_distance_constraints(set)?;
for _ in 0..200 {
    let report = solver.step(&obj, &mut x)?;
    if report.grad_norm < 1e-8 {
        break;
    }
}
let set = solver.distance_constraints().unwrap();
assert!(set.excess(x.view()) <= 1.0);
```

`DistanceConstraints::new` takes the lengths instead of reading them from `x`.
Both constructors check their input.
They refuse a pair of one atom and a pair given twice.
They also refuse a length that is not positive and finite, and a rigid triangle that breaks the triangle inequality.
`excess` is the largest ratio of a constraint's relative residual `|d^2 - r^2| / (2 d^2)` to its tolerance, so at most one means every constraint is met.
`grad_norm` is the norm of the projected gradient, the force that the set leaves free.

A start off the set is put on it first, by corrections from the start itself.
A step that cannot meet the set returns `Error::Constraint`.
It leaves `x` and the method memory unchanged.

## C

```c
#include "rgmin.h"

const uint32_t pi[3] = {0, 0, 1};
const uint32_t pj[3] = {1, 2, 2};
const double masses[3] = {15.999, 1.008, 1.008};
rgmin_constraints_t *set = rgmin_constraints_create_at(pi, pj, 3, x, 9);
if (set =` NULL || rgmin_constraints_set_masses(set, masses, 3) !` RGMIN_SUCCESS) {
    /* rgmin_last_error() says why, rgmin_last_constraint_error() names it */
}
rgmin_control_t ctrl = rgmin_control_default();
rgmin_solver_t *s = rgmin_solver_create(RGMIN_LBFGS, &ctrl, 9);
rgmin_solver_set_accept(s, RGMIN_ACCEPT_ENERGY);
if (rgmin_solver_set_distance_constraints(s, set) != RGMIN_SUCCESS) {
    /* RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_ERROR: the session cannot carry the set */
}
rgmin_constraints_free(set);
rgmin_status_t st = rgmin_solver_step(s, eval, grad, user, xt, &report);
if (st == RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_ERROR) {
    /* x is unchanged; rgmin_last_constraint_error() says what failed */
}
```

The session copies the set, so the caller can free it right after `rgmin_solver_set_distance_constraints`.
`rgmin_solver_clear_distance_constraints` drops it.
These functions need ABI minor 31.
`xts.h` spells each one with the `xts_` prefix, and each enumerator with `XTS_`.

## C++

```cpp
#include "rgmin/optimize.hpp"

std::uint32_t const pi[3] = {0, 0, 1};
std::uint32_t const pj[3] = {1, 2, 2};
double const masses[3] = {15.999, 1.008, 1.008};
auto set = rgmin::DistanceConstraints::at(pi, pj, 3, x.data(), 9);
set.with_masses(masses, 3).with_solver(rgmin::ConstraintSolver::Auto);
rgmin::Solver solver(rgmin::Method::Lbfgs, ctrl, 9);
solver.set_accept(RGMIN_ACCEPT_ENERGY);
solver.set_distance_constraints(set);
try {
    solver.step(eval, grad, user, xt);
} catch (rgmin::ConstraintError const& e) {
    // e.kind() is the rgmin_constraint_error_t; x is unchanged
}
```

`rgmin::ConstraintError` derives from `std::runtime_error`, so code that catches that keeps working.
`xts::optimize` names the same three types.

## Choose a solver

Each block of coupled constraints is solved on its own, and a block is a connected part of the constraint graph.
A block of three atoms and three constraints is a rigid triangle, and SETTLE solves it in closed form for any masses and any triangle.
`with_settle(false)` leaves triangles to the iterative solver.
The other blocks go to the solver that `with_solver` names, the Gauss-Seidel bond solver (SHAKE) or the linear constraint solver (LINCS).

| `ConstraintSolver` | Use |
|---+---|
| `Auto` (default) | LINCS where its expansion contracts at least as fast per pass as the Gauss-Seidel bound of SHAKE, SHAKE elsewhere |
| `Shake` | Gauss-Seidel SHAKE on every block, for any coupling the projection can still solve |
| `Lincs` | LINCS on every block; a block where the expansion diverges is `ConstraintError::LincsUnsafe` |

`with_lincs_order(Some(n))` fixes the expansion order as GROMACS `lincs-order` does.
`None`, the default, derives it per block from the coupling and the tolerance.
`with_tolerance(t)` asks for the relative residual `t`, the GROMACS `shake-tol` measure.
Zero, the default, is the rounding floor of each constraint, and a smaller `t` is raised to that floor.

## Choose masses

GROMACS energy minimization sets every mass to one.
rgmin uses unit masses until `with_masses` is called.
Masses change the path to the minimum, and the constrained minimum depends on the energy and the set alone.
With real masses a correction moves a light atom more than a heavy one, as in molecular dynamics.

## What a set refuses

A set refuses each setting below with `ConstraintError::Unsupported`.
The refusal comes from `set_distance_constraints`, or from the next step when the setting changes later.

- Manifolds other than Euclidean coordinates: the set defines its own manifold.
- The exponential preconditioner: its metric would replace the mass metric of the projector.
- The HiGHS feasible-set step: it solves a quadratic program over linear equalities and has no place for the distance constraints.
- A periodic cell: the session carries no lattice vectors and so cannot form a minimum image.
- Particle swarm: it samples the whole box.
- Rigid-mode projection while a coordinate sits on its bound.

Coordinate bounds act only on atoms outside every pair.
A constrained coordinate is never clipped, and a trial that takes a constrained atom to its bound is `ConstraintError::Bound`.

## Failures

| Rust `ConstraintError` | C `rgmin_constraint_error_t` | Cause |
|---+---+---|
| `Malformed` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_MALFORMED` | Pairs, lengths or options that describe no set |
| `OutOfRange` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_OUT_OF_RANGE` | A pair names an atom past the end of `x` |
| `Mass` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_MASS` | A mass that is not positive and finite |
| `Unsupported` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_UNSUPPORTED` | A session setting from the list above |
| `NotConverged` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_NOT_CONVERGED` | SHAKE, LINCS or the tangent solve spent its derived budget |
| `Reversed` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_REVERSED` | A bond turned too far from its direction at the anchor |
| `Dependent` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_DEPENDENT` | The constraints of a block are linearly dependent at the anchor |
| `LincsUnsafe` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_LINCS_UNSAFE` | `Lincs` was asked for where its expansion diverges |
| `SettleDegenerate` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_SETTLE_DEGENERATE` | A trial moved a rigid triangle beyond any SETTLE solution |
| `Bound` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_BOUND` | A constrained atom reached its coordinate bound |
| `NonFinite` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_NON_FINITE` | A coordinate, mass or residual is not finite |

Under `Accept::Energy` and `Accept::Nonmonotone` a trial that the set cannot take counts as refused, and the search tries a shorter one.
The error reaches the caller only when no trial could be placed.
The dogleg and Newton-CG trust regions count such a trial as a rejected model step and shrink the radius.
Under `Accept::None` there is no shorter step to try, so the error reaches the caller.
A smaller `istep`, `maxmove` or per-atom cap keeps trials close enough to the set.

# Embed in anneal

Hopping chains in [anneal](https://github.com/HaoZeke/anneal) relax thousands of times from perturbations of
an already-relaxed structure. They do not own a second L-BFGS: they hold
an `rgmin::Lbfgs` through `anneal_core::methods::warm_lbfgs::WarmLbfgs`.

## Checkout layout

#+begin_example
Rust/
  eindir/
  rgmin/
  anneal/
  landfold/
#+end_example

`anneal` and `landfold` path-depend on the two siblings so there is one
`eindir-core` and one `rgmin` in the graph.

## Call site

The public hopping API is unchanged:

```rust
use anneal_core::methods::warm_lbfgs::WarmLbfgs;
use ndarray::Array1;

let mut opt = WarmLbfgs::default();
let x0 = Array1::from(vec![1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]);
let (f, x, evals) = opt.minimize(x0.view(), 200, |v| Some(fg(v)));
```

`WarmLbfgs::forget` drops the pair history when the chain jumps to a
structurally different basin. `minimize_watched` still sits at the top of
each accepted iterate so a screening predictor can stop the relaxation.

## Why this crate, not a copy

A second two-loop in anneal drifted from the Nocedal-Wright 7.20 scale
once already. The production method and the pair history belong in
one place.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/fire.org`

# Run fire2 with the published parameters or bias correction

A `fire2` session runs the Fast Inertial Relaxation Engine (FIRE)
2.0 on the crate's own parameters.
Two opt-in settings change that.
`set_fire_preset` selects the parameters of
Guenole et al. @@rst::cite:`guenoleAssessmentOptimizationFast2020`@@ Table 1.
`set_fire_abc` turns on the accelerated bias-corrected (ABC) FIRE
update @@rst::cite:`echeverrirestrepoABCFIREAcceleratedBiascorrected2023`@@.
Both return an error on any method other than `fire2`.
The values and the update are listed under FIRE on the reference
page @@rst::doc:`../reference/sota`@@.

## Rust

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1, array};
use rgmin::{Control, FireKind, FirePreset, Method, Oracle, Solver};

let control = Control::default()
    .with_maxiter(5000)
    .with_gtol(1e-5)
    .with_istep(1e-3)
    .with_maxmove(0.2);
let mut solver = Solver::new(Method::fire(FireKind::V2), control, 2);
solver.set_fire_preset(FirePreset::Guenole2020).unwrap();
solver.set_fire_abc(true).unwrap();
let obj = Oracle::unbounded(2, |x: ArrayView1<f64>| {
    (x.dot(&x), Array1::from_iter(x.iter().map(|v| 2.0 * v)))
});
let mut x = array![0.5, -0.25];
let report = solver.step(&obj, &mut x).unwrap();
```

## C

```c
#include "rgmin.h"

rgmin_control_t ctrl = rgmin_control_default(); /* gtol 1e-5 */
ctrl.maxiter = 5000;
ctrl.istep = 1e-3;
ctrl.maxmove = 0.2;
rgmin_solver_t *s = rgmin_solver_create(RGMIN_FIRE2, &ctrl, n);
if (rgmin_solver_set_fire_preset(s, RGMIN_FIRE_PRESET_GUENOLE2020) != 0
    || rgmin_solver_set_fire_abc(s, 1) != 0) {
    /* rgmin_last_error() says why */
}
```

Both setters need ABI minor 30.
`xts.h` spells them `xts_solver_set_fire_preset` and
`xts_solver_set_fire_abc`.
The C++ wrapper has `set_fire_preset` and `set_fire_abc`.

## What each setting does

`set_fire_preset` restarts the integrator: the time step goes back
to `istep`, the velocity to zero and the counters to zero.
Call it before the first step.
The preset scales its time-step bounds by `istep`, so
`dt_max = 10 istep` and `dt_min = 0.02 istep`.
A shrink that would take the time step below `dt_min` leaves it
where it is, as in Algorithm 2 of the paper.
The default parameters clamp it to `dt_min` instead.

`set_fire_abc` keeps its value across `set_fire_preset`.
With ABC on, each displacement component is bounded by the
per-atom cap, or by `maxmove` without one, and the velocity is
clipped to the same bound divided by the time step.
That follows ASE `FIRE2(use_abc=True)`.
Without ABC, the cap scales the whole step, as before.
With neither cap set, ABC has no clip.

The default session is unchanged by either setter until it is
called.

A `fire2` session can take its velocity from the secant of the step.
On a curved kind that secant is projected onto the tangent space.
The projection is at the new point.
Flat kinds keep the plain secant.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/gpmin.org`

# Run Gaussian-process-accelerated optimization (GPMin)

`GPMin` implements the local Gaussian-process-accelerated geometry
optimizer of Garijo del Río, Mortensen, and Jacobsen
@@rst::cite:`garijodelrioLocalBayesianOptimizer2019`@@.
At every step, `rgmin` fits a Gaussian process (GP) surrogate over all
observed energies and gradients with a squared-exponential covariance
kernel and analytic derivative blocks, minimizes the GP posterior mean
from the current point with an inner L-BFGS search, and evaluates the
true objective at the proposed point.
If the true energy does not decrease, the trial observation is appended
to the GP and the surrogate is minimized again from the current point
until a descent step is found, the gradient tolerance is met, or the
refinement budget is reached.

Because each training step factors a dense `(n * (D + 1))` covariance
matrix with Cholesky decomposition, `GPMin` targets expensive objectives
(such as ab initio calculators) on modest dimensions (roughly up to 100
atoms).

## Python drop-in for ASE

The maturin package provides `rgmin.optimize.GPMin` (also re-exported as
`rgmin.GPMin`), matching the constructor signature, defaults, and
`run(fmax, steps)` contract of `ase.optimize.GPMin`:

```python
from rgmin.optimize import GPMin

opt = GPMin(
    atoms,
    logfile="gpmin.log",
    trajectory="gpmin.traj",
    update_prior_strategy="maximum",
    update_hyperparams=False,
)
converged ` opt.run(fmax`0.01, steps=100)
```

To enable bounded marginal log-likelihood hyperparameter updates on a
batch schedule:

```python
opt = GPMin(
    atoms,
    update_hyperparams=True,
    batch_size=1,
    bounds=0.1,
)
converged ` opt.run(fmax`0.01)
weight, scale, noise = opt.hyperparameters
```

`maxstep` defaults to `0.2` Å, matching the per-atom displacement cap of
the other `rgmin.optimize` drop-ins. Pass `maxstep=0.0` to disable the
cap and match ASE's uncapped surrogate steps.

For non-ASE objectives, construct `rgmin.Session("gpmin", n, ...)`
directly and drive `session.step(x, callback)`.

## Rust API

The Rust implementation lives in `rgmin::gpmin` and works on any
`D`-dimensional smooth objective, with no assumption that `D` is a
multiple of 3.
Use either the standalone `GpMin` stepper or a `Solver` session with
`Method::GpMin`:

```rust
use ndarray::array;
use rgmin::{Control, GpMin, GpMinConfig, Method, Oracle, PriorStrategy, Solver};

let obj = Oracle::unbounded(2, |x| {
    (x[0] * x[0] + 3.0 * x[1] * x[1], array![2.0 * x[0], 6.0 * x[1]])
});

let cfg = GpMinConfig::default()
    .with_scale(0.4)
    .with_weight(1.0)
    .with_noise(0.001)
    .with_prior(PriorStrategy::Maximum)
    .with_max_step(Some(0.2));

let mut x = array![0.3, -0.2];
let mut gpmin = GpMin::new(cfg.clone(), 2)?;
let report = gpmin.run(&obj, &mut x, &Control::default().with_gtol(1e-4))?;

// Or through Solver:
let mut x2 = array![0.3, -0.2];
let mut solver = Solver::new(Method::GpMin, Control::default().with_gtol(1e-4), 2);
solver.set_gpmin_config(cfg)?;
let report2 = solver.run(&obj, &mut x2)?;
```

## Configuration and defaults

Every hyperparameter is configured through `GpMinConfig` (Rust) or
`GPMin(...)` / `Session("gpmin", ...)` (Python), with defaults matching
ASE's `ase.optimize.GPMin`:

| Parameter               | `update_hyperparams=False` | `update_hyperparams=True` | Meaning |
|-------------------------+----------------------------+---------------------------+---------|
| `scale`                 | `0.4`                      | `0.3`                     | Squared-exponential kernel length scale. |
| `weight`                | `1.0`                      | `2.0`                     | Kernel prefactor (energy scale). |
| `noise`                 | `0.001`                    | `0.004`                   | Observation noise regularization (energy variance `(noise * scale)^2`, gradient variance `noise^2`). |
| `update_prior_strategy` | `"maximum"`                | `"maximum"`               | Constant energy prior rule: `"maximum"`, `"init"`, `"average"`, or a fixed constant `prior`. |
| `batch_size`            | unused (`1`)               | `1`                       | Number of new observations between marginal-likelihood updates. |
| `bounds`                | unused (`0.1`)             | `0.1`                     | Relative box half-width `[(1 - b) t0, (1 + b) t0]` for `(weight, scale)`; `False` / `None` disables bounds. |
| `max_refinements`       | `30`                       | `30`                      | Maximum surrogate refinements per step before failing closed. |

## Fail-closed error handling

`GPMin` never adds silent jitter or falls back to another step when the
surrogate fails:

- Non-positive-definite covariance matrices after applying the configured
  `noise` regularization return `Error::GpMin` in Rust (`ValueError` in
  Python) naming the Cholesky failure.
- Non-finite energies or gradients from the objective return
  `Error::Oracle` (`ValueError` in Python).
- Exhausting `max_refinements` without finding a descent step returns
  `Error::GpMin` (`ValueError` in Python).

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/gromacs-cg.org`

# Run GROMACS-style conjugate-gradient minimization

Use `gromacs-cg` when a workflow uses GROMACS MDP parameters (`emtol`,
`emstep`, `nsteps`, `nstcgsteep`) and wants the GROMACS `do_cg`
Polak-Ribière direction update (periodic steepest-descent restart every
`nstcgsteep` steps, $|\beta| \le 5$ cap, steepest-descent fallback, and
largest per-atom force norm `MaxAtom`) paired with `rgmin`'s strong-Wolfe
line search. It does not implement GROMACS's own secant/bisection line
search or LINCS-constrained CG, so intermediate iterates differ from
`gmx mdrun`; see @@rst::doc:`../reference/gromacs-cg`@@ for the exact
differences and tested comparison.

## Python and MDP keys

`gromacs_mdp_options` accepts `integrator = "cg"`, `emtol`, `emstep`,
`nsteps`, `nstcgsteep`, and `constraints = "none"` in GROMACS units and
converts the force tolerance and initial step to the eV/Å units used by
ASE calculators.

```python
import numpy as np
import rgmin

options = rgmin.gromacs_mdp_options(
    {
        "integrator": "cg",
        "emtol": 10.0,
        "emstep": 0.01,
        "nsteps": 500,
        "nstcgsteep": 1000,
    }
)
method = options.pop("method")
report, x = rgmin.minimize(value_and_gradient, np.asarray(x0), method, **options)
```

The defaults for `integrator = "cg"` are `emtol = 10.0` kJ mol^-1 nm^-1,
`emstep = 0.01` nm, `nsteps = -1` (no iteration limit),
`nstcgsteep = 1000`, and `constraints = "none"`. `nstcgsteep = 0` turns the
periodic steepest-descent restart off, as in GROMACS. Any non-`"none"`
value of `constraints` raises `ValueError`: `gromacs-cg` has no constrained
line search, so use `gromacs-steep` for constrained systems.

For an ASE `Atoms` or cell filter, use `GromacsCg` in `rgmin.optimize`:

```python
from rgmin.optimize import GromacsCg

opt ` GromacsCg(atoms, emtol`10.0, emstep`0.01, nsteps`500, nstcgsteep=1000)
opt.run()
```

An explicit `fmax` or `steps` passed to `run` overrides the mapped `emtol`
or `nsteps` for that call. Holonomic bond/angle constraints on `atoms` are
refused with a `ValueError`.

## Rust, C, and C++

The core is unit-agnostic. Put the force tolerance and initial step scale in
the units of the objective:

```rust
let control = rgmin::Control::default()
    .with_gtol(force_tolerance)
    .with_istep(initial_step_scale)
    .with_maxiter(number_of_steps);
let mut solver = rgmin::Solver::new(rgmin::Method::GromacsCg, control, x.len());
solver.set_gromacs_cg_config(
    rgmin::GromacsCgConfig::default().with_nstcgsteep(1000),
)?;
let report = solver.run(&objective, &mut x)?;
```

The C selector is `RGMIN_GROMACS_CG` and the C++ selector is
`rgmin::Method::GromacsCg`. Configure `nstcgsteep` with
`rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_cg` in C or `Solver::set_gromacs_cg` in C++.
Distance constraints (`Solver::set_distance_constraints` /
`rgmin_solver_set_distance_constraints`) are refused on `GromacsCg` with a
constraint error.

The algorithm, line search, and `gmx mdrun` comparison are in
@@rst::doc:`../reference/gromacs-cg`@@.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/gromacs-lbfgs.org`

# Run GROMACS L-BFGS minimization

Use `gromacs-lbfgs` to carry a GROMACS `integrator = l-bfgs`
energy-minimization block into rgmin. The defaults are `emtol = 10.0`
kJ mol^-1 nm^-1, `emstep = 0.01` nm, `nsteps = -1`, `nbfgscorr = 10`,
and `constraints = none`.

## Python and MDP keys

```python
from rgmin.optimize import GromacsLbfgs

opt = GromacsLbfgs(
    atoms,
    emtol=10.0,
    emstep=0.01,
    nsteps=500,
    nbfgscorr=10,
)
opt.run()
```

For the functional API, map the MDP keys first:

```python
options = rgmin.gromacs_mdp_options(
    {
        "integrator": "l-bfgs",
        "emtol": 10.0,
        "emstep": 0.01,
        "nsteps": 500,
        "nbfgscorr": 10,
        "constraints": "none",
    }
)
method = options.pop("method")
report, x = rgmin.minimize(value_and_gradient, x0, method, **options)
```

Unknown keys raise `ValueError` and name the key. A non-`none`
`constraints` value is refused, as it is by GROMACS L-BFGS.

## Rust, C, and C++

The Rust core is unit-agnostic:

```rust
let control = rgmin::Control::default()
    .with_gtol(force_tolerance)
    .with_istep(emstep)
    .with_maxiter(nsteps);
let mut solver =
    rgmin::Solver::new(rgmin::Method::GromacsLbfgs, control, x.len());
solver.set_gromacs_lbfgs_config(
    rgmin::GromacsLbfgsConfig::default().with_nbfgscorr(10),
)?;
let report = solver.run(&objective, &mut x)?;
```

The C selector is `RGMIN_GROMACS_LBFGS` and
`rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_lbfgs` sets the correction count. C++ uses
`rgmin::Method::GromacsLbfgs`, `Solver::set_gromacs_lbfgs`, and
`SolverConfig::with_gromacs_lbfgs`. The `nbfgscorr` runtime setting
selects the same count.

The exact line search, restart, stopping rules, and documented
differences from GROMACS 2023.3 are in
@@rst::doc:`../reference/gromacs-lbfgs`@@.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/gromacs-steep.org`

# Run GROMACS steepest descent

Use the `gromacs-steep` method when a setup should keep the update rule of
GROMACS `integrator = steep`, rather than rgmin's line-searched `steepest`
method.

## Python and MDP keys

`gromacs_mdp_options` accepts the three minimization keys in GROMACS units
and converts them to the eV/Å units used by ASE calculators.

```python
import numpy as np
import rgmin

options = rgmin.gromacs_mdp_options(
    {"integrator": "steep", "emtol": 10.0, "emstep": 0.01, "nsteps": 500}
)
method = options.pop("method")
report, x = rgmin.minimize(value_and_gradient, np.asarray(x0), method, **options)
```

The defaults are `emtol = 10.0` kJ mol^-1 nm^-1, `emstep = 0.01` nm,
and `nsteps = -1`. The last maps to no iteration limit. A non-negative
`nsteps` maps to the native iteration budget.

For an ASE `Atoms` or filter, use the class in `rgmin.optimize`:

```python
from rgmin.optimize import GromacsSteep

opt ` GromacsSteep(atoms, emtol`10.0, emstep`0.01, nsteps`500)
opt.run()
```

An explicit `fmax` or `steps` passed to `run` overrides the mapped
`emtol` or `nsteps` for that run.

## Rust, C, and C++

The core is unit-agnostic. Put the force tolerance and displacement in
the units of the objective:

```rust
let control = rgmin::Control::default()
    .with_gtol(force_tolerance)
    .with_istep(initial_maximum_displacement)
    .with_maxiter(number_of_steps);
let mut solver = rgmin::Solver::new(rgmin::Method::GromacsSteep, control, x.len());
let report = solver.run(&objective, &mut x)?;
```

The C selector is `RGMIN_GROMACS_STEEP` and the C++ selector is
`rgmin::Method::GromacsSteep`. Set `rgmin_control_t.gtol` and
`rgmin_control_t.istep` in the same units as the callback.
`RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION` reports that the displacement is below
rgmin's steep displacement floor, or that it cannot change a
coordinate. GROMACS `do_steep` has no such floor.

A non-finite callback value or gradient is returned as an oracle error
(Rust `Error::Oracle`, C `RGMIN_INTERNAL_ERROR` with
`rgmin_last_error` text). A distance-constraint placement failure
returns a constraint error (Rust `Error::Constraint`, C
`RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_ERROR` with `rgmin_last_constraint_error`) when an
explicit shrink budget runs out while the displacement is still at
least the floor. Crossing the floor stops with
`RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION` instead.

The exact update and stop rules are in
@@rst::doc:`../reference/gromacs-steep`@@. For GROMACS
`integrator = cg`, see @@rst::doc:`gromacs-cg`@@ and
@@rst::doc:`../reference/gromacs-cg`@@.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/highs-qp.org`

# L-BFGS quadratic model through HiGHS

The two-loop recursion is the unconstrained L-BFGS step. HiGHS is
used only when that step must sit in a feasible set: an L_inf trust
region, a box on `x + p`, and optional linear equalities.

The QP is `min 1/2 ||p - d||^2` with `d ` -H g` and `Q ` I`. A dense
compact Hessian is not formed; that matrix is indefinite after a tiny
accepted step and `Highs_run` does not return.

Unconstrained, `highs_step` is the two-loop direction. A box or trust
region scales the whole increment (direction preserved). Packed
centering is a mean subtract. Arbitrary equalities still go to HiGHS.

When a host Hessian is present (`rgmin_solver_step_hess`) and
`rgmin_solver_set_highs` is on, HiGHS solves the convex Newton QP
`min 1/2 p^T P p + g^T p` with per-coordinate boxes from
`rgmin_solver_set_box` (a NULL side is unbounded) and, if no box
was set, from atom maxmove. `rgmin_solver_set_trust` sets the
L_inf radius on the step; `rgmin_solver_add_equality` appends
`a · p ` rhs=. That is the path eOn / rgpot / any eindir
objective share. Without the `highs` cargo feature every setter
returns 1.

Enable the feature.
Its `highs-sys` crate builds HiGHS from source with CMake and a C++ compiler.
The tests also need SciPy (@@rst::doc:`install`@@):

```bash
cargo test --features highs
```

```rust
use rgmin::{HighsStep, Lbfgs};

let mut opt = Lbfgs::default();
opt.highs = Some(
    HighsStep::default()
        .with_trust(0.5)
        .with_lo(-1.0)
        .with_hi(1.0),
);
```

`lo` and `hi` are one bound for every coordinate.
`Solver::set_box` takes one bound per coordinate.

landfold `--highs` is this step on chi, not sequential LP.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/howto/install.org`

# Install rgmin

rgmin 0.8.0 is a Rust crate with a C ABI.
It needs Rust 1.88 or newer, the `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml`.
This page covers the crate, the C library from cargo-c or Meson, the two Python packages and the LAMMPS plugin.

## From crates.io

Add rgmin, the `ndarray` it takes, and `eindir-core` for the objective traits:

```bash
cargo add rgmin@0.8 ndarray@0.17 eindir-core@0.6
```

rgmin takes `eindir-core` 0.6 from crates.io too, so Cargo builds one copy of it.

### Features

`simd` is on by default.
The others are off until you name them.

| Feature     | Adds                                                                                          | Needs                                                                       |
|-------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `simd`      | single instruction, multiple data (SIMD) versions of the vector loops, chosen for the CPU at run time | nothing more                                                                |
| `capi`      | the C symbols behind `include/rgmin.h`                                                        | nothing more                                                                |
| `par`       | rayon threads for long dot products and vector updates                                        | nothing more                                                                |
| `highs`     | the HiGHS step of @@rst::doc:`highs-qp`@@                                                     | CMake, a C++ compiler and libclang, since `highs-sys` builds HiGHS from source |
| `slepc`     | `EigensolverKind::Slepc`                                                                      | PETSc and SLEPc, and a C compiler                                           |
| `primme`    | `EigensolverKind::Primme`                                                                     | PRIMME 3.0 or newer, and a C compiler                                       |
| `chase`     | `EigensolverKind::Chase`                                                                      | the compiled ChASE C interface, and a C compiler                            |
| `libkrylov` | `EigensolverKind::Libkrylov`                                                                  | libkrylov, the gfortran runtime, a Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms (BLAS) library, and a C compiler |
| `readcon`   | `read_checkpoint` and `write_checkpoint` for CON geometry files                               | nothing more, since it pulls in `readcon-core`                              |

For example:

```bash
cargo add rgmin@0.8 --features highs
```

The `slepc`, `primme`, `chase` and `libkrylov` features each look for a library.
They try pkg-config first.
Next they try a directory variable.
That is `PETSC_DIR` and `SLEPC_DIR`, `PRIMME_DIR`, `CHASE_DIR` or `LIBKRYLOV_DIR`.
Last they try `CONDA_PREFIX` and then `/usr`.
If the library is missing, the build still passes.
That eigensolver kind then returns `Error::EigenUnavailable` at run time.
Cargo prints the build warning for a dependency only with `cargo build -vv`.

The `periodic-product` feature adds `periodic_product::periodic_product_spectrum`, which multiplies short transfer matrices and finds the multipliers of the product at a chosen binary precision.
It pulls in `rug`, which links `gmp-mpfr-sys`.
Both crates are LGPL-3.0 or later, unlike the MIT licence of rgmin, and a binary that links either one statically must meet the LGPL terms for it.
`gmp-mpfr-sys` builds GMP, MPFR and MPC from source with autotools, so it needs `m4`, `make`, `diffutils` and a C compiler.
The crate always builds a static library. When `capi` is also enabled, including under `--all-features`, the module is left out so that library does not link GMP. `--features periodic-product` is the build that includes it.

## From git

To build a commit that is not on crates.io, such as the tip of `develop`, depend on the repository:

```bash
cargo add rgmin --git https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgmin --branch develop
cargo add ndarray@0.17 eindir-core@0.6
```

`develop` also takes `eindir-core` 0.6 from crates.io, so this builds one copy of it as well.
Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z`; `--tag` in place of `--branch develop` pins one.

## Check the install

```bash
cargo build
```

@@rst::doc:`../tutorials/quickstart`@@ is a first program.

## From a checkout

A clone starts on `main`.
These pages describe `develop`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgmin.git
cd rgmin
git switch develop
cargo test --features capi
```

With `--features highs`, some tests check HiGHS steps against SciPy through `tests/highs_scipy_gold.py`.
They run `python3`, or the interpreter named in `PYTHON`, and that interpreter needs SciPy:

```bash
PYTHON=python3.12 cargo test --features highs
```

## For C and C++ with cargo-c

cargo-c builds and installs the C library, the headers and a pkg-config file from a checkout.
rgmin needs cargo-c 0.10.17 or newer, the `min_version` in `Cargo.toml`.
Each cargo-c release needs a recent Rust: 0.10.17 builds with Rust 1.89, and 0.10.26 needs Rust 1.97.
On Linux cargo-c also needs pkg-config and the OpenSSL headers, such as `libssl-dev` on Debian and Ubuntu.
This is the cargo-c that CI installs:

```bash
cargo +1.89.0 install cargo-c --locked --version 0.10.17+cargo-0.92.0
```

With Rust 1.97 or newer, `cargo install cargo-c --locked` installs the newest release instead.
Then, in the checkout:

```bash
cargo cinstall --prefix=/usr/local --features capi
```

`cargo cinstall` builds in release mode.
It installs `librgmin` as a shared and a static library, `rgmin.h`, the C++ headers `rgmin/optimize.hpp` and `rgbind/rgbind.hpp`, the `xts` headers, `dlpack/dlpack.h` and the `rgmin` pkg-config file.
On Debian and Ubuntu the library and the pkg-config file go under the multiarch directory of the prefix, such as `lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`.
Compile a C program against the install with pkg-config:

```bash
cc $(pkg-config --cflags rgmin) prog.c $(pkg-config --libs rgmin) -o prog
```

If the dynamic loader does not search that library directory, run the program with it in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

@@rst::doc:`c-abi`@@ walks through the C calls.
`tests/cinstall/smoke.sh` is the check that CI runs: it installs into `target/rgmin-cinstall` and compiles a C and a C++ program.

## For C and C++ with Meson

The repository is also a Meson project.
It needs Meson 1.3 or newer, Ninja, a C and a C++ compiler, Python 3, and Cargo with Rust 1.88 or newer.
Meson runs Cargo to build `librgmin` and declares `rgmin_dep`: the include directory, the static library, the system libraries it needs, and the define `USE_RGMIN`.

To use rgmin as a subproject, add `subprojects/rgmin.wrap` to your project:

```ini
[wrap-git]
url = https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgmin.git
revision = develop
depth = 1

[provide]
dependency_names = rgmin
```

A release tag in `revision` pins that release.
Then ask for the dependency in your `meson.build`:

```meson
rgmin_dep = dependency('rgmin')
```

The `rgmin_features` option holds the Cargo features, `capi,highs` by default.
With `highs`, the static library holds HiGHS, which is C++.
A C++ target that links `rgmin_dep` gets the C++ standard library from its linker, and a C target does not and fails to link.
`highs` also needs a libclang new enough for the HiGHS headers.
For a C program, or where libclang is missing, build only `capi`:

```bash
meson setup build -Drgmin:rgmin_features=capi
meson compile -C build
```

A build of the repository itself makes `librgmin.so` and `librgmin.a`:

```bash
meson setup build
meson compile -C build
meson install -C build
```

`meson install` installs the shared library only, with no headers or pkg-config file.
Use cargo-c for a full install.

## Python

PyPI has the nanobind package: the free-threaded module `rgmin._core` and the ASE optimizers in `rgmin.ase`.
The `ase` extra adds ASE, which `rgmin.ase` needs and `import rgmin` does not load:

```bash
python -m pip install rgmin
python -m pip install 'rgmin[ase]'
```

There are wheels for Linux with glibc 2.28 or newer (`manylinux_2_28`) on `x86_64` and `aarch64`, macOS 14 or newer on `arm64` and `x86_64`, and Windows on `x86_64`.
CPython 3.10 and 3.11 each have a wheel, one abi3 wheel serves 3.12 and newer, and the free-threaded 3.14t and 3.15t each have a wheel.
On any other platform or interpreter, pip builds the sdist, which has the requirements of a checkout below, the Corrosion download included.

The repository root builds the same package with scikit-build-core.
It needs a C++17 compiler, CMake 3.15 or newer, and Rust 1.88 or newer.
CMake downloads Corrosion from GitHub while it configures.
From the checkout:

```bash
python -m pip install '.[ase]'
```

`python/` builds the PyO3 module with maturin.
It is not on PyPI.
It adds `rgmin.optimize`, the ASE drop-in of @@rst::doc:`ase-migration`@@, and needs Rust 1.88 or newer:

```bash
python -m pip install './python[ase]'
```

Both install the import package `rgmin`, so an environment holds one of them.
@@rst::doc:`python`@@ shows both.

## LAMMPS plugin

`lammps/` builds `min_style rgmin`, a plugin for LAMMPS 22Jul2025 or newer built with CMake and the `PLUGIN` package.
@@rst::doc:`lammps-migration`@@ gives the build commands.
