# API reference

Two published surfaces, one implementation.

## Rust

`cargo doc --no-deps` in a checkout.
The crate root is `rgmin`.
The types a host works with:

| Type | Role |
|---+---|
| `Solver` | One stepper step. Hosts own the loop. |
| `Lbfgs` | Persistent limited-memory quasi-Newton; `minimize_box` keeps iterates in bounds. |
| `Method` / `Control` / `LineSearch` | Which step, and how far. |
| `ManifoldKind` | `project` / `retract` / `transport`. |
| `RiemannianManifold` | Stiefel, SPD and product handles; see the manifold page. |
| `IrcTrust` | GS2 / Sella MW-sphere equality. |
| `lowest_eigenpair` / `lowest_mode` | Matrix-free lowest Hessian pair. |
| `lowest_eigenpairs` | Block LOBPCG. Residuals and an optional `T` (Knyazev 2001). |
| `EigensolverKind` / `EigenParams` | Closed eigen waist. |
| `HessianVector` / `FdHvp` | `H v` without forming `H`. |
| `TryHessianVector` | The same callbacks, each one allowed to fail. |
| `Solver::step_hvp` | Analytic product for `newton-cg` / `newton-pcg`. |
| `Solver::try_step_hvp` | That step. The first host error is `Error::Host`. |
| `TryApplyHessian` | A block-eigen product that can fail. |
| `try_lowest_eigenpairs` | `lowest_eigenpairs` on that product, without `T`. |
| `try_lowest_eigenpairs_precond` | `lowest_eigenpairs_precond` on that product, with an optional `T`. |
| `kantorovich_ball` / `KantorovichBall` | Newton--Kantorovich existence ball from supplied majorants (Kantorovich and Akilov 1982; Gragg and Tapia 1974). |
| `adjoint_functional_bar` / `AdjointFunctionalBar` | Dual-weighted residual functional bound and remainder (Becker and Rannacher 2001). |
| `certify_morse_gap` / `MorseGap` | Self-adjoint spectral gap certified by Weyl's inequality (Weyl 1912). |

`newton-cg` and `newton-pcg` are `Method::from_name` tokens. The
session counts `gradient_calls` and `hvp_calls` separately. A
forward-difference product on `step` costs one gradient and is
charged as a product.

`kantorovich_ball`, `adjoint_functional_bar`, and `certify_morse_gap`
combine caller-supplied majorants in standard `f64` floating-point
arithmetic without outward rounding. Given a primal norm and its
induced operator norm, a Jacobian Lipschitz bound on `B(x0, 2 eta)`
suffices for the Kantorovich ball ([10.1016/B978-0-08-023036-8.50024-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-08-023036-8.50024-2),
[10.1137/0711002](https://doi.org/10.1137/0711002)) @@rst::cite:`kantorovichNewtonsMethod1982,graggOptimalErrorBounds1974`@@.
`adjoint_functional_bar` pairs `first_order = |lambda^T F(x0)|` for an
exact adjoint `J(x0)^T lambda = grad q(x0)` with `gradient_norm` in the
dual norm and `hessian_bound` in the induced operator norm from the
primal space to its dual ([10.1017/S0962492901000010](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0962492901000010))
@@rst::cite:`beckerOptimalControlApproach2001`@@. `certify_morse_gap`
requires `operator_lipschitz` to bound the spectral-norm Lipschitz
constant of the projected self-adjoint operator and subtracts that
perturbation plus `eigensolver_roundoff` from `computed_gap` by Weyl's
inequality ([10.1007/BF01456804](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01456804))
@@rst::cite:`weylAsymptotischeVerteilungsgesetzEigenwerte1912`@@.

The generated Sphinx pages under `crates/rgmin/` (when the docs
environment is built with `sphinxcontrib-rust`) are the same
rustdoc, exported.

| Type | Role |
|---+---|
| `magnus::magnus_step` / `magnus::MagnusStep` | Sixth-order Magnus map with an embedded fourth-order exponential. |
| `magnus::expm` / `magnus::Exponential` / `magnus::gauss_legendre_three` / `magnus::MagnusError` | Padé matrix exponential, Gauss-Legendre nodes and typed refusal. |

## C

`include/rgmin.h` is the C ABI. `cargo cinstall` installs that
header and `dlpack/dlpack.h`. `include/xts.h` is the compatibility
alias. The hourglass is `rgmin_solver_create` /
`rgmin_solver_step` / `rgmin_solver_free`, plus `rgmin_minimize`.
Tensors are dlpk `DLManagedTensorVersioned`. HTML for this waist
is Doxygen plus doxyYoda; see @@rst::doc:`howto/doxygen <../howto/doxygen>`@@.

`rgmin_minimize_eindir` takes an `eindir_objective_t` and an
`eindir_abi_stamp_t` that no `rgmin_` function builds. librgmin
therefore re-exports the C ABI of eindir-core as public API:
`eindir_core_abi_compatible`, `eindir_core_abi_family`,
`eindir_core_abi_stamp`, `eindir_core_version`, `eindir_last_error` and
the `eindir_objective_` functions `new`, `free`, `eval`, `grad`,
`has_grad`, `dim`, `bounds_low` and `bounds_high`. A C caller that links
only librgmin builds the objective with `eindir_objective_new` and the
stamp with `eindir_core_abi_stamp`. These names have been exported
since 0.7.0, and `scripts/check_exports.py` fails if one goes missing
or if eindir-core exports a name not on this list.

## What belongs next door

Band, min-mode, and IRC *sessions* are [rgsaddle](https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgsaddle). Potentials
are [rgpot](https://github.com/OmniPotentRPC/rgpot).

# Architecture

`rgmin` has an hourglass interface, the design in [Stefanus Du Toit's "Hourglass Interfaces for C++ APIs" (CppCon 2014)](https://github.com/CppCon/CppCon2014/tree/master/Presentations/Hourglass%20Interfaces%20for%20C%2B%2B%20APIs).
The core of [metatensor](https://docs.metatensor.org/latest/devdoc/architecture.html) has the same layout: Rust behind a C interface, with a header-only C++ wrapper on top.
The wide top is the code that calls the solvers, the wide bottom is the Rust code that implements them, and the narrow middle, the /waist/, is one small C application binary interface (ABI) between them.
The waist is the only way from C and C++ to the solvers.
No solver is written a second time above it.
Rust hosts such as rgsaddle use the crate directly and never cross the waist.

## Layer diagram

#+CAPTION: C and C++ headers at the top, the C ABI in the middle, and the Rust modules it calls at the bottom.
[[file:../../figures/architecture/hourglass.png]]

The top row is the public headers under `include/` and the `#include` edges between them.
`include/rgmin.h` declares the functions of the waist and `src/ffi.rs` defines the same ones.
The bottom box lists the modules `src/ffi.rs` takes types and functions from.
Every vector that crosses the waist is a DLPack `DLManagedTensorVersioned` from the *dlpk* crate, so a later device path keeps the same functions.

`docs/figures/architecture/draw_hourglass.py` draws the figure from the headers and `src/` with Graphviz `dot`.
It stops if the header and the Rust source name different functions.
Redraw the figure after changing a header or the C ABI:

```bash
python3 docs/figures/architecture/draw_hourglass.py
```

## Objects

- `Lbfgs` :: Persistent pair history, two-loop recursion, eOn cap by default. `LbfgsStep::Wolfe` opts into the line search.
  Hopping chains hold this type (anneal `WarmLbfgs` is a handle).
- `Solver` :: Method-agnostic session. One `step` is one outer
  iteration. The C type `rgmin_solver_t` is a pointer to this.
- `StopReason` :: Typed stop on `Report`, beside `Status`.
  `converged()` is the `gtol` stop, including a last step that
  meets it. `MaxIter` is a spent budget and stays `Ok` unless
  `Control::with_error_on_unmet` is set, in which case the error
  is `Error::StopUnmet` and carries the report. A zero iteration
  budget is that same unmet stop. `LineSearchFailed` is a budget
  spent without accepting a step. An L-BFGS run that never moves
  reports it from `minimize_method`, `Solver::run`,
  `Solver::run_gauged`, `rgmin_minimize` and Python `minimize` alike.
  The C++ one-shots throw `rgmin::StopUnmetError` and Python
  `minimize` raises `rgmin.StopUnmetError`. Each is a runtime error
  that carries the report of the stop, as `report()` and `.report`.
  `StopReason::Iterating` is a step still in progress and has no C
  code of its own. A session step that has not stopped reports
  `RGMIN_STOP_BUDGET`. A finished one-shot never reports it, and the C
  one-shots return `RGMIN_INTERNAL_ERROR` if one did.
- `backward_error_floor` :: `n * eps * (1 + |V| + sum |x_i|)` with
  `eps` equal to `f64::EPSILON`. `with_backward_polish` takes a
  shifted Newton or RFO step from a supplied Hessian or
  Hessian-vector product. The point is accepted only when the
  Newton decrement, every coordinate step, and the gradient norm
  sit under that scale. A tiny step that misses the gradient test
  is not converged. An unmet polish is `StopReason::PolishUnmet`.
  The C names are `rgmin_backward_error_floor`,
  `rgmin_solver_set_error_on_unmet`,
  `rgmin_solver_set_backward_polish`, and the `*_opts` one-shots,
  which include `rgmin_minimize_eindir_opts`.
  `xts.h` aliases `RGMIN_UNMET_STOP`, `RGMIN_STOP_LINE_SEARCH`,
  `RGMIN_STOP_POLISH_UNMET`, `RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION`, and
  `RGMIN_STOP_LINE_SEARCH_ROUNDING`.
  `RGMIN_UNMET_STOP` is status 6. `RGMIN_STOP_LINE_SEARCH` is 4,
  `RGMIN_STOP_POLISH_UNMET` is 5, `RGMIN_STOP_ENERGY_TOLERANCE` is 6,
  `RGMIN_STOP_EVAL_BUDGET` is 7, `RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION` is 8,
  and `RGMIN_STOP_LINE_SEARCH_ROUNDING` is 9.
- `minimize_method` :: Cold-start dispatch for every `Method`.
- `LineSearch::Wolfe` :: Nocedal-Wright 3.5 / 3.6. The default line
  search of a session's line-searched methods, BFGS among them. The
  default L-BFGS step does not search a line.
- `Oracle` :: Closure adapter that implements
  `DifferentiableObjective` for a fused `(f, g)` function.
- `ecnoise` :: Moré–Wild difference table for the noise in an energy
  or in one projection of the gradient, plus the 2012 forward and
  gradient steps (Algorithm 5.1, not the noise table). One uniform
  projection has variance `tr(Σ) / n`. `Control::noise_floor` stops at
  `c * sqrt(n_free) * eps_g` with `Status::NoiseFloor`, after the
  `gtol` test. The same stop fires when a line search finds no trial
  whose decrease clears `c * eps_f`, and when a Newton-CG trust region
  trial is refused while its model predicts at most `c * eps_f`.
- `rgmin_solver_create` / `rgmin_solver_step` / `rgmin_solver_free` ::
  The session half of the waist.
  Callbacks are arguments of each step, not stored on the handle.
  `include/rgmin.h` sets `abi_major` 1, `abi_minor` 69 and
  `layout_revision` 7.
  Minor 49 adds `StopReason` on the report, the opt-in unmet-stop
  error, and the backward-error polish. A zero iteration budget
  follows the same unmet-stop policy. Minor 50 adds the energy and
  evaluation stops. Minor 51 adds `rgmin_minimize_rlbfgs` and
  `rgmin_rlbfgs_default`. Minor 52 adds `RGMIN_GROMACS_STEEP`,
  `RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION`,
  `rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_steep`, and
  `rgmin_gromacs_steep_max_constraint_shrinks`. Minor 53 adds
  `rgmin_minimize_eindir_opts`, the
  eindir one-shot with the same two flags. `rgmin_control_t` is unchanged.
  Minor 54 adds `RGMIN_GROMACS_CG` and `rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_cg`.
  Minor 55 adds
  `require_convergence` on `rgmin_control_t`, `converged` on
  `rgmin_report_t`, `RGMIN_NOT_CONVERGED`,
  `rgmin_solver_set_require_convergence`, `rgmin_control_init`, and a
  `_sized` form of each entry that reads a `rgmin_control_t`. The plain
  exported entries read and write the layout revision 5 structs.
  Minor 56 adds `rgmin_manifold_rigid_quotient`, `rgmin_rtr_tcg_solve`, `rgmin_rtr_radius_update`, `rgmin_lowest_eigenpair_on_manifold` and `rgmin_lowest_eigenpairs_projected`.
  Minor 57 adds `RGMIN_STOP_LINE_SEARCH_ROUNDING`. `rgmin_control_t` is
  unchanged. Minor 64 covers this branch's stop-reporting and eindir
  callback-error fixes without a layout change.
  Minor 65 adds `RGMIN_RCG`, `rgmin_rcg_options_t`, `rgmin_rcg_options_default` and `rgmin_minimize_rcg`.
  The new struct leaves every existing struct as it was, so the layout revision stays 6.
  Minor 66 adds `rgmin_vec_precond_fn`, `rgmin_minimize_hvp_precond` and
  `rgmin_minimize_hvp_precond_sized`. No struct changes, so the layout revision stays 6.
  Minor 67 adds `RGMIN_GROMACS_LBFGS` and
  `rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_lbfgs`. `rgmin_control_t` is unchanged.
  Minor 68 adds `noise_eps_f` on `rgmin_control_t` and `RGMIN_CONTROL_REVISION6_SIZE`; the struct grows, so the layout revision becomes 7.
  Minor 69 adds `rgmin_solver_set_fixed_h0` and
  `rgmin_solver_set_ase_linesearch`.
  `rgmin_abi_compatible` checks the major version and the layout revision only.
- `DistanceConstraints` :: Holonomic atom-pair distances for a session.
  SHAKE, LINCS and SETTLE return each trial to the set.
  The C type `rgmin_constraints_t` is a pointer to this.
- `ManifoldKind` :: Embedded geometry. Euclidean is the identity.
  Every kind implements `project` / `retract` / `transport`, for
  example Sphere, SO(3), Stiefel `St(n,1)`, SE(3), Spd and a product.
  @@rst::doc:`../howto/manifolds`@@ lists the kinds.
- `rgmin_minimize` :: First-order / quasi-Newton C entry. CPU f64
  tensors only; other devices return `RGMIN_UNSUPPORTED_DEVICE`.
- `rgmin_minimize_hess` :: Newton / RFO C entry. Caller supplies a
  dense row-major Hessian. This is a different solver, not an
  L-BFGS option.
- `Solver::set_precon` / `rgmin_solver_set_precon` :: Exp, Lindh, the
  bonded metric, or `select_precon`. ABI minor 32.
- `rgmin_solver_set_quickmin_variant` :: Quick-min options from C:
  `RGMIN_QUICKMIN_RGMIN`, `RGMIN_QUICKMIN_EON`,
  `RGMIN_QUICKMIN_PER_ATOM`. ABI minor 33.
  `rgmin_solver_precon_scale` is `μ` after the sine probe.
- `select_precon` :: L-BFGS and CG: Exp at 100 atoms for bulk,
  surface, and a metal cluster (ASE `PreconLBFGS`). Lindh for a
  covalent molecule or cluster up to `N_LINDH`. Bonded metric when
  that caller has a force field and every element is covalent.
  FIRE auto is the identity.

| C kind | Rust | role |
|---+---|---|
| `RGMIN_PRECON_EXP` | `PreconSpec::Exp` | `H_0 ` P^{-1}= for L-BFGS, metric for CG and FIRE |
| `RGMIN_PRECON_LINDH` | `PreconSpec::Lindh` | model Hessian, same solve |
| `RGMIN_PRECON_FF` | `PreconSpec::Ff` | bonded metric, harmonic terms on the C struct |
| `RGMIN_PRECON_AUTO` | `select_precon` | the session method plus the how-to table |
| `RGMIN_PRECON_NONE` | `clear_precon` | drop the metric |

# Distance constraints

This page states what a `DistanceConstraints` set computes, which tolerances and budgets it derives, and where it agrees with GROMACS.
@@rst::doc:`../howto/constraints`@@ shows how to install a set on a session.

## The set and its metric

Constraint `k` fixes the bond `r_k = x_i - x_j` of the pair `(i, j)` at the length `d_k`.
`J` is the Jacobian of `(|r_k|^2 - d_k^2) / 2`, so row `k` has `r_k` at atom `i` and `-r_k` at atom `j`.
`M` is the diagonal matrix of atom masses, three entries per atom, and `W = M^{-1}`.
Without `with_masses`, `M = I`.

These masses weight the coordinates of the session, `q = M^{1/2} x`.
A vector `v` of `x` is `M^{1/2} v` in `q`, and a gradient `g` of `x` is `W^{1/2} g` in `q`.
Steps, stored pairs and the stop test all live in `q`, so a quasi-Newton method works on the set with the inner product `<u, v>_M = u^T M v`.

## Tangent projection

Tangent vectors at a point `x` of the set come from the projector

`Pi = I - W J^T (J W J^T)^{-1} J`,

which RATTLE applies to velocities (Andersen [1983](https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-9991(83)90014-1)).
A direction is projected with `Pi` and a gradient with `Pi^T g = g - J^T lambda`, `lambda = (J W J^T)^{-1} J W g`.
In `q`, `Pi_q = M^{1/2} Pi M^{-1/2}` is symmetric, so it is the orthogonal projector of that space.
The gradient of a step is `g_q = W^{1/2} Pi^T g`, and `grad_norm` reports `|Pi^T g|` in the session's stop norm.
At a constrained minimum `g = J^T lambda`, with `lambda` the vector of Lagrange multipliers.

The projector and the multipliers need one solve with `J W J^T` per block of coupled constraints, a connected part of the constraint graph.
For one block the solve uses the scaled coupling `S = D^{-1/2} J W J^T D^{-1/2}` with `D = diag(J W J^T)`, which has a unit diagonal.
Its extreme eigenvalues come from cyclic Jacobi rotations, largest entry first, to `U ||S||_F`, with `U` the unit roundoff.
A backward-stable Cholesky solve with `S` gains `log2(1 / (b kappa gamma(6)))` bits per pass, with `b` the block size, `kappa = lambda_max / lambda_min` and `gamma(n) = n U / (1 - n U)` (Higham 2002, Lemma 3.1).
A block where that is under one bit is `ConstraintError::Dependent`.
The projection repeats the solve until every `|J_k u|` is within `gamma(6)` of the magnitudes it was formed from, a budget of the bits to gain over the bits per pass.

## Return to the set

A step leaves the set at a point `x`, the anchor, and arrives at a trial `y`.
The trial returns to the set by corrections along the anchor bonds,

`y' = y - W J(x)^T mu`, with `mu` chosen so that `|r_k(y')| = d_k` for every `k`.

Three solvers meet these equations.
Ryckaert, Ciccotti and Berendsen ([1977](https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-9991(77)90098-5)) gave the Gauss-Seidel bond solver (SHAKE).
The linear constraint solver (LINCS) comes from Hess, Bekker, Berendsen and Fraaije ([1997](https://doi.org/10.1002/(sici)1096-987x(199709)18:12%3C1463::aid-jcc4%3E3.0.co;2-h)).
Miyamoto and Kollman ([1992](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.540130805)) solved the rigid triangle in closed form with SETTLE.
They differ in how, not in the answer, so `R_x(v) = constrain(x + v)` is one retraction whichever solver ran.
The corrections run along `W J(x)^T`, a fixed complement of the tangent space at `x`.
Hence `R_x(0) = x`, and `R_x` has the identity on tangent vectors as its derivative at zero.
That makes `R` a retraction in the sense of Absil, Mahony and Sepulchre @@rst::cite:`absilOptimizationAlgorithmsMatrix2008`@@, of the projection-like kind that Absil and Malick study ([2012](https://doi.org/10.1137/100802529)).

The residual of constraint `k` is the GROMACS SHAKE measure `e_k = |d_k^2 - |r_k|^2| / (2 d_k^2)`.
Its tolerance is `max(t, f_k)`, with `t` from `with_tolerance` and the floor

`f_k = gamma(6) / 2 + U reach_k / d_k`, `reach_k = || |x_i| + |x_j| ||_2`.

The first term bounds the rounding error of `e_k` itself: five operations for `|r_k|^2` and one for `d_k^2`.
The second covers the stored coordinates, each rounded to `U` of its magnitude, along the bond.
No constraint can be met more tightly than its floor, so `t = 0`, the default, asks for the floor.
`excess` is the largest `e_k` over its tolerance.

### SHAKE

Gauss-Seidel SHAKE takes the constraints of a block in turn and moves the two atoms of each along its anchor bond by the Newton step of its own length equation, split by the inverse masses.
A constraint within its tolerance is skipped.
SHAKE returns `ConstraintError::Reversed` when a trial bond turns a right angle or more from its anchor direction.
No correction along the anchor bond can then restore its length.

Near the set the sweep is linear Gauss-Seidel on `S`.
With the splitting `S = (I + L) + L^T`, its contraction in the `S` norm is `rho_GS^2 <= 1 - lambda_min / ||I + L||_F^2`.
The bound follows from the Xu-Zikatanov identity, with the Frobenius norm as an upper bound on the spectral norm.
The sweep budget is the number of sweeps that contraction needs to bring the largest residual to its tolerance, after converting between the residual and the `S` norm.
A lone bond adds its Newton sweeps, which double the correct bits each time.
A block that spends the budget is `ConstraintError::NotConverged`.

### LINCS

One LINCS projection sets every `n_k . r_k` to a target, with `n_k` the unit anchor bond, by summing the expansion `(I - A)^{-1} = sum_p A^p` of `S = I - A` (Hess et al. 1997, eqs. 18-20).
The expansion converges when `rho_L = max |1 - lambda(S)| < 1`.
The order is the number of terms that brings the truncation bound `rho_L^{n + 1} / (1 - rho_L)` to the tolerance, unless `with_lincs_order` fixes it.
The first projection removes `n_k . r_k - d_k`.
Each later correction removes `d_k - sqrt(2 d_k^2 - l_k^2)`, the lengthening a rotation leaves (eq. 21, GROMACS `calc_dist_iter`), until every constraint meets its tolerance.
Each correction gains one bit from the rotation and `(order + 1) log2(1 / rho_L)` bits from the expansion, and the budget counts the smaller gain.

`ConstraintSolver::Auto` takes LINCS on a block when `rho_L < 1` and `rho_L <= rho_GS`, and SHAKE otherwise.
`ConstraintSolver::Lincs` on a block with `rho_L >= 1` is `ConstraintError::LincsUnsafe`.
A light atom bonded to two or more heavy ones gives such a block: the off-diagonal couplings of `S` approach the cosines of the bond angles.

### SETTLE

A block of three atoms and three constraints is a rigid triangle.
Corrections along the anchor bonds lie in the anchor plane and are central forces between the anchor positions.
So every atom keeps its coordinate along the anchor normal, and the centre of mass stays where the trial put it.
The corrections also exert no torque about the normal at the anchor positions.
The rigid triangle that meets these conditions is the converged SHAKE answer.
SETTLE finds it in closed form: the normal coordinates fix the tilt of the triangle, and the torque condition fixes its angle in the plane through `C cos(theta) + D sin(theta) = E`.
SETTLE takes the root nearer the trial in the mass metric.
When `|E| > sqrt(C^2 + D^2)` no root exists, and SETTLE returns `ConstraintError::SettleDegenerate`.
A SHAKE pass then removes the rounding of the closed form.
Miyamoto and Kollman treat water with equal hydrogen masses and equal O-H lengths; the derivation here needs neither.

## Steps on the set

Every method projects its direction with `Pi_q` and places the trial at `x + W^{1/2} d`.
The trial is capped like an unconstrained one and then returned to the set.
Coordinate bounds act only on atoms outside every pair, where `Pi` is the identity, so the box projection commutes with `Pi`.
A constrained atom that a trial takes to its bound is `ConstraintError::Bound`.
What each method stores is moved to the new tangent space by projection, the vector transport of Absil, Mahony and Sepulchre (section 8.1.3) @@rst::cite:`absilOptimizationAlgorithmsMatrix2008`@@:

- L-BFGS stores `s_q = Pi_q(x+) M^{1/2} (x+ - x)` and `y_q = g_q+ - Pi_q(x+) g_q`, and projects every stored pair at each new point.
- Nonlinear conjugate gradients project the previous gradient and direction, and Barzilai-Borwein projects its last pair.
- Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS), SR1 and SR2 update with the same tangent pair as L-BFGS.
- The fast inertial relaxation engine (FIRE) projects its velocity and its force with the same projector.
- Adam keeps its moments, and its direction is projected like every other.

Under `Accept::Energy` and `Accept::Nonmonotone`, L-BFGS runs its line search along the curve `R(t) = constrain(x + t d)`.
The slope of the curve at a trial `r = R(t)` is `g(r)^T R'(t)`, with `R'(t) = d - W J(x)^T mu` and `J(r) R'(t) = 0`, one oblique block solve per trial.
Newton, the rational function optimization (RFO) step and dogleg use the Hessian of the Lagrangian `H - sum_k lambda_k nabla^2 c_k` on the tangent space.
Newton-CG uses the same operator through Hessian-vector products.

## Agreement with GROMACS

The GROMACS 2026.4 sources `src/gromacs/mdlib/shake.cpp`, `lincs.cpp`, `settle.cpp`, `constr.cpp` and `mdrun/minimize.cpp` were the working reference.
The code here is written for minimization and is not a translation.

| Topic | GROMACS | rgmin |
|---+---+---|
| SHAKE residual | `0.5 abs(d^2 - r^2) / d^2` against `shake-tol` | Same measure, tolerance at least the rounding floor |
| Iteration budget | `maxnit = 1000` | Derived from the Gauss-Seidel contraction |
| Bond reversal | `r_ref . r < 1e-10 d^2` is an error | A right angle between anchor and trial bond is `Reversed` |
| LINCS order | `lincs-order`, default 4; `grompp` asks for 8 with CG and L-BFGS | Derived from `rho_L` and the tolerance, or fixed |
| Rotational corrections | `lincs-iter`, default 1 | Until the tolerance, within a derived budget |
| Coupled angles | Accepted; triangles get extra recursions | `Auto` picks SHAKE where the expansion diverges or is slower |
| SETTLE | Water: equal hydrogen masses and O-H lengths | Any rigid triangle, any masses |
| Masses in minimization | Every mass is one | Unit by default, real masses on request |
| SHAKE in minimization | `grompp` refuses it for CG and L-BFGS ("use LINCS"); steepest descent stops in `mdrun`, which cannot project forces with SHAKE | Supported |
| L-BFGS with constraints | Not implemented; `mdrun` stops | Supported, with transported pairs and a search on the curve |
| Conjugate gradients with constraints | LINCS and SETTLE only; a step they cannot meet ends the run | Supported with every solver; under the energy tests such a trial is refused and shortened |

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/reference/gromacs-cg.org`

# GROMACS-style conjugate gradient

`Method::GromacsCg` pairs the GROMACS-style Polak-Ribière
conjugate-gradient direction update from GROMACS 2025.4
[do_cg](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/v2025.4/src/gromacs/mdrun/minimize.cpp#L1313)
(`src/gromacs/mdrun/minimize.cpp`, lines 1313-2035) with `rgmin`'s
strong-Wolfe line search (`c1 = 1e-4`, `c2 = 0.1`) rather than
GROMACS's own golden-section/cubic-secant line search:

\[
\mathbf{p}_k = -\mathbf{g}_k + \beta_k \mathbf{p}_{k-1}, \qquad
\beta_k = \frac{\mathbf{g}_k \cdot (\mathbf{g}_k - \mathbf{g}_{k-1})}{\mathbf{g}_{k-1} \cdot \mathbf{g}_{k-1}},
\]

where $\mathbf{g}_k = -\mathbf{F}_k$ is the potential-energy gradient.

Because the line search differs from `do_cg`, `Method::GromacsCg` is not
a step-for-step clone of `gmx mdrun` under `integrator = cg`. What matches
`do_cg` and what is `rgmin`-specific is listed below.

## Direction update and strong-Wolfe line search

Rather than duplicating `do_cg`'s bracket/secant/bisection search loop,
`Method::GromacsCg` runs on top of `rgmin`'s existing `Inner::Nlcg`
(`Conjugacy::PolakRibiere`) and `LineSearch::Wolfe` infrastructure
(`take_session_step`), adding the direction and acceptance rules from
`do_cg`:

1. *Periodic steepest-descent restart (`nstcgsteep`)*: `do_cg` counts its
   iterations with `for (step = 0; ...; step++)` and, once iteration
   `step` has moved, sets $\beta = 0$ for the next direction when
   `nstcg && ((step % nstcg) == 0)` (`minimize.cpp` lines 1497 and
   1868-1871). `GromacsCg::step` is that counter and
   `GromacsCg::filter_beta` applies the test before `GromacsCg::advance`,
   so the steepest-descent directions are those of iterations 0, 1,
   $\text{nstcgsteep} + 1$, $2\,\text{nstcgsteep} + 1$, and so on: the
   second step is always steepest descent. As in `do_cg`, a restart for a
   positive $\mathbf{g} \cdot \mathbf{p}$ (`gpa > 0`, which undoes its count
   with `step--`) keeps the index, while the retry of a stalled conjugate
   step spends one. `nstcgsteep = 0` turns the periodic restart off.
   `Solver::forget` sets the counter back to zero, so a forgotten session
   restarts like a fresh one. The default is
   `GROMACS_CG_NSTCGSTEEP_DEFAULT = 1000`
   ([MDP nstcgsteep](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdp-options.html#mdp-nstcgsteep)).
2. *Polak-Ribière multiplier cap*: `do_cg` suppresses the conjugate term
   when $|\beta_k| > 5.0$ (`minimize.cpp` lines 1883-1887:
   `if (std::fabs(beta) > 5.0) { beta = 0.0; }`). `GromacsCg::filter_beta`
   enforces the same `GROMACS_CG_BETA_CAP = 5.0` bound on the raw
   Polak-Ribière ratio from `Conjugacy::PolakRibiere`.
3. *Unit search direction and opening step scale*: before entering the line
   search, the search direction is normalized to unit Euclidean length via
   overflow-safe scaling. On the first step, the opening trial step is
   `Control::istep` (`emstep`, default `GROMACS_CG_EMSTEP_DEFAULT = 0.01`);
   subsequent steps scale the previous accepted step length through
   rgmin's Nocedal-Wright eq. 3.60 opening estimate (`nlcg_opening_alpha`).
   The session defaults to strong Wolfe with $c_1 = 10^{-4}$ and the
   conjugate-gradient curvature parameter $c_2 = 0.1$ so cubic Hermite
   zoom locates the 1D directional stationary point before the next
   Polak-Ribière update. Callers can override the line search via
   `Solver::set_linesearch` or `minimize_method`.
4. *Steepest-descent fallback on a stalled conjugate direction*: if a
   line search along a conjugate direction ($\beta_{k-1} \neq 0$) fails to
   decrease the energy or rounds away all coordinates, the session clears
   the CG memory and retries the step along the steepest-descent direction
   $-\mathbf{g}_k$, matching the `beta = 0.0; continue;` branch of `do_cg`
   (`minimize.cpp` lines 1814-1832). If a steepest-descent step still cannot change any
   coordinate or decrease the energy, the session stops with
   `Status::MachinePrecision` (`RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION`).
5. *Downhill energy-rise tolerance near machine precision*: `do_cg`
   accepts a trial whose energy rises slightly below
   $\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\text{mach}}}\,|E_0|$ when the directional
   derivative remains negative (`minimize.cpp` lines 1665-1672:
   `tmp = std::sqrt(GMX_REAL_EPS) * std::fabs(s_a->epot); if (s_c->epot < s_a->epot || (gpc < 0 && s_c->epot < (s_a->epot + tmp)))`).
   `Method::GromacsCg` enables this same tolerance in `LineSearchOptions`
   and `take_step_with_options`.
6. *Max-atom force norm (`Fmax`)*: `Report::stop_norm` defaults to
   `StopNorm::MaxAtom` ($\max_i \|\mathbf{F}_i\|_2$ over consecutive xyz
   atom triples), matching `gmx_f_norm_max` in `minimize.cpp` and
   `Method::GromacsSteep`. There is no implicit 0.2 per-atom displacement
   cap unless explicitly requested.
7. *Step counting (`nsteps` / `maxiter`)*: `rgmin` takes `Control::maxiter`
   steps (`nsteps = 0` evaluates only the initial point; Python/MDP
   `nsteps = -1` maps to unlimited `sys.maxsize`). By contrast, upstream
   GROMACS `do_cg` loops `for (step = 0; (number_steps < 0 || step <= number_steps) && !converged; step++)`
   (`minimize.cpp` line 1497), executing `nsteps + 1` iterations on a
   budget stop (13 steps for `nsteps = 12` in the committed `mdrun.txt`)
   and decrementing `step` by one when converged.

## Refusal of holonomic constraints

GROMACS 2025.4 runs `do_cg` with LINCS constraints applied to each trial
configuration; `gmx grompp` refuses only SHAKE with `integrator = cg`
([grompp.cpp](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/v2025.4/src/gromacs/gmxpreprocess/grompp.cpp#L2371))
and suggests `lincs-order` of 8 or more
([readir.cpp](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/v2025.4/src/gromacs/gmxpreprocess/readir.cpp#L5365)).
`gromacs-cg` does not implement that constrained line search: projecting
coordinates back onto a nonlinear constraint manifold after a step breaks
the conjugacy of consecutive search directions that the rest of the
session relies on. Use `gromacs-steep` for constrained systems.

`rgmin` refuses holonomic constraints on `gromacs-cg` across every layer:
- Rust / C / C++: `Solver::set_distance_constraints` (`rgmin_solver_set_distance_constraints`)
  and stepping with an installed `DistanceConstraints` set return
  `Error::Constraint(ConstraintError::Unsupported)` (`RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_ERROR`).
- Python `gromacs_mdp_options`: any `constraints` value other than `"none"`
  raises `ValueError`.
- Python `GromacsCg` ASE optimizer: holonomic geometry constraints on
  `atoms` (such as `FixBondLength` / `FixBondLengths`) or a non-`"none"`
  `constraints` keyword raise `ValueError`. Linear coordinate subspace
  masks (`FixAtoms`, `FixCartesian`, `FixedLine`, `FixedPlane`, analogous
  to GROMACS `freezegrps` / `freezedim`) remain supported.

## Stops and reports

| condition | `Status` | C ABI |
|-----------+----------+-------|
| largest per-atom force is below `Control::gtol` (`emtol`) | `Tolerance` | `RGMIN_STOP_TOLERANCE` |
| `Control::maxiter` (`nsteps`) steps were taken | `Budget` | `RGMIN_STOP_BUDGET` |
| a steepest-descent step cannot change any coordinate or decrease the energy | `MachinePrecision` | `RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION` |
| callback returned a non-finite value or gradient | `Error::Oracle` | `RGMIN_INTERNAL_ERROR` (+ `rgmin_last_error`) |
| holonomic distance constraints were attached | `Error::Constraint` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_ERROR` (+ `rgmin_last_constraint_error`) |

## GROMACS-unit mapping

The Python `gromacs_mdp_options` helper converts:

| MDP key | default | native option |
|---------+---------+---------------|
| `integrator` | `"steep"` (`"cg"` selects CG) | `method = "gromacs-cg"` |
| `emtol` | 10.0 kJ mol^-1 nm^-1 | `gtol` in eV Å^-1 |
| `emstep` | 0.01 nm | `istep` in Å |
| `nsteps` | -1 | no limit; otherwise `maxiter` |
| `nstcgsteep` | 1000 | `nstcgsteep` ($\ge 0$, 0 turns the restart off; `cg` only) |
| `constraints` | `"none"` | validated; non-`"none"` raises `ValueError` on `cg` |

The Rust stepper, C ABI, and C++ wrapper do no unit conversion. C and C++
expose `nstcgsteep` through `rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_cg` /
`Solver::set_gromacs_cg`; `RGMIN_GROMACS_CG` and
`rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_cg` are declared in `include/rgmin.h`.

## Comparison against `gmx mdrun` on the 7-atom argon cluster

The 7-atom Lennard-Jones argon cluster fixture
(`tests/data/gromacs_steep_argon.txt`, $\sigma = 0.34\text{ nm}$,
$\epsilon ` 1.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, $r_c ` 3.0\text{ nm}$,
$\text{emstep} ` 0.02\text{ nm}$, $\text{nstcgsteep} ` 1000$) was run with
both double-precision `gmx_d mdrun` and single-precision `gmx mdrun`
(GROMACS 2023.3 built from source with GCC 13.3.0 and AVX2_256 SIMD,
`-nt 1 -ntmpi 1`) under `integrator = cg` and compared against `rgmin`
(`Method::GromacsCg`). The complete inputs, terminal output, `em.log` files,
and machine-readable summary are committed under
`tests/data/gromacs_cg_reference/`.

| run / tolerance | solver | steps | force evals | final $E_{\text{pot}}$ (kJ mol^-1) | final $F_{\max}$ (kJ mol^-1 nm^-1) |
|-----------------+--------+-------+-------------+------------------------------------+------------------------------------|
| `nsteps = 12`, `emtol = 1e-8` | `gmx_d mdrun` (f64) | 12 | 16 | `-1.25489376279604e+01` | `3.54506056338870e-03` |
| `nsteps = 12`, `emtol = 1e-8` | `gmx mdrun` (f32) | 11 | 25 | `-1.2548939e+01` | `4.3311492e-03` |
| `nsteps = 12`, `emtol = 1e-8` | `rgmin` `GromacsCg` | 12 | 60 | `-1.25489377088303e+01` | `4.735427e-07` |
| `emtol = 1e-2` | `gmx_d mdrun` (f64) | 9 | 12 | `-1.25489364597334e+01` | `5.54402580304420e-03` |
| `emtol = 1e-2` | `rgmin` `GromacsCg` | 6 | 18 | `-1.25489374174275e+01` | `8.694525e-03` |
| `emtol = 1e-3` | `gmx_d mdrun` (f64) | 13 | 18 | `-1.25489376639539e+01` | `4.98089785018483e-04` |
| `emtol = 1e-3` | `rgmin` `GromacsCg` | 7 | 22 | `-1.25489377085847e+01` | `1.529776e-04` |
| `emtol = 1e-6` | `gmx_d mdrun` (f64) | 57 | 72 | `-1.25489377088303e+01` | `3.48102157458076e-07` |
| `emtol = 1e-6` | `rgmin` `GromacsCg` | 9 | 33 | `-1.25489377088303e+01` | `7.015111e-07` |

Both solvers take steepest-descent steps at iterations 0 and 1 and
conjugate steps after that. Because `rgmin` uses its strong-Wolfe
bracketing and cubic-zoom line search ($c_1 ` 10^{-4}, c_2 ` 0.1$) rather
than `do_cg`'s midpoint/cubic secant heuristic (and stops at `nsteps`
steps rather than `nsteps + 1`), step-by-step intermediate
iterates differ while
converging to the same potential-energy minimum
($-12.548937708830\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) on this fixture. Note also that in
the `nsteps = 12` run below, `summary.tsv` records `12` (the `nsteps`
input / last step index `Step 12`), while `gmx_d mdrun` actually executed
13 steps (`Step 0` through `Step 12`) before reporting `in 13 steps`.
On this fixture, `rgmin` uses fewer outer iterations at each tested
tolerance. It uses more force evaluations at `emtol = 1e-2` and `1e-3`,
but fewer at `emtol = 1e-6`. At the 12-step cap it uses more force
evaluations and reaches a lower $F_{\max}$. The single-precision
GROMACS run stops at machine precision after 11 steps. No GROMACS
trajectory equivalence beyond these tested final-energy and force-norm
comparisons is claimed.

# GROMACS L-BFGS

`Method::GromacsLbfgs` follows `do_lbfgs` in the tagged GROMACS 2023.3
source,
[minimize.cpp, lines 1978--2797](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/v2023.3/src/gromacs/mdrun/minimize.cpp#L1978-L2797)
(`src/gromacs/mdrun/minimize.cpp`). The MDP defaults come from the same
tag's MDP option documentation for
[nsteps](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/v2023.3/docs/user-guide/mdp-options.rst#L206-L210),
[emtol and emstep](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/v2023.3/docs/user-guide/mdp-options.rst#L328-L337), and
[nbfgscorr](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/v2023.3/docs/user-guide/mdp-options.rst#L345-L349).

## Algorithm

The first direction is the force, $\mathbf p_0=-\mathbf g_0$, and the
opening scalar step is $1/\|\mathbf F_0\|_2$. Before evaluation, GROMACS
repeatedly multiplies it by 0.1 until the largest positive coordinate
displacement is no greater than `emstep`. Although the MDP manual calls
`emstep` the "initial step-size", `do_lbfgs` uses it as this displacement
ceiling (lines 2348--2374); rgmin follows the source.

An opening point $C$ is accepted immediately when its energy is lower
than point $A$, or when its directional derivative is still negative
and its energy rise is below
$\sqrt{\epsilon}\lvert E_A\rvert$. Otherwise the search brackets between
$A$ and $C$. It interpolates the derivative zero when the opening
derivatives at $A$ and $C$ have opposite signs, bisects otherwise, and
stops at the
first point below both endpoints. The search makes at most 20 bracket
trials (lines 2400--2557).

For an accepted displacement $\mathbf s$ and gradient change
$\mathbf y$, rgmin keeps at most `nbfgscorr` pairs and uses the same
two-loop recursion and scalar initial inverse Hessian
$H_0=(\mathbf s^T\mathbf y)/(\mathbf y^T\mathbf y) I$ as lines
2559--2663. The default correction count is 10.

If the line search cannot resolve a lower energy, nonempty correction
memory is cleared and the next direction is the force. That clear drops
every stored pair. GROMACS leaves the ring index in place; the
difference is documented below. Failure with empty memory stops at
machine precision (lines 2510--2534). Every accepted step resets the
opening scalar step to 1 (line 2725).
Calling `Solver::rebase`, `Solver::forget_evaluation`, or supplying
externally moved coordinates retains the correction pairs and rebuilds
the two-loop direction at the new point with opening step
$1/\|\mathbf F\|_2$.

## Stops and reporting

`emtol` is the largest per-atom force norm, so the default stop norm is
`StopNorm::MaxAtom`. `nsteps` maps to `Control::maxiter` and `-1` maps
to no Python iteration limit. Reports expose outer iterations and
all objective/force evaluations, including line-search trials.

| condition | status |
|-----------+--------|
| $F_{\max}<\texttt{emtol}$ | `Tolerance` |
| `nsteps` exhausted | `Budget` |
| line step below the relative-coordinate precision threshold, or an empty-memory search cannot lower energy | `MachinePrecision` |
| callback produces a non-finite value or gradient | `Error::Oracle` |

## Exactness and differences

For an unconstrained Euclidean objective without active coordinate
bounds, no frozen coordinates, and no line-search reset, the correction
recursion, displacement check, line search, and force stop reproduce
GROMACS 2023.3 `do_lbfgs`. `do_lbfgs` is the same algorithm in the tagged
2023.3 and 2025.4 sources. The following differences are deliberate:

- After a line search that cannot lower the energy, GROMACS sets
  `ncorr = 0` and leaves the ring index `point` unchanged (lines
  2524--2533). The two-loop recursion then wraps a negative index to
  `ncorr - 1`, not to `nbfgscorr - 1` (lines 2600--2609). Once new
  corrections fill past the end of the buffer, that walk reads pairs
  stored before the reset. rgmin clears the correction deque in
  `restart_steepest`, and `apply_pairs` walks only pairs stored since
  that clear.
- rgmin leaves the frozen-coordinate force in the L-BFGS direction, the
  stored pairs, and the curvature, so a frozen atom moves on the first
  iteration. `project_vec` removes only rigid modes that already vanish
  on the frozen coordinates. GROMACS writes zero into the stored search
  direction on frozen components (lines 2205--2216 and 2654--2663) but
  keeps the raw force in `p`, `dg`, and `dgdg` (lines 2570--2598).
  `get_f_norm_max` excludes frozen components from `fnorm` and `fmax`
  (lines 279--298). A GROMACS reset copies the raw force, frozen
  components included, into the next direction (line 2529). The two
  trajectories therefore differ from iteration 1.
- GROMACS refuses L-BFGS with domain decomposition, multiple ranks, or
  constraints (lines 1993--2008). rgmin has no rank/domain-decomposition
  state and refuses holonomic distance constraints. Frozen linear
  coordinate masks stay available, with the force treatment above.
- rgmin uses binary64 `f64::EPSILON`. A single-precision GROMACS build
  uses its larger `GMX_REAL_EPS`.
- GROMACS uses 1 nm as the characteristic coordinate in its
  machine-precision step test (lines 2289--2307). The unit-agnostic Rust
  API uses 1 in the objective's coordinate unit. Consequently the Python
  Å mapping can stop at a slightly different last representable step.
- rgmin checks `emtol` at the point supplied to a session before taking
  another step. `do_lbfgs` checks it after an accepted step.
- The existing Python MDP helper defaults `nsteps` to `-1` (unlimited);
  the GROMACS 2023.3 MDP default is 0. An explicit `nsteps` value maps
  directly to the rgmin iteration budget. GROMACS `do_lbfgs` uses an
  inclusive `step <= nsteps` loop and can attempt one additional outer
  iteration; rgmin keeps the exact-budget convention shared by its
  other GROMACS front ends.
- `do_lbfgs` divides by curvature without validating it. rgmin returns
  `Error::GromacsLbfgs` for zero or non-finite curvature instead of
  propagating a non-finite direction.
- Active objective bounds or non-Euclidean retractions alter trial
  coordinates, so their iterates are extensions rather than an exact
  GROMACS trajectory.

The C ABI selector is `RGMIN_GROMACS_LBFGS`. ABI minor 67 adds it and
`rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_lbfgs`.

## GROMACS comparison

The seven-atom argon fixture in `tests/data/gromacs_steep_argon.*` was
minimized with double-precision `gmx_d` from Ubuntu's `gromacs` 2023.3
package (`2023.3-Ubuntu_2023.3_1ubuntu3`, SSE4.1, one thread). The run
uses `integrator = l-bfgs`, `emtol = 1e-8`, `emstep = 0.02`,
`nbfgscorr = 10`, and `nsteps = 12`. GROMACS treats that limit as
inclusive (`step <= nsteps`), so the footer is the state after 13
accepted iterations:

| solver | accepted steps | force evaluations | final energy | final Fmax |
|--------+----------------+-------------------+--------------+------------|
| `gmx_d` 2023.3 double | 13 | 15 | -1.25489377088304e+01 | 7.27914686102068e-08 |
| rgmin `GromacsLbfgs`, `maxiter = 13` | 13 | 15 | -1.25489377088303e+01 | 7.28008804951526e-08 |

The evaluation counts match. The energies agree to `1e-11`, which is
tighter than the change of the last accepted step. `Fmax` differs in
the last digits because a coordinate difference far below the printed
energy moves the force. `tests/data/gromacs_lbfgs_argon.txt`, produced
by `tests/data/gromacs_lbfgs_argon_driver.py`, records the same footer
energy, maximum force, and evaluation count at every inclusive
`nsteps` for several `nbfgscorr` and `emstep` settings.
`tests/gromacs_lbfgs.rs` asserts that file. A single-precision GROMACS
build still uses a larger `GMX_REAL_EPS` than `f64::EPSILON`, so this
table does not describe that build.
