Source: `docs/orgmode/reference/gromacs-steep.org`

# GROMACS steepest descent

`Method::GromacsSteep` implements the update documented in the
[GROMACS reference manual, Energy Minimization: Steepest Descent](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/reference-manual/algorithms/energy-minimization.html#steepest-descent):

\[
r_{n+1} = r_n + h_n F_n / \max_i |F_{n,i}|.
\]

The maximum is the largest Euclidean norm of one consecutive xyz atom
triple. A trailing partial triple is one atom. A strict energy decrease
accepts the trial and sets `h <- 1.2 h`. An equal or larger energy rejects
the trial, keeps the old point and force, and sets `h <- shrink * h`.
`GromacsSteepConfig` defaults `shrink` to 0.5.

The implementation follows the state-swap structure and strict energy
comparison in GROMACS 2025.4
[do_steep](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/v2025.4/src/gromacs/mdrun/minimize.cpp#L3104).
That function multiplies a rejected `ustep` by 0.5 (`minimize.cpp`
line 3104) and an accepted one by 1.2 when `count > 0` (line 3092).
The reference manual still says 0.2. `GromacsSteepConfig::with_shrink`
and `Solver::set_gromacs_steep_config` select that factor, or any other
finite value in `(0, 1)`. The Python `Session` keyword `shrink`
does the same for `gromacs-steep`.

## Stops and reports

| condition | `Status` | C ABI |
|---+---+---|
| largest per-atom force is below `Control::gtol` | `Tolerance` | `RGMIN_STOP_TOLERANCE` |
| `Control::maxiter` trials were attempted | `Budget` | `RGMIN_STOP_BUDGET` |
| the proposed displacement cannot change any coordinate, or it fell below rgmin's displacement floor | `MachinePrecision` | `RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION` |
| callback returned a non-finite value or gradient | `Error::Oracle` | `RGMIN_INTERNAL_ERROR` (+ `rgmin_last_error`) |
| an explicit shrink budget ran out while the displacement was still at least the floor | `Error::Constraint` | `RGMIN_CONSTRAINT_ERROR` (+ `rgmin_last_constraint_error`) |

`Report::stop_norm` is `StopNorm::MaxAtom` by default for this method,
even when the input `Control` names another norm. An explicit
`Solver::set_stop_norm` call after construction overrides that default,
the same as for any other method. Rejected trials count as steps.
`Solver::gromacs_step_size` returns the displacement that the next trial
will use.
This differs from GROMACS `do_steep` in one place by design: a
non-finite trial is an immediate oracle error here, where GROMACS
refuses the trial and shrinks.

## Session hooks

The core state contains `h` and the 1.2 / `shrink` update. The session
projects rigid motion from the force before normalization, applies an
explicit per-atom or Euclidean `maxmove` cap to the proposed displacement,
and uses the ordinary manifold, coordinate-bound, and holonomic-distance
constraint placement. A constraint the trial cannot meet is a refused
step: the old point is kept and `h` is multiplied by `shrink`, the
same branch GROMACS takes by setting the trial energy to +infinity
(`minimize.cpp` lines 3008-3009 and 3104).
`GromacsSteepConfig::max_constraint_shrinks` bounds that run. The
session derives its default from the actual `emstep` and shrink factor:
the least `k` with `h * shrink^k` below `GROMACS_STEEP_MIN_USTEP`,
rgmin's own displacement floor. GROMACS `do_steep` has no such floor.
At the canonical `emstep = 0.01` and `shrink = 0.5`, that count is 34,
and that default budget is the same rgmin safeguard. Crossing the
floor stops with `Status::MachinePrecision` and keeps the last accepted
point. An explicit budget that runs out while `h` is still at least
the floor returns `Error::Constraint`. Zero returns that error on the
first failure and does not shrink. A placement that meets the
constraints restarts the count. The trial energy is tested only after
those hooks,
so an accepted step and its reported gradient describe the point the host
receives.

There is no implicit rgmin 0.2 per-atom cap: `h` is already the GROMACS
maximum displacement. An explicit cap still applies.

## GROMACS-unit mapping

The Python `gromacs_mdp_options` layer converts:

| MDP key | default | native option |
|---+---+---|
| `emtol` | 10.0 kJ mol^{-1} nm^{-1} | `gtol` in eV Å^{-1} |
| `emstep` | 0.01 nm | `istep` in Å |
| `nsteps` | -1 | no limit; otherwise `maxiter` |

The Rust stepper, C ABI, and C++ wrapper do no unit conversion.
C and C++ expose both `shrink` and `max_constraint_shrinks` through `rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_steep` / `Solver::set_gromacs_steep`.
`RGMIN_GROMACS_STEEP`, `RGMIN_STOP_MACHINE_PRECISION`, `rgmin_solver_set_gromacs_steep`, and `rgmin_gromacs_steep_max_constraint_shrinks` belong to ABI minor 52.
`include/rgmin.h` names minor 69.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/reference/lammps-min-style.org`

# LAMMPS min_style rgmin

This page lists the `min_modify` keywords of the LAMMPS plugin in `lammps/`, the rgmin C ABI call behind each one, and the errors the plugin raises.
@@rst::doc:`../howto/lammps-migration`@@ shows how to build and load it.

```text
plugin load rgminplugin.so
min_style rgmin
min_modify keyword value ...
minimize etol ftol maxiter maxeval
```

`min_modify` applies to the current minimizer, so it comes after `min_style rgmin`.
A new `min_style` command starts again from the defaults.

## Keywords of the plugin

| keyword | values | default | C ABI |
|---+---+---+---|
| `method` | `lbfgs`, `fire`, `fire2`, `sd`, `bb` | `lbfgs` | `rgmin_method_from_name`, `rgmin_solver_create` |
| `memory` | integer, at least 1 | 10 | `rgmin_control_t.memory` |
| `trust` | radius, at least 0 (distance units) | 0, off | `rgmin_solver_set_lbfgs_trust` |
| `linesearch` | `none`, `wolfe` | `none` | `rgmin_solver_set_lbfgs_wolfe` |
| `accept` | `default`, `energy`, `none`, `nonmonotone` | `default` | `rgmin_solver_set_accept` |
| `istep` | step scale, at least 0 | 0 | `rgmin_control_t.istep` |

- `method` takes rgmin's method names, so `steepest` and `barzilai-borwein` are `sd` and `bb`.
  Any other rgmin method is an error.
- `memory` is the number of L-BFGS pairs.
  Other methods ignore it.
- `trust` is the Burdakov ray-truncation radius of L-BFGS, which replaces the per-atom cap and the acceptance test while it is on.
  It needs `method lbfgs` and excludes `linesearch wolfe`.
- `linesearch wolfe` needs `method lbfgs`.
  With a positive `dmax` it is rgmin's geometry L-BFGS step, whose trials the per-atom cap bounds; with `dmax 0` it is the strong Wolfe search of Nocedal and Wright, algorithms 3.5 and 3.6.
- `accept` is how a session takes a proposed step.
  `default` keeps the C ABI default, `energy`, which refuses a trial that raises the energy.
- `istep` is the FIRE time step of `fire` and `fire2`, 0.1 when it is 0.
  For `sd` and `bb`, 0 is the C ABI default: a unit step scale, with `min(1, 1/|g|)` on the first step.

## LAMMPS keywords the plugin reads

| keyword | default | use |
|---+---+---|
| `dmax` | 0.1 | `rgmin_solver_set_atom_maxmove`: the largest displacement of one atom in one step; 0 leaves the cap off |
| `norm` | `two` | `rgmin_solver_set_stop_norm`: `two` is `TWO`, `max` is `MAX_ATOM`, `inf` is `INF` |
| `abcfire` | `no` | `rgmin_solver_set_fire_abc` on a `fire2` session |

`method fire2` selects `RGMIN_FIRE_PRESET_GUENOLE2020`, the parameter set of the LAMMPS `min_style fire` defaults.
`delaystep`, `dtgrow`, `dtshrink`, `alpha0`, `alphashrink`, `tmax`, `tmin`, `integrator`, `halfstepback`, `initialdelay` and `vdfmax` must keep those defaults, and `line` must stay `quadratic`.
The `minimize` command checks them and stops with an error otherwise.

## Stopping rules

| LAMMPS | plugin |
|---+---|
| `etol` | `rgmin_solver_set_etol`: `abs(E_k - E_{k-1}) < etol (abs(E_k) + abs(E_{k-1}) + sqrt(DBL_EPSILON)) / 2` after an accepted step; `0` is off |
| `ftol` | `rgmin_report_t.grad_norm < ftol`, with `rgmin_control_t.gtol = ftol` and the stop norm of `norm` |
| `maxiter` | number of `rgmin_solver_step_fg` calls |
| `maxeval` | number of `Min::energy_force` calls the plugin made, checked after each step |

`E` is the total energy rgmin minimizes. The relative test is the same on the per-atom energy that LAMMPS prints, apart from the floor, which is `sqrt(DBL_EPSILON)` here and 1e-8 in LAMMPS.
The gradient rgmin sees is `-F` over all `3N` coordinates after every fix, so `grad_norm` is the force norm that `min_style cg` compares with `ftol`.
A failed rgmin step ends the minimization with the stopping criterion `rgmin step failed:` and the text of `rgmin_last_error`.

## Errors

| message contains | cause |
|---+---|
| `Unknown min_modify keyword X for min_style rgmin` | a keyword that neither LAMMPS nor the plugin defines |
| `Unknown rgmin method X` | a name `rgmin_method_from_name` refuses |
| `stores a dense 3N x 3N matrix` | `bfgs`, `sr1` or `sr2` |
| `needs a dense Hessian` | `newton`, `rfo` or `dogleg` |
| `is not available with min_style rgmin` | any other rgmin method |
| `does not support fixes that add global degrees of freedom such as fix box/relax` | `fix box/relax` or another fix with `min_dof` |
| `does not support pair styles that add per-atom degrees of freedom` | for example `pair_style eff/cut` |
| `requires consecutive atom IDs 1 to N` | gaps in the atom IDs |
| `does not take min_modify line` | `min_modify line` other than `quadratic` |
| `keeps the Guenole 2020 FIRE parameters` | a LAMMPS FIRE keyword changed from its default |
| `replicated rgmin sessions diverged across ranks` | ranks that reached different step energies |

Keywords with a bad value (`memory 0`, `linesearch armijo`, `accept maybe`) and settings that need another method (`trust` or `linesearch wolfe` without `lbfgs`, `abcfire yes` without `fire2`) also stop with an error that names them.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/reference/manifold.org`

# Riemannian manifolds

`RiemannianManifold` is a Stiefel manifold `St(n, p)`, a cone `SPD(p)` of symmetric positive definite matrices, the rigid quotient `R^{3N}/SE(3)` of `N` atoms, or a product of them.
Rust, C, C++ and Python call the same code.
@@rst::doc:`../tutorials/manifold-fit`@@ fits a point on `St x SPD` by gradient steps.

## Packing

Every buffer is caller-owned, column-major and `len` doubles long.

| Factor        | Point                                  | `len`   |
|---------------+----------------------------------------+---------|
| `St(n, p)`    | `n x p` frame, `U^T U = I`, `1 <= p <= n` | `n p`   |
| `SPD(p)`      | `p x p` symmetric positive definite    | `p^2`   |
| Rigid quotient | `3 N` Cartesians `x0, y0, z0, x1, ...`, `N >= 1` | `3 N`   |
| Product       | factor blocks in factor order          | the sum |

Tangent vectors and Euclidean gradients use the packing of the point.
A nested product contributes its factors.

## Operations

| Operation        | Stiefel (embedded metric)                         | SPD affine-invariant                       | SPD log-Euclidean                         | Rigid quotient (Euclidean metric)                    |
|------------------+---------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------|
| `project`        | `V - X sym(X^T V)`                                | `sym(V)`                                   | `sym(V)`                                  | remove translations and rotations (rotations kept when periodic) |
| `egrad_to_rgrad` | the projection                                    | `X sym(G) X`                               | `Dlog(X)^{-2}[sym(G)]`                    | the projection                                       |
| `retract`        | QR (first order) or polar (second order) of `X + V` | `exp`                                      | `exp`                                     | `X + V`                                              |
| `exp`            | Edelman, Arias, Smith (1998) eq. 2.41             | `X^{1/2} expm(X^{-1/2} V X^{-1/2}) X^{1/2}` | `expm(log X + Dlog(X)[V])`                | `X + P_X V`                                          |
| `log`            | refused                                           | inverse of `exp`                           | inverse of `exp`                          | refused                                              |
| `transport`      | projection at the arrival point                   | `E V E^T`, `E = (Y X^{-1})^{1/2}`          | `Dlog(Y)^{-1}[Dlog(X)[V]]`                | projection at the arrival point                      |
| `inner`          | `tr(U^T V)`                                       | `tr(X^{-1} U X^{-1} V)`                    | `<Dlog(X)[U], Dlog(X)[V]>`                | `U . V`                                              |

`sym(A) = (A + A^T) / 2`.
`Dlog(X)` is applied in the eigenbasis of `X` with the divided differences of `log` on its eigenvalues (Daleckii-Krein).
`exp` projects `v` to the tangent space first.
The product metric is the sum of the factor metrics.
`P_X` is the horizontal projector at `X`.
`gradient_step(x, egrad, t)` returns `rgrad = egrad_to_rgrad(x, egrad)` and `retract(x, -t rgrad)`.

The affine-invariant metric is Pennec, Fillard and Ayache ([2006](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11263-005-3222-z)).
The log-Euclidean metric is Arsigny, Fillard, Pennec and Ayache ([2007](https://doi.org/10.1137/050637996)).
The Stiefel geodesic is Edelman, Arias and Smith ([1998](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0895479895290954)).

## The rigid quotient and its strata

For an isolated cluster, the factor is a manifold on the regular stratum, `N >= 3` atoms that are not collinear.
The horizontal space has dimension `3N - 6` and the projector has rank 6.
The projector is built from a rank-revealing factorization of the six rigid motions, with every column scaled to unit size, so the rank does not depend on the size of the cluster.

At a singular isolated configuration the quotient is not a manifold.
One atom, or atoms that all coincide, have rank 3: the three rotations move nothing.
Collinear atoms have rank 5: the rotation about the line moves nothing.
The horizontal space is then larger than `3N - 6`, and its dimension changes with the configuration.
The projection stays valid there and removes exactly the motions that move the atoms.
The retraction `X + V` and the transport are well defined, but a step that bends a collinear cluster changes the dimension of the tangent space, so a method that keeps a subspace across the step gets no guarantee from the transport.
Treat a singular configuration as the boundary of the manifold.

When `periodic` is true, the factor quotients translations only.
The translation action is free for every nonempty configuration, so the periodic quotient has dimension `3N - 3`, projector rank 3, and no rotational singular strata.

## Refusals

A wrong length, a non-finite entry, an SPD point that is not symmetric positive definite, a rank-deficient `X + V` under a Stiefel retraction, a non-finite step size, and `log` on a Stiefel or rigid-quotient factor are refused.
A rigid-quotient factor with no atoms is refused too.
Rust returns `Error::ManifoldArgument`, C returns `RGMIN_INVALID_PARAMETER` with `rgmin_last_error`, C++ throws `std::runtime_error`, and Python raises `ValueError`.
C writes the outputs only on success, so an output may alias an input.

## Rust

```rust
use rgmin::{RiemannianManifold, SpdMetric, StiefelRetraction};

let m = RiemannianManifold::product([
    RiemannianManifold::stiefel(6, 2, StiefelRetraction::Polar)?,
    RiemannianManifold::spd(3, SpdMetric::AffineInvariant)?,
    RiemannianManifold::rigid_quotient(5, false)?,
])?;
m.gradient_step(&x, &egrad, 0.1, &mut rgrad, &mut x_next)?;
```

`RiemannianManifold` implements the `Manifold` trait, so generic code such as `rtr::truncated_cg` accepts it.
`Solver` selects its manifold with the closed `ManifoldKind` and does not take this type.

## C

`rgmin_manifold_t` is the session token of `rgmin_solver_set_manifold`.
The handle here is `rgmin_manifold_handle_t`. ABI minor 41.

| Function                         | Shapes and effect                                              |
|----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `rgmin_manifold_stiefel(n, p, r)` | `r` is `RGMIN_STIEFEL_QR` or `RGMIN_STIEFEL_POLAR`. Null on a bad shape. |
| `rgmin_manifold_spd(p, metric)`  | `RGMIN_SPD_AFFINE_INVARIANT` or `RGMIN_SPD_LOG_EUCLIDEAN`.     |
| `rgmin_manifold_rigid_quotient(n, periodic)` | `R^{3N}/SE(3)`, or `R^{3N}/T(3)` when `periodic` is nonzero. Packed length `3 n`. ABI minor 56. |
| `rgmin_manifold_product(fs, k)`  | Copies `k` factors; the caller still frees them.               |
| `rgmin_manifold_free(m)`         | Null is a no-op.                                               |
| `rgmin_manifold_len(m)`          | Packed length. Zero for null.                                  |
| `rgmin_manifold_project`         | `(m, x, v, out, len)`                                          |
| `rgmin_manifold_egrad_to_rgrad`  | `(m, x, egrad, out, len)`                                      |
| `rgmin_manifold_retract`         | `(m, x, v, out, len)`                                          |
| `rgmin_manifold_exp` / `_log`    | `(m, x, v or y, out, len)`                                     |
| `rgmin_manifold_transport`       | `(m, x_from, x_to, v, out, len)`                               |
| `rgmin_manifold_inner`           | `(m, x, u, v, &value, len)`                                    |
| `rgmin_manifold_gradient_step`   | `(m, x, egrad, t, rgrad_out, x_out, len)`                      |

## C++

`rgmin::Manifold` owns the handle: `Manifold::stiefel(n, p, r)`, `Manifold::spd(p, metric)`, `Manifold::rigid_quotient(n_atoms, periodic)` and `Manifold::product(a, b, ...)`.
The members take buffers of `len()` doubles. `xts::optimize::Manifold` is the same class.

## Python

`rgmin.Stiefel(n, p, retraction="qr")`, `rgmin.SPD(p, metric="affine_invariant")`, `rgmin.RigidQuotient(n_atoms, periodic=False)` and `rgmin.Product(*factors)` take and return NumPy arrays.
A Stiefel point is an `(n, p)` array, an SPD point a `(p, p)` array, a rigid-quotient point a `(3 n_atoms, 1)` column of Cartesians (`x.reshape(-1, 3)` gives one atom per row), and a product point a tuple with one array per factor.
Each class has `project`, `egrad_to_rgrad`, `retract`, `exp`, `log`, `transport`, `inner`, `norm` and `gradient_step`, which returns `(rgrad, x_next)`.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/reference/periodic.org`

# Periodic block determinants

`rgmin::periodic` computes \(\ln|\det A|\) of a bordered cyclic block matrix, and factors it so that linear systems with \(A\) can be solved afterwards.
The matrix is what multiple shooting builds for a periodic orbit \(x_{k+1} ` T_k x_k\), \(k ` 0, \dots, b-1\), whose monodromy is \(M = T_{b-1} \cdots T_0\).
The determinant \(\det(I - M)\) equals the determinant of the cyclic block matrix without ever forming \(M\), so the product of the period never overflows or drops the decaying multipliers.

## The matrix

Row block \(i\) holds \(-T_i\) in block column \(i\) and the identity in block column \((i + 1) \bmod b\).
With \(b = 1\) the two coincide and the matrix is \(I - T_0\).
Each \(T_i\) is a row-major \(m \times m\) block.

An optional border of \(p\) columns and \(p\) rows turns the singular matrix of a periodic orbit into a regular one.
Column \(s\) of the border has \(m\) entries in the rows of block \(b - 1\), and row \(s\) of the border has \(m\) entries in the columns of block 0.
The trailing \(p \times p\) block is zero.
The order of the bordered matrix is \(b m + p\).

## Factoring

```rust
use rgmin::periodic::bordered_cyclic_log_abs;

// Free particle: T = [[1, h], [0, 1]] has the Jordan block at the
// multiplier one. Bordering the velocity row and the position column
// leaves |det| equal to the period.
let beta = 7.0;
let b = 4;
let h = beta / b as f64;
let transfers: Vec<Vec<f64>> = (0..b).map(|_| vec![1.0, h, 0.0, 1.0]).collect();
let column = [vec![0.0, 1.0]];
let row = [vec![1.0, 0.0]];

let factor = bordered_cyclic_log_abs(&transfers, 2, &column, &row)?;
assert!((factor.log_abs - beta.ln()).abs() < 1e-12);
let x = factor.solve(&vec![1.0; factor.order()])?;
```

`bordered_cyclic_log_abs(transfers, m, column_border, row_border)` takes one slice of `m * m` entries per block and two lists of `p` border vectors of length `m`.
It returns a `CyclicFactor` with these public items:

- `log_abs`, the natural logarithm of the absolute value of \(\det A\);
- `norm1`, the 1-norm of \(A\), its largest column sum of absolute values;
- `inverse_norm1`, the Hager-Higham estimate of the 1-norm of \(A^{-1}\), usually within a factor of three;
- `order()`, \(b m + p\);
- `solve(y)`, the vector \(x\) with \(A x = y\);
- `solve_transpose(w)`, the vector \(z\) with \(A^T z = w\).

The product `norm1 * inverse_norm1` is a 1-norm condition estimate of \(A\).
Both solves reuse the stored factors and form no new factorization.

## Method

Block column \(0, 1, \dots, b - 1\) is eliminated in turn with Householder reflectors on the block rows it couples.
Each new block row is stacked above the running one, and the fill stays in block column \(b - 1\) and in the border.
Every transformation is orthogonal, so no intermediate entry grows, and the total work is \(O(b m^3)\) instead of the \(O((b m)^3)\) of a dense factorization.

Rows and columns are first scaled by powers of two so that each has unit largest entry.
Householder QR is backward stable column by column only, and shooting blocks mix positions and momenta whose rows differ by many decades.
The scaling is exact and is undone in `log_abs` and in both solves.

For one block the scaled matrix is formed from the entries of \(I - T_0\) directly, not from \(T_0\) and the identity scaled apart.
A unit diagonal entry of \(T_0\) makes the matrix entry exactly zero, and scaling the two terms separately by large powers of two would overflow both and leave \(\infty - \infty\).

## Errors

`CyclicError` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and has four variants:

| Variant                    | Raised when                                                                                                                                  |
|----------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Shape(why)`               | there are no blocks, `m` is zero, `p` exceeds `m`, a block is not `m * m`, a border vector is not length `m`, the border lists differ in length, a dimension overflows, or a right-hand side has the wrong length |
| `NonFinite`                | an input entry is NaN or infinite, or a triangular diagonal produced by the factorization is not finite                                      |
| `NonFiniteNormEstimate`    | the 1-norm of the matrix or the estimate of the 1-norm of its inverse overflows or becomes NaN                                               |
| `Singular`                 | a triangular diagonal entry is exactly zero                                                                                                  |

A singular matrix is an expected outcome: the identity transfers of the unbordered periodic problem, for example, have \(\det(I - M) = 0\) and are reported as `Singular`.
A matrix that is finite and nonsingular but whose inverse has entries beyond the range of `f64` is reported as `NonFiniteNormEstimate`, not as `Singular`: for one block \(T_0 ` [[1, \epsilon], [\epsilon, 2]]\) the inverse of \(I - T_0\) is of order \(\epsilon^{-2}\), so ~epsilon ` 1e-150` factors and `epsilon ` 1e-160~ and ~epsilon ` 1e-200` return `NonFiniteNormEstimate~.
No error is turned into a default value.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/reference/product-manifold.org`

# Product manifold

The weighted Riemannian product \(\mathcal{M}_1 \times \cdots \times \mathcal{M}_k\) with metric \(g = \sum_i w_i\, g_i\), the sphere of a subspace, tangent metrics on product factors, and the trust-region and session drivers that run on them.
@@rst::doc:`../explanation/product-manifold`@@ derives every operation listed here.

## Construction

`rgmin::manifold::ProductFactor` is one factor.
It is `#[non_exhaustive]` with public fields:
- `kind: ManifoldKind`, the geometry;
- `len: usize`, the packed length of a factor point;
- `weight: f64`, the weight \(w_i\) of the factor metric.
`ProductFactor::default()` is a Euclidean factor of length 1 and weight 1.
`ProductFactor::new(kind, len)` has weight 1, and `with_kind`, `with_len` and `with_weight` set one field each.
`with_metric(Arc<dyn TangentMetric>)` attaches a tangent metric and `metric()` returns it as `Option<&Arc<dyn TangentMetric>>`; two factors compare equal only when they share the same metric object.

`ProductManifold::new(factors)` builds the product of an iterator of `ProductFactor` in packing order.
A factor whose kind is itself a product is flattened into its blocks, and their weights are multiplied by the factor's weight; the blocks keep their tangent metrics.
It fails with `Error::ProductFactor { index, what }`, where `what` is one of:
- `"weight must be finite and positive"`;
- `"packed length must be positive"`;
- `"packed length does not fit the kind"`, from `Manifold::required_dim` of the kind;
- `"a nested product takes tangent metrics on its factors"`, for a tangent metric on a factor whose kind is a product;
- `"packed length overflows"`;
- `"a product needs at least one factor"`, with index 0.

`ProductManifold::power(kind, block, count)` is manopt's `powermanifold`: `count` unit-weight copies of `kind`, each of packed length `block`.
`count = 0` fails with `"a power needs at least one copy"`.

`ManifoldKind::product(factors)` and `ManifoldKind::power(factor, block, count)` wrap the two constructors in `ManifoldKind::Product(Arc<ProductManifold>)`, whose `as_str` is `"product"`.
`Oblique` stays the dedicated kind for a power of spheres.

## Accessors

| Method                 | Returns                                                                       |
|------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `packed_len()`         | packed length of a point                                                      |
| `factor_count()`       | number of factors after flattening                                            |
| `factors()`            | the flattened factors, with their weights in the metric and their tangent metrics |
| `tangent_metric_factor()` | `Some` index of the first factor with a tangent metric                     |
| `range(index)`         | `Some` slice of the packed vector holding factor `index`, `None` past the end |
| `is_flat()`            | every factor keeps a straight step on its set                                 |
| `is_chart()`           | every factor has weight one in these coordinates, so `chart` is the identity  |
| `chart_scales()`       | \(d\) of \(z = d \odot x\): \(\sqrt{w_i}\) on factor \(i\) of a product from `new`, 1 on a chart |
| `chart()`              | the same manifold in the coordinates \(z = d \odot x\), all weights one       |

## Packing

A point packs the factor points end to end in the order given, each in its kind's own packing (@@rst::doc:`../howto/manifolds`@@).
A tangent vector and a Euclidean gradient pack the same way.
The hyperplane \(\mathbb{R}^n \times S^{n-1}\) is `[p_1, ..., p_n, n_1, ..., n_n]`:

```rust
use rgmin::manifold::ProductFactor;
use rgmin::ManifoldKind;

let n = 4;
let hyperplane = ManifoldKind::product([
    ProductFactor::new(ManifoldKind::Euclidean, n).with_weight(0.3),
    ProductFactor::new(ManifoldKind::Sphere, n),
])?;
```

## Operations

| `Manifold` method                   | On the product                                                                        |
|-------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `required_dim`                      | the packed length, exactly                                                            |
| `project`                           | each factor's projection; no weights                                                  |
| `egrad2rgrad`                       | each factor's `egrad2rgrad` of its block, then \(G^{-1}\), divided by \(w_i\)         |
| `retract`                           | each factor's retraction                                                              |
| `transport`                         | each factor's transport                                                               |
| `inner`                             | \(\sum_i w_i\, g_i(u_i, G v_i)\)                                                      |
| `norm`                              | the square root of `inner`                                                            |
| `ehess2rhess`                       | each factor's `ehess2rhess` of its block of the full action, then \(G^{-1}\), divided by \(w_i\) |
| `exp`, `log`                        | each factor's                                                                         |
| `dist`                              | \((\sum_i w_i\, d_i^2)^{1/2}\)                                                        |
| `parallel_transport_along`          | each factor's, along \(t \mapsto \exp_x(t d)\)                                        |
| `parallel_transport`                | each factor's, along the geodesic of `log`                                            |
| `transport_is_isometric`            | true when it is for every factor and no factor has a tangent metric                   |
| `typical_dist`                      | \((\sum_i w_i\, t_i^2)^{1/2}\) over the factor typical distances \(t_i\)              |

\(G\) is the factor's tangent metric, the identity when it has none.
The optional operations, `ehess2rhess`, `exp`, `log`, `dist` and both parallel transports, return `None` as soon as one factor returns `None`; all but `ehess2rhess` also return `None` when a factor has a tangent metric.
Arrays of the wrong length leave the input unchanged: `project`, `egrad2rgrad` and `transport` return the vector, `retract` returns the point, `inner` and `norm` return NaN, and the optional operations return `None`.

## Factor capabilities

| Kind                                                        | `ehess2rhess` | `exp` | `log`, `dist`, parallel transport | isometric `transport` | typical distance                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------------+---------------+-------+-----------------------------------+-----------------------+-----------------------------------|
| `Euclidean`                                                 | yes           | yes   | yes                               | yes                   | \(\sqrt{n}\)                      |
| `Sphere`, `Stiefel`                                         | yes           | yes   | yes                               | no                    | \(\pi\)                           |
| `SubspaceSphere`                                            | yes           | yes   | yes                               | no                    | \(\pi\)                           |
| `StiefelP { n, p }`                                         | yes           | no    | no                                | no                    | \(\sqrt{p}\)                      |
| `So3`                                                       | yes           | yes   | yes                               | no                    | \(\pi \sqrt{3}\)                  |
| `Se3`                                                       | yes           | yes   | yes                               | no                    | \((3 \pi^2 + 3)^{1/2}\)           |
| `Oblique { n, m }`                                          | yes           | yes   | yes                               | no                    | \(\pi \sqrt{m}\)                  |
| `ComplexCircle { n }`                                       | yes           | yes   | yes                               | no                    | \(\pi \sqrt{n}\)                  |
| `SphereComplex { n }`                                       | yes           | yes   | yes                               | no                    | \(\pi\)                           |
| `Positive { n }`                                            | yes           | yes   | yes                               | no                    | \(\sqrt{n}\)                      |
| `Symmetric`, `SkewSymmetric`                                | yes           | yes   | yes                               | yes                   | \(\sqrt{\mathrm{len}}\)           |
| `CenteredMatrix { m, n, rows }`                             | yes           | yes   | yes                               | yes                   | \(\sqrt{\dim}\)                   |
| `EuclideanComplex { n }`                                    | yes           | yes   | yes                               | yes                   | \(\sqrt{n}\)                      |
| `Constant { n }`                                            | yes           | yes   | yes                               | yes                   | 0                                 |
| `Spd`                                                       | yes           | no    | no                                | no                    | \(\sqrt{\mathrm{len}}\)           |
| `Multinomial`                                               | no            | no    | no                                | no                    | \(\sqrt{\mathrm{len}}\)           |
| `MultinomialDoublyStochastic`, `MultinomialSymmetric`       | no            | no    | no                                | no                    | \(\sqrt{\mathrm{len}}\)           |
| `MwRigid`, `RigidQuotient`                                  | no            | no    | no                                | no                    | \(\sqrt{\mathrm{len}}\)           |

\(\mathrm{len}\) is the packed length and \(\dim\) the dimension of the centered matrices, \(m n - n\) for centered rows and \(m n - m\) for centered columns.
`Positive`, `Spd` and the doubly stochastic kinds carry their own metric through `inner` and `egrad2rgrad`; every other kind uses the dot product of its packed coordinates.
`Multinomial` pairs a Fisher-orthogonal projection with the dot product, so its gradient does not represent the differential in its inner product.

## Subspace sphere

`rgmin::manifold::SubspaceSphere` is the unit sphere \(S(U) ` \{x \in U : \|x\| ` 1\}\) of a linear subspace \(U \subset \mathbb{R}^n\), in the ambient Euclidean metric.
- `SubspaceSphere::within(basis: Array2<f64>) -> Result<Self>` takes \(U\) as the span of the rows of `basis`, each of length \(n\).
- `SubspaceSphere::excluding(basis: Array2<f64>) -> Result<Self>` takes \(U\) as the orthogonal complement of that span; no row gives the whole sphere \(S^{n-1}\).
`ManifoldKind::sphere_within(basis)` and `ManifoldKind::sphere_excluding(basis)` wrap them in `ManifoldKind::SubspaceSphere(Arc<SubspaceSphere>)`, whose `as_str` is `"subspace_sphere"`.
The rows are orthonormalized by modified Gram–Schmidt with a second pass.
Both constructors fail with `Error::SubspaceBasis { what }`, where `what` is one of:
- `"the ambient dimension must be positive"`;
- `"a basis entry is not finite"`;
- `"the basis rows are linearly dependent"`, when the part of a row outside the span of the earlier rows is at most \(\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) of its length;
- `"the subspace needs at least one direction"`, from `within` with no row;
- `"the excluded directions leave no subspace"`, from `excluding` with \(n\) independent rows.

| Method                 | Returns                                                                       |
|------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ambient_dim()`        | \(n\), the packed length of a point                                           |
| `subspace_dim()`       | \(\dim U\); the sphere has dimension one less                                 |
| `basis()`              | the orthonormal rows, spanning \(U\), or \(U^\perp\) when `excludes()`        |
| `excludes()`           | `true` for a sphere from `excluding`                                          |
| `project_subspace(v)`  | \(P_U v\); a vector of another length comes back unchanged                    |
| `closest_point(x)`     | \(P_U x / \Vert P_U x \Vert\); `None` for another length or no component in \(U\) |

As a `Manifold`, `project` is \(P_U - x x^\top\), `retract` is \(P_U(x + v) / \Vert P_U(x + v) \Vert\), `transport` is projection at the arrival point and `ehess2rhess` is \((P_U - x x^\top)(\nabla^2 \bar f\, v - (x^\top \nabla \bar f)\, v)\).
The exponential, logarithm, distance and both parallel transports are the sphere's.

## Tangent metrics

```rust
pub trait TangentMetric: Send + Sync {
    fn apply(&self, x: &Array1<f64>, v: &Array1<f64>) -> Array1<f64>;
    fn solve(&self, x: &Array1<f64>, r: &Array1<f64>) -> Array1<f64>;
}
```

`rgmin::manifold::TangentMetric` is an operator \(G_x\) on the tangent spaces of one factor, attached with `ProductFactor::with_metric`.
The factor's term of the product metric becomes \(w_i\, g_i(u, G_x v)\).
`apply` returns \(G_x v\) and `solve` returns \(G_x^{-1} r\), for the factor point `x` and tangent vectors in the factor's own packing.
At every `x`, \(G_x\) must map the tangent space into itself and be self-adjoint and positive definite in \(g_i\), and `solve` must invert `apply`; the product projects both results onto the tangent space.
With a tangent metric the gradient is \(w_i^{-1} G_x^{-1} \mathrm{grad}_i f\), and `ehess2rhess` returns the model \(w_i^{-1} G_x^{-1} \mathrm{Hess}_i f\), which is self-adjoint in the metric and exact at critical points.
`chart` keeps tangent metrics unchanged.

## Sphere Hessians

`ehess2rhess` of `Sphere`, `SubspaceSphere` and the other embedded kinds that supply it keeps the Weingarten term explicit; on the sphere it is \((I - x x^\top) \nabla^2 \bar f\, v - (x^\top \nabla \bar f)\, v\).
`egrad` and `ehess` may come from any smooth extension \(\bar f\) of the cost, and the result does not depend on the choice.
The session's dogleg, Newton-CG and Newton-PCG steps model the Hessian of a curved kind without the term, which is exact for the degree-zero extension \(\bar f(x) = f(x / \Vert x \Vert)\) and converges linearly for others; `minimize_rtr` keeps the term.

## Sessions

`Solver::set_product(factors) -> Result<()>` selects a weighted product; on `Error::ProductFactor` the session keeps its manifold.
`Solver::set_power(factor, block, count) -> bool` selects a power, and returns `false`, keeping the manifold, when `factor` cannot hold `block` or `count` is 0.
`Solver::set_manifold` accepts a `ManifoldKind::Product` directly.
A change of manifold clears the session's history.
The session dimension must equal the packed length.

A product whose weights are not all one is stored as its chart.
The caller's points, gradients, Hessians and reports stay in natural coordinates, and the reported gradient norm is the length in the product metric.
A step on such a product fails with `Error::ProductChart { what }` while one of these settings is active:
- the exponential preconditioner;
- the Lindh model Hessian;
- rigid-motion projection of the whole vector (`set_project_rigid`);
- with the `highs` feature, the HiGHS box and equalities.

`MwRigid` and `RigidQuotient` factors are projected block by block with the session's periodic flag.
`Solver::set_masses` is read by the `MwRigid` blocks as one molecule reused on every block when its length is the atom count of one block, or as every block's masses in order when its length is the atom count of all `MwRigid` blocks; any other length means unit masses.

A step on a product with a tangent metric fails with `Error::ProductTangentMetric { index }`, `index` being the first such factor after flattening; `search_direction` fails the same way and `push_pair` returns `false`.

```rust
pub fn run_gauged<O, G>(&mut self, obj: &O, x: &mut Array1<f64>, gauge: G) -> Result<Report>
where
    O: DifferentiableObjective<f64> + ?Sized,
    G: FnMut(&mut Array1<f64>);
```

`Solver::run_gauged` is `run` with `gauge(x)` called before every step but the first, to replace the iterate with another representation of the same point.
A call that changes `x` rebases the session as `Solver::rebase`: the curvature memory stays, and the next step evaluates the objective afresh instead of reading the move as a step.
The returned report describes the point left in `x`.

## Trust region

```rust
pub fn minimize_rtr<M, FV, GG, HH>(
    manifold: &M,
    x0: Array1<f64>,
    value: FV,
    egrad: GG,
    ehess: HH,
    opts: RtrOptions,
) -> RtrMin
where
    M: Manifold + ?Sized,
    FV: FnMut(&Array1<f64>) -> f64,
    GG: FnMut(&Array1<f64>) -> Array1<f64>,
    HH: FnMut(&Array1<f64>, &Array1<f64>) -> Array1<f64>;
```

`rgmin::rtr::minimize_rtr` is the Absil-Baker-Gallivan trust region with truncated conjugate gradients, run in the metric of `manifold`.
`egrad(x)` is the Euclidean gradient and `ehess(x, v)` the Euclidean Hessian action, both in packed coordinates.
The Hessian is `ehess2rhess`, or `egrad2rgrad` of the action when that returns `None`.

`RtrOptions` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, and its defaults are those of manopt `trustregions`:

| Field                | Default  | Setter                    | Meaning                                                                       |
|----------------------+----------+---------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `radius_max`         | `None`   | `with_radius_max`         | \(\bar\Delta\); `None` takes `Manifold::typical_dist`, and \(\Delta_0 = \bar\Delta / 8\) |
| `grad_tol`           | `1e-6`   | `with_grad_tol`           | stop when the Riemannian gradient is at most this long                        |
| `max_iter`           | `1000`   | `with_max_iter`           | outer iterations                                                              |
| `cg_max`             | `None`   | `with_cg_max`             | inner iterations; `None` takes the packed length                              |
| `theta`              | `1.0`    | `with_theta`              | \(\theta\) of the inner rule \(\Vert r_j \Vert \le \Vert r_0 \Vert \min(\Vert r_0 \Vert^\theta, \kappa)\) |
| `kappa`              | `0.1`    | `with_kappa`              | \(\kappa\) of the inner rule                                                  |
| `rho_regularization` | `1e3`    | `with_rho_regularization` | both decreases gain \(\max(1, \lvert f \rvert)\, \varepsilon\) times this     |

A step is accepted when \(\rho > 0.1\); the radius is quartered below \(\rho ` 1/4\) and doubled, up to \(\bar\Delta\), above \(\rho ` 3/4\) on the boundary.
A non-finite or non-positive \(\bar\Delta\) is replaced by 1.
`RtrMin` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and holds `x`, `value`, `grad_norm` (in the manifold metric), `iterations`, `accepted` and `inner_iterations`, the conjugate-gradient iterations over all subproblems.

```rust
pub fn minimize_rtr_gauged<M, FV, GG, HH, GA>(
    manifold: &M,
    x0: Array1<f64>,
    value: FV,
    egrad: GG,
    ehess: HH,
    gauge: GA,
    opts: RtrOptions,
) -> RtrMin
where
    M: Manifold + ?Sized,
    FV: FnMut(&Array1<f64>) -> f64,
    GG: FnMut(&Array1<f64>) -> Array1<f64>,
    HH: FnMut(&Array1<f64>, &Array1<f64>) -> Array1<f64>,
    GA: FnMut(&mut Array1<f64>);
```

`rgmin::rtr::minimize_rtr_gauged` is `minimize_rtr` with `gauge(x)` called after every accepted step, to replace the iterate with another representation of the same point.
The step is accepted on the value before the call.
The value is evaluated again when the call changed `x`, and the gradient always is, so the next model, the stopping test and the returned `RtrMin` belong to the moved point.

```rust
pub fn truncated_cg_riemannian<M, H>(
    manifold: &M,
    x: &Array1<f64>,
    egrad: &Array1<f64>,
    ehess: H,
    radius: f64,
    opts: &RtrOptions,
) -> TcgResult
where
    M: Manifold + ?Sized,
    H: FnMut(&Array1<f64>) -> Array1<f64>;
```

`rgmin::rtr::truncated_cg_riemannian` solves one subproblem of `minimize_rtr` at `x` with the trust radius `radius`, using `theta`, `kappa` and `cg_max` from `opts`; on a product with a tangent metric it is the preconditioned subproblem.
`TcgResult` holds the step `eta`, the model decrease `model_decrease`, the stopping reason `stop` and the conjugate-gradient `iterations`.
A driver that measures the decrease itself retracts `eta` and passes the measured and model decreases with `manifold.norm(x, &eta)` to `RtrRadius::update(actual_decrease, model_decrease, eta_norm) -> bool`, which applies the acceptance and radius rule above and returns whether the step is accepted.
`RtrRadius::new(radius_max)` starts at a radius of `radius_max / 8`.

## C ABI

```c
int32_t rgmin_solver_set_power(rgmin_solver_t *solver, int32_t factor, size_t block,
                               size_t count);
```

ABI minor 41.
`factor` is an `rgmin_manifold_t` value for a kind without shape parameters: `RGMIN_MANIFOLD_EUCLIDEAN`, `SPHERE`, `SO3`, `STIEFEL`, `SE3`, `RIGID_QUOTIENT`, `MW_RIGID`, `MULTINOMIAL`, `SYMMETRIC` or `SKEWSYMMETRIC`.
It returns 0, or 1 with the manifold unchanged and `rgmin_last_error` set to:
- `rgmin_solver_set_power: null solver`;
- `rgmin_solver_set_power: the factor token needs a shape`, for a token with shape parameters or a value outside `rgmin_manifold_t`;
- `rgmin_solver_set_power: the block does not fit the factor`, for a block the factor cannot hold or a count of 0.
`MW_RIGID` copies read `rgmin_solver_set_masses` as described under Sessions.
The C++ wrapper is `rgmin::Solver::set_power(rgmin_manifold_t factor, std::size_t block, std::size_t count)`, and `xts.h` aliases it as `xts_solver_set_power`.
Weighted products of arbitrary factors, subspace spheres, tangent metrics and gauges are not exposed to C or Python; @@rst::doc:`../explanation/product-manifold`@@ gives the reasons.

Source: `docs/orgmode/reference/proofs.org`

The Lean development under `proofs/lean/Rgmin/` pins the exact
rational facts the solvers' termination and honesty arguments rest
on. It builds on Mathlib, so the statements are the real ones: widths
and radii over the reals, `Real.sqrt` in the boundary root rather
than a named-root hypothesis, actual limits for the termination
envelopes, and the Gram positive-semidefiniteness of the sketch as a
matrix theorem. Check it with `lake exe cache get && lake build` in
`proofs/lean/`; the cache makes Mathlib a download, not a compile.

The division of labor is deliberate. The Lean side proves the exact
algebra and the budget envelopes -- facts about the formulas, true in
every execution. The Rust tests hold the floating-point
implementation to those facts at concrete tolerances. A claim without
a row in both columns is an opinion.

| Theorem (Rgmin.*)                  | Pins                                              | Code                          | Rust test                                          |
|------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------+-------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------|
| `guarded_above`, `guarded_below`   | zoom trials land in the interior band             | `linesearch/zoom.rs`          | `the_cubic_zoom_keeps_the_evaluation_budget`       |
| `zoom_shrinks`                     | bracket loses >= 10 percent per step              | `linesearch/zoom.rs`          | (same)                                             |
| `width_envelope`, `_tendsto`       | geometric width envelope, and it reaches zero     | `linesearch/zoom.rs`          | (same)                                             |
| `armijo_strict`                    | an accepted point strictly improves               | `linesearch/conditions.rs`    | `armijo_and_curvature_match_xtsci`                 |
| `boundary_on_sphere`               | the boundary root lands on the trust sphere       | `hvp.rs::boundary_tau`        | `negative_curvature_walks_to_the_trust_boundary`   |
| `boundary_tau_nonneg`              | a boundary exit never retracts                    | `hvp.rs::boundary_tau`        | (same)                                             |
| `ray_further_is_lower`             | negative curvature: boundary is optimal greed     | `hvp.rs::steihaug_pcg`        | (same)                                             |
| `step_scale_invariant`             | CG step ignores preconditioner scale              | `hvp.rs::steihaug_pcg`        | `nystrom_flattens_a_decaying_spectrum`             |
| `beta_scale_invariant`             | conjugacy weight ignores preconditioner scale     | `hvp.rs::steihaug_pcg`        | `the_preconditioned_boundary_lives_in_the_sketch_metric` |
| `metric_update_scales`             | tracked M-norm recurrence is scale-consistent     | `hvp.rs::steihaug_pcg`        | (same)                                             |
| `shrink_ge_floor`, `shrink_pos`    | the trust radius stays positive                   | `trust.rs::update_radius`     | `hvp.rs` suite                                     |
| `shrink_strict`, `collapse_envelope`, `collapse_tendsto` | rejections decay the radius to any floor | `hvp.rs::minimize_newton_cg`  | `TrustCollapsed` paths                             |
| `grow_le_cap`, `grow_ge`           | growth is capped and never loses ground           | `trust.rs::update_radius`     | `dogleg_stays_on_the_trust_sphere`                 |
| `rejection_propagates`             | an uphill step cannot be accepted                 | `trust.rs::reduction_ratio`   | `an_uphill_everywhere_oracle_is_refused_not_moved` |
| `sketch_posSemidef`, `sketch_form_nonneg`, `sumSq_nonneg` | the Gram sketch is PSD, as a matrix theorem | `hvp.rs::NystromPrecond`      | `nystrom_flattens_a_decaying_spectrum`             |
| `shifted_weight_pos`, `equalized_weight_bounds` | the solve's weights are positive, damping only | `hvp.rs::NystromPrecond::solve` | (same)                                        |

# Module `rgmin`

`Method` is an `enum.IntEnum` of the C method ids. Members are
UPPER_SNAKE, for example `LBFGS` and `POLAK_RIBIERE`. The older
CamelCase spellings are aliases of the same values.
`Stop` is why a step ended. Its members are `TOLERANCE`,
`NOISE_FLOOR`, `STEP_TOLERANCE`, `BUDGET`, `LINE_SEARCH`,
`POLISH_UNMET`, `ENERGY_TOLERANCE`, `EVAL_BUDGET`,
`MACHINE_PRECISION`, and `LINE_SEARCH_ROUNDING`, again with CamelCase
aliases.
`Report` has `value`, `steps`, `grad_norm`, and `stop`.
`Report.converged` is true when `stop` is `TOLERANCE`.
`backward_error_floor(value, x)` is the first-order stationarity
floor `n * eps * (1 + |value| + sum |x_i|)`.
`NumericalError` is an `ArithmeticError`.
`NotConverged` is a `RuntimeError` with a `report` attribute holding
the terminal `Report`.
`SolverConfig(method`"lbfgs", **options)= validates options.
`Solver(n, config)` is the session. `step(f_and_grad, x)` takes one
iteration. `step_hess(f_and_grad, hessian, x)` is the same for Newton,
RFO, and dogleg.
`minimize(f_and_grad, x0, method`"lbfgs", **options)= returns
`(report, x)`. `x0` must already be a contiguous float64 vector.
An `lbfgs` run that spends its budget with `x` unmoved stops on
`LINE_SEARCH`, as the C `rgmin_minimize` does, not on `BUDGET`.
`require_convergence`, `error_on_unmet`, and `backward_polish` are flags
and default to off. `require_convergence` raises `NotConverged` when the
gradient norm is not below `gtol`. `error_on_unmet` raises
`StopUnmetError` when the run stops on `BUDGET`, `LINE_SEARCH`,
`LINE_SEARCH_ROUNDING`, `MACHINE_PRECISION`, `POLISH_UNMET`, or
`EVAL_BUDGET`. It is a
`RuntimeError` whose `report` attribute is the `Report` of the stop.
`backward_polish` is stored on the session. This step loop does not form
a Hessian, so
the polish itself is the C `rgmin_minimize_hess_opts` and
`rgmin_minimize_hvp_opts` entries.

`__version__` is the version string of the extension.

`c1`, `c2`, and `linesearch_maxiter` are the line-search constants.
They are accepted only together with `linesearch`, one of `brent`,
`backtracking`, `goldstein`, `wolfe`, or `ase`. Passing a non-default
constant alone raises `ValueError`. So does a `linesearch` the chosen
step ignores: any kind with `accept="step"` or on a method that takes
no line search, any kind but `wolfe` and `ase` on `lbfgs`, and `ase`
on a method other than `bfgs` and `lbfgs`.

# Two packages, one import name

Both packages install the import package `rgmin`, so an environment holds one of them.
The PyPI wheel (the repository root, nanobind) has `SolverConfig`, `Solver`, `minimize`, `Report`, `Stop`, `Method`, `NotConverged` and `rgmin.ase`.
It has no manifolds, no `Session` and no `lowest_eigenpairs`.
The maturin package under `python/` is not on PyPI and has `Session`, `LineSearch`, `LbfgsPairs`, `Stiefel`, `SPD`, `Product`, `lowest_eigenpairs` and `rgmin.optimize`.
@@rst::doc:`../howto/install`@@ shows how to build each one.

# Options of `SolverConfig` and `minimize`

Names are lower case, and `-` or a space reads as `_`.
An unknown name raises `ValueError` and lists the valid ones.
The PyPI wheel starts from `maxiter` 100, `gtol` 1e-8, `istep` 0.1, `memory` 10 and `maxmove` 0.
Those differ from the Rust `Control::default` (`gtol` 1e-5, `istep` 1) and from the C `rgmin_control_default`, so a script that moves between bindings should set them.

| Option               | Value                                              | Default | Meaning |
|----------------------+----------------------------------------------------+---------+---------|
| `maxiter`            | int >` 0                                           | 100     | Steps `minimize` takes. Zero returns a report without a step. A `Solver` takes one step per `step= call. |
| `gtol`               | float                                              | 1e-8    | Stop when the gradient norm is below it. |
| `istep`              | float                                              | 0.1     | Initial step scale. For FIRE it is the initial time step. |
| `memory`             | int >= 0                                           | 10      | L-BFGS pairs. |
| `nbfgscorr`          | int >` 1                                           | 10      | Correction pairs for `gromacs_lbfgs=. Other methods reject it. |
| `maxmove`            | float                                              | 0       | Euclidean cap on the step. Zero keeps the method's own caps, and a negative value leaves every cap off. |
| `atom_maxmove`       | float                                              | unset   | Per-atom cap on the longest atom displacement. `maxstep` is the same option. Unset keeps the method's default, 0.2 for L-BFGS. |
| `accept`             | `none`, `energy`, `nonmonotone`, `step`            | unset   | How a step is taken. Unset keeps the C session's `energy`. |
| `linesearch`         | `brent`, `backtracking` (`armijo`), `goldstein`, `wolfe`, `ase` | unset | Line search. L-BFGS searches none unless this is `wolfe` or `ase`. `ase` is ASE 3.29's search, on `bfgs` and `lbfgs` only. |
| `h0`                 | finite float > 0                                  | unset   | Initial inverse-Hessian scale of `bfgs` and `lbfgs`. Unset keeps the identity BFGS matrix and the Nocedal-Wright L-BFGS scale. |
| `stpmax`             | float                                              | unset   | Step-multiplier bound of the ASE line search. Requires `linesearch="ase"`. A value below 1 fails each search, as in ASE. |
| `c1`, `c2`           | float                                              | 1e-4, 0.9 | Wolfe and Armijo constants. Need `linesearch`. |
| `linesearch_maxiter` | int >` 1                                           | 20      | Trial budget of the line search. Needs `linesearch=. |
| `beta`               | a CG variant name, or `cg`                         | unset   | Conjugacy coefficient. Only for a CG method. `cg` is Polak-Ribiere. |
| `fire_variant`       | `rgmin`, `guenole2020` (`fire2`)                   | unset   | FIRE schedule. |
| `qn_step`            | `lbfgs`, `newton`, `rfo`                           | unset   | Quasi-Newton step. Newton and RFO need `Solver.step_hess`. |
| `neb_guards`         | bool                                               | unset   | Opt-in L-BFGS NEB guards. Other methods ignore it. |
| `periodic`           | bool                                               | unset   | Periodic cell. Drops rotation. |
| `project_rigid`      | bool                                               | unset   | eOn `lbfgs_project_rigid`. |
| `extra_updates`      | int >= 0                                           | unset   | Al-Baali extra updates. Accepted and without effect. |
| `cautious_eps`, `cautious_alpha` | float, set together                    | unset   | Li-Fukushima filter: a pair is dropped when s.y < eps * norm(s)^2 * norm(g)^alpha. |
| `noise_eps`, `noise_c` | float                                            | 0, 0    | Gradient noise floor. `noise_eps` <` 0 leaves it off, and `noise_c` <` 0 selects 3. |
| `objective_roundoff` | float                                              | unset   | Relative value window of the approximate Wolfe test, in place of the default four epsilon. Zero permits no rise, and a negative or non-finite value raises `ValueError`. |
| `etol` | float >` 0 | unset | Relative accepted-energy change stop. Unset disables it. A negative or non-finite value raises `ValueError=. |
| `max_evals` | int >= 1 | unset | Objective evaluation budget, including line-search trials. Unset disables it. |
| `nstcgsteep` | int >` 0 | unset | Steepest-descent restart interval of a `gromacs_cg` session. Omitted keeps 1000. Zero turns the periodic restart off. Another method raises `ValueError=. |
| `shrink` | float | unset | Refused-trial factor of a `gromacs_steep` session. Omitted keeps 0.5. The session accepts a finite value in the open interval (0, 1). |
| `max_constraint_shrinks` | int >` 0 | unset | Consecutive constraint-failure budget of a `gromacs_steep= session. Omitted derives it from the step size and the shrink factor. |
| `error_on_unmet` | bool | false | Raise `StopUnmetError` when the run stops on `BUDGET`, `LINE_SEARCH`, `LINE_SEARCH_ROUNDING`, `MACHINE_PRECISION`, `POLISH_UNMET`, or `EVAL_BUDGET`. `MACHINE_PRECISION` is unmet: the step can no longer move while the gradient is still above `gtol`. |
| `backward_polish` | bool | false | Record the backward-error polish request. This step loop does not form a Hessian. |
| `require_convergence` | bool                                              | False   | Raise `NotConverged` from `minimize` when the gradient norm is not below `gtol`. A first-order session step that took no move and left its state unchanged reports `STEP_TOLERANCE`. |

A count must be an int, and a flag must be a bool.
A kind or constant that the method ignores raises `ValueError` rather than being dropped.
Method names are `adam`, `bb`, `bfgs`, `cg`, `conjugate_descent`, `dai_yuan`, `diis`, `dogleg`, `eon_cg`, `fire`, `fire2`, `fletcher_reeves`, `fr_pr`, `gromacs_cg`, `gromacs_lbfgs`, `gromacs_steep`, `hager_zhang`, `hestenes_stiefel`, `lbfgs`, `liu_storey`, `newton`, `newton_cg`, `newton_pcg`, `ode12r`, `polak_ribiere`, `polak_ribiere_plus`, `pso`, `quickmin`, `rcg`, `rfo`, `sd`, `sr1`, `sr2`, and `steepest`.
Hyphens and spaces match underscores.
The `Method` enum does not expose `NEWTON_CG`, `NEWTON_PCG`, `POLAK_RIBIERE_PLUS`, or `EON_CG`. Those four are still accepted as names.
`gpmin` is a maturin `Session` token. It has no C method discriminant.

# Module `rgmin` in the maturin package

`Session(kind, n, **options)` is the stepper. `kind` is any gradient-only method token; `cg` is Polak-Ribiere-Plus, and `newton`, `rfo`, `dogleg` and `pso` are refused.
`step(x, callback)` takes one outer step and returns `(x, value, grad_norm)`, where `callback(x)` returns `(value, gradient)`.
`push_pair(s, y)` stores an L-BFGS pair without an evaluation and returns whether the curvature gate kept it. `pair_count()`, `steps`, `forget()` and `set_level_set(target)` complete it.
The options and their defaults are:

| Option            | Default | Meaning |
|-------------------+---------+---------|
| `max_atom`        | 0.2     | Per-atom cap. Non-positive leaves it off. |
| `maxmove`         | `None`  | Euclidean cap. Non-positive leaves it off. |
| `wolfe`           | False   | L-BFGS takes the strong Wolfe search. |
| `eon_cap`         | False   | L-BFGS takes the eOn capped step. |
| `memory`          | 8       | L-BFGS pairs. |
| `nbfgscorr`       | `None`  | Correction pairs for a `gromacs-lbfgs` session. Omitted keeps 10. Other methods reject it. |
| `h0`              | `None`  | Fixed L-BFGS inverse-Hessian scale. |
| `dt`, `dt_max`, `n_min`, `f_inc`, `f_dec`, `alpha`, `f_alpha` | 0.1, 1.0, 5, 1.1, 0.5, 0.1, 0.99 | FIRE parameters, the ASE set. |
| `preset`, `abc`   | `None`, False | `preset="guenole2020"` and `abc` select FIRE 2.0 parameters and ABC-FIRE. |
| `accept`          | `None`  | `none`, `energy` or `nonmonotone`. `step` is not accepted here. |
| `downhill`        | False   | The same as `accept="energy"`. |
| `istep`           | `None`  | Step scale of a method other than FIRE, whose scale is `dt`. |
| `level_set`       | `None`  | Target of the level-set constraint, as in @@rst::doc:`../howto/level-set`@@. |
| `scale`, `weight`, `noise` | `0.4`, `1.0`, `0.001` (or `0.3`, `2.0`, `0.004` when updating) | GPMin kernel length scale, weight, and observation noise. |
| `prior`, `update_prior_strategy` | `None`, `"maximum"` | Fixed GPMin prior mean constant or adaptive strategy (`"maximum"`, `"init"`, `"average"`). |
| `update_hyperparams`, `batch_size`, `bounds`, `unbounded_hyperparams`, `max_refinements` | `False`, `1`, `0.1`, `False`, `30` | GPMin marginal-likelihood hyperparameter update schedule and refinement cap (see @@rst::doc:`../howto/gpmin`@@). |
| `shrink` | `None` | Refused-trial factor of `gromacs-steep`. Omitted keeps 0.5. |
| `max_constraint_shrinks` | `None` | Consecutive constraint-failure budget of `gromacs-steep`. Omitted derives it. |
| `nstcgsteep` | `None` | Restart interval of `gromacs-cg`. Omitted keeps 1000. Zero turns the periodic restart off. |
| `cap_two_step_overshoot` | False | Cap FIRE 2.0 `dt_max` after one downhill step and an uphill reset. |
| `error_on_unmet` | False | Recorded on the session. One `step` stays `Ok`. |
| `backward_polish` | False | Recorded on the session. One `step` does not form a Hessian. |
| `etol` | `None` | Relative accepted-energy change stop. `None` disables it. |
| `max_evals` | `None` | Objective evaluation budget. `None` disables it. |

`rgmin.optimize.GPMin` (also re-exported as `rgmin.GPMin`) wraps `Session("gpmin", ...)` with `ase.optimize.GPMin`'s constructor signature, defaults, and `run(fmax, steps)` convergence flag, plus `maxstep` (default `0.2`, or `0.0` for ASE's uncapped steps) and `hyperparameters` property. `Session.set_gtol(gtol)` updates the session gradient tolerance and `Session.gpmin_hyperparameters` reports `(weight, scale, noise)`.
The other ASE-style classes in `rgmin.optimize` are `BFGS`, `LBFGS`, `LBFGSLineSearch`, `FIRE`, `FIRE2`, `SR1`, `SR2`, `SteepestDescent`, `GromacsSteep`, `GromacsCg`, `GromacsLbfgs`, `BarzilaiBorwein`, `Adam`, `CG`, `PolakRibiere`, `FletcherReeves`, `HestenesStiefel`, `DaiYuan`, `ConjugateDescent`, `HagerZhang`, `LiuStorey`, `FRPR`, `EonCG`, `RiemannianCG`, `NewtonCG`, and `NewtonPCG`.
`rgmin.ase` adds `BFGSLineSearch`, `LBFGSLineSearch`, and `QuasiNewton`.
`CG` there is Polak-Ribiere-Plus. `RiemannianCG` is `rcg`, and its per-atom cap stays off unless `maxstep` is set.

`LineSearch(kind, x, direction, istep`1.0, c1`1e-4, c2`0.9, beta`0.5, maxiter`40, tol`1e-10)` is the supplied search. `offer(f, gradient)` takes the value and gradient at `x`, then at each trial, and returns `(x, alpha, value, done)`. `done` is False when `x` is the next trial.
`LbfgsPairs(n, capacity`10)` is the pair memory. `push(s, y, rho`None)` returns whether the pair was stored, and `direction(gradient, h0)` returns `-H g` for `h0` a float, an array or a callable. `clear()`, `dim()` and `len()` complete it.
`Stiefel`, `SPD` and `Product` are the manifold classes of @@rst::doc:`manifold`@@.
`lowest_eigenpairs(hvp, x0_block, *, x`None, tol`1e-8, max_iter`None, precond`None, strict`True)` is block LOBPCG, as @@rst::doc:`../tutorials/eigenpairs`@@ shows. It raises `RuntimeError` for a pair that misses `tol` unless `strict`False`.

# Errors

`ValueError` means an option name or an option value is invalid, or a
coordinate array has the wrong shape. A count such as `memory` that
does not fit in a signed 64-bit integer is a `ValueError`. A count
passed as a float or a bool, for example `memory` set to `1.5`, is
also a `ValueError` whose message says it must be an int.
`TypeError` means an array has the wrong dtype or order, an option
value is not a bool, an int, a float, or a str, `method` is not a
string or a `Method`, or `f_and_grad` did not return
`(value, gradient)`.
`RuntimeError` means the solver is already in use on another thread,
or the native step failed. The message is the text reported by the
library. `Solver.step` on Newton, RFO, or dogleg, with no Hessian
callback, raises `RuntimeError`.
`NumericalError` is an `ArithmeticError`. It means the value or the
gradient was not finite.
`NotConverged` is a `RuntimeError` raised by `minimize` when
`require_convergence`True= and the final gradient norm is not below
`gtol`. `error.report` is the terminal `Report`.
An exception raised inside the objective is raised again on the
calling thread.

# Module `rgmin.ase`

`Optimizer` subclasses `ase.optimize.optimize.Optimizer`.
Named classes: `LBFGS`, `LBFGSLineSearch`, `FIRE`, `FIRE2`, `QuickMin`, `BFGS`, `BFGSLineSearch`, `QuasiNewton`, `SD`,
`Adam`, `Newton`, `RFO`, `SR1`, `SR2`, `BB`, `Dogleg`, `DIIS`, `PSO`,
`FletcherReeves`, `HestenesStiefel`, `DaiYuan`, `ConjugateDescent`,
`HagerZhang`, `LiuStorey`, `FrPr`, and `CG`.
`BFGSLineSearch` is also exported as `QuasiNewton`, and
`LBFGSLineSearch` subclasses `LBFGS`. Their constructors match ASE 3.29.0
([BFGSLineSearch](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.29.0/ase/optimize/bfgslinesearch.py),
[LBFGS](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.29.0/ase/optimize/lbfgs.py)).
`CG` defaults to Polak-Ribiere, the C method `RGMIN_POLAK_RIBIERE`.
`beta` can name another conjugacy token, including `polak_ribiere_plus`,
which is `RGMIN_POLAK_RIBIERE_PLUS`.

`run` returns a Python `bool`. `True` means the force criterion was
met.
`NotImplementedError` means `restart`, `read`, or `dump` on a class
other than `BFGSLineSearch` and `LBFGSLineSearch`, or a Hessian
optimizer called without `hessian`. Those two classes replay an rgmin
evaluation log from `restart`. Both run `linesearch="ase"`, a port of
ASE's `LineSearch`, and raise `RuntimeError("LineSearch failed!")` when
a search fails. `h0` and `linesearch="ase"` are opt-in `SolverConfig`
options: `h0` scales the initial inverse Hessian of `bfgs` and `lbfgs`,
and `linesearch="ase"` runs ASE's search on those two methods, with
`maxstep` limiting each trial increment of an atom. `stpmax`, 50 by
default, bounds its step multiplier and requires `linesearch="ase"`.
A failed search stops the step with `Stop.LINE_SEARCH`. Omitting both
leaves the session defaults.

---

Source: `docs/orgmode/reference/sota.org`

# State of the art

Every DOI on this page is in the `rgmin-docs` ookcite collection
and on @@rst::doc:`reference/bibliography <bibliography>`@@ after
`verify_references`.

## Unconstrained local minimization

The production method for a smooth unconstrained problem with an
analytic or fused gradient is limited-memory BFGS without a line
search. The eOn client does not line-search its L-BFGS step
(<https://github.com/TheochemUI/eOn>, `client/LBFGS.cpp`, commit
579738a9387e8d0ea55496f45dd057812cfab892; the client is described by
Chill et al., [10.1088/0965-0393/22/5/055002](https://doi.org/10.1088/0965-0393/22/5/055002)). The default cap is that
client's `max_move`, 0.2. The first step estimates curvature with a
finite difference of length 0.01 and sets `H0 = 1/C`. Later steps use
`(s · y) / (y · y)` when that quotient is positive, and the client's
`inverse_curvature` 0.01 otherwise. A proposal whose longest atom
move is at least the cap clears the memory and steps along `H0`
times the force (`distance_reset`). A direction that is not descent
does the same (`angle_reset`). Negative curvature clears the memory
and steps along the force at the cap. `LbfgsStep::Scaled` is the ASE
length control: shorten the two-loop step and keep the pairs.
`LbfgsStep::Wolfe` opts into the strong Wolfe search.
The force counts are `bench/results.md`.

- Nocedal 1980 introduced the limited-memory update
  ([10.1090/s0025-5718-1980-0572855-7](https://doi.org/10.1090/s0025-5718-1980-0572855-7)).
- Liu and Nocedal 1989 is the method used in practice
  ([10.1007/BF01589116](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01589116)).
- Nocedal and Wright, *Numerical Optimization*, chapter 7, records the
  two-loop recursion (algorithm 7.4) and the `H0 ` ((s.y)/(y.y)) I=
  scale (7.20) ([10.1007/978-0-387-40065-5](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-40065-5)).
- Wolfe 1969 is the curvature condition
  ([10.1137/1011036](https://doi.org/10.1137/1011036)). Algorithms 3.5 and 3.6 of Nocedal and Wright are
  the bracketing / zoom search.

Armijo alone is not enough for a quasi-Newton method. A pair that
decreases the value without measuring curvature poisons every later
direction. anneal measured that on Lennard-Jones 75: Armijo warm-start
was 1.8 times worse than discarding the memory; strong Wolfe reverses
the sign.

## Bound-constrained model

`Lbfgs.highs` keeps the two-loop direction and asks HiGHS only to
project it onto the trust region, the box, and any equalities
(`min 1/2 norm(p - d)^2`, `Q ` I=;
[10.1007/s12532-017-0130-5](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12532-017-0130-5)).
A dense compact Hessian is not a production QP: after a short accepted
step it is indefinite and the HiGHS QP solver does not return.
landfold `--highs` is this projection, not sequential LP.

## Bound-constrained reference

SciPy's `scipy.optimize.minimize(..., method="L-BFGS-B")` is the Byrd,
Lu, Nocedal, Zhu algorithm
([10.1137/0916069](https://doi.org/10.1137/0916069)), with the Morales and Nocedal 2011 remark on the
Fortran 778 code ([10.1145/2049662.2049669](https://doi.org/10.1145/2049662.2049669)).
Its `gtol` is an infinity-norm on the projected gradient.
`Lbfgs` defaults to that same infinity-norm so a hopping polish is
comparable to L-BFGS-B.

`Lbfgs::minimize_box` is that algorithm in this crate: the generalized Cauchy point, the subspace step and the projection test (@@rst::doc:`../howto/lbfgs-box`@@).

### Lennard-Jones, 75 atoms

The 75-atom Lennard-Jones (LJ75) protocol is anneal's `examples/warm_quench_lj.rs`: 400 relaxations from perturbed minima, overlaps repaired first, no bounds.
`examples/lbfgsb_bench.rs` rebuilds the same starts and traces rgmin.
`docs/figures/lbfgsb/bench_lbfgsb.py` runs SciPy 1.18.1 on those starts.
The `minimize` arm opts into `LbfgsStep::Wolfe`.
That is the strong Wolfe search these numbers record.
The default step stays the eOn cap, and this table does not time it.

| arm                                         | evaluations per relaxation | to `gmax <= 1e-5` | after | worst final `gmax` |
|---------------------------------------------+---------------------------:+------------------:+------:+-------------------:|
| `Lbfgs::minimize` with `LbfgsStep::Wolfe`   |                      314.4 |             291.5 |  22.9 |             1.94e-5 |
| `Lbfgs::minimize_box`                       |                      314.3 |             291.1 |  23.1 |             1.87e-5 |
| L-BFGS-B, `maxcor 8`, `gtol 1e-6`, `ftol 0` |                      278.5 |             252.6 |  25.9 |             1.29e-5 |
| L-BFGS-B, SciPy defaults                    |                      181.2 |       not reached |       |             5.63e-2 |

`gmax` is the largest absolute gradient component at the last accepted iterate.
The "to" column counts evaluations up to the first accepted iterate with `gmax <= 1e-5`; every run of the first three arms gets there.
The "after" column is the mean of what each of those runs spends past that point.
The two rgmin arms end in the same minimum on all 400 starts.
rgmin and SciPy agree on 382 starts.
Of the other 18, SciPy finds the lower minimum on 9 and rgmin on 9.

This page used to give 386.1 against 273.
Those runs used anneal's pinned rgmin, and the SciPy options were not recorded.
The Wolfe search now takes 314.4 evaluations against SciPy's recorded
278.5, 1.13 times.

Bound handling is not the cause.
LJ75 has no bounds.
SciPy skips its Cauchy point when a problem has none (`mainlb` in `scipy/optimize/src/lbfgsb.c`, SciPy 1.18.1, commit e4e854ea), and `minimize_box` costs what the Wolfe `minimize` costs.
All three converged arms reach `gmax <= 1e-5`; the two rgmin arms now
take about 291 evaluations to get there.
The remaining difference is the end of the run.
Near `gmax = 1e-6` the energy, about -380, changes only in its last bits, so the strong Wolfe zoom cannot meet its tests.
Before the rounding stop it spent up to 40 evaluations, dropped the
pairs, and spent up to 40 more from steepest descent.
The search now follows the relative-bracket warning of More and Thuente
1994 ([10.1145/192115.192132](https://doi.org/10.1145/192115.192132)) and stops when the step or value
cannot be resolved at machine precision.
On the measured 400-run trace, 5.9 evaluations per relaxation come
after the last accepted iterate.
SciPy's More-Thuente search (`dcsrch`) returns a warning once rounding blocks progress, and `lnsrlb` takes that point as the step.
With `ftol = 0` the run then stops at the first step that does not lower f (115 of 400 runs), on the gradient test (284), or on a failed line search (1).
It spends 0.1 evaluations per relaxation after its last accepted iterate.
With SciPy's default `ftol` the run stops much earlier, at a median `gmax` of 5.7e-3, which is not a converged relaxation by this page's test.

[[file:../../figures/lbfgsb/lj75_tail.png]]

Left: the median over the 400 starts of the best accepted `gmax` so far, against evaluations; a dot marks the median run length.
Right: mean evaluations before and after `gmax <= 1e-5`.
`docs/figures/lbfgsb/plot_lbfgsb.py` draws it from the two traces and prints the table above.

### A bounded problem

`driver1` of the L-BFGS-B 3.0 distribution is an extended Rosenbrock function on 25 variables.
The odd variables lie in [1, 100] and the even ones in [-100, 100].
The runs start from its own start, x = 3, and from 19 seeded starts in the box, with 5 pairs and a projected `gtol` of 1e-5.

| arm                       | evaluations per run | worst final projected `gmax` |
|---------------------------+--------------------:+-----------------------------:|
| `Lbfgs::minimize_box`     |                38.2 |                       9.87e-6 |
| L-BFGS-B, `ftol 0`        |                37.9 |                       9.78e-6 |
| L-BFGS-B, default `ftol`  |                34.0 |                       2.42e-4 |

All 20 runs of the first two arms meet the tolerance.
With its default `ftol`, SciPy stops first and none of its 20 runs meets it.

## Relative-decrease stop

The L-BFGS-B code also stops when one iteration lowers the value by
little relative to the value.
After a line search from `f_k` to `f_{k+1}`, `mainlb` in the 3.0
`lbfgsb.f` stops on this test
([10.1145/2049662.2049669](https://doi.org/10.1145/2049662.2049669)).

#+begin_example
f_k - f_{k+1} <= factr * eps * max(|f_k|, |f_{k+1}|, 1)
#+end_example

Its comments give `factr = 1e7` for moderate accuracy, and SciPy's
default `ftol` is that `factr` times the machine epsilon, about 2.22e-9.
`Lbfgs::ftol` is the same test, and its default of zero turns it off.
`LBFGSB_FTOL` is the SciPy value.
SciPy with `ftol = 0` still stops on a step that leaves the value
unchanged, while `Lbfgs` with `ftol = 0` skips the test.

`cargo run --release --example lbfgs_ftol` runs the default `Lbfgs` with
each setting.
The extended Rosenbrock runs start from `(-1.2, 1, -1.2, 1, ...)`, and
the Lennard-Jones (LJ) runs start from a cubic grid of spacing 1.1 with
a small jitter.

| problem         | evals, `ftol = 0` | evals, `LBFGSB_FTOL` | final `gmax`, `LBFGSB_FTOL` |
|-----------------+-------------------+----------------------+-----------------------------|
| Rosenbrock, 2   |                49 |                   48 |                     1.96e-5 |
| Rosenbrock, 10  |                92 |                   87 |                     1.33e-4 |
| Rosenbrock, 100 |               635 |                  620 |                     1.31e-4 |
| LJ7             |                58 |                   45 |                     2.33e-4 |
| LJ13            |               135 |                  101 |                     1.23e-3 |
| LJ38            |               415 |                  316 |                     3.42e-3 |

Every `ftol = 0` run ends with `norminf(g) < 1e-6`.
The test saves the most on the clusters, where `|f|` is well above one.
On LJ38 it saves 99 evaluations and ends 7.7e-6 above the energy of the
`ftol = 0` run.
A caller that needs the gradient below `gtol` keeps `ftol` at zero.

## Capped step for atomistic L-BFGS

`LbfgsStep::Capped` drops the line search. The two-loop direction
keeps the Nocedal-Wright scale `H0 = ((s · y) / (y · y)) I`
(equation 7.20). The step is shortened so the longest per-atom
displacement is at most the caller's cap, which is the ASE LBFGS
length control with the line search left off. An empty memory
steps along the force at that length. Pairs stay in the memory
when the step is shortened. The geometry step selected by
`set_atom_maxmove` still clears that memory when the quasi-Newton
step is longer than its cap, and it can spend further evaluations
on backtracking. The capped rule does neither.

`LbfgsStep::Scaled` is the step in the table below, not the default.
The default is the eOn reset described above.
`LbfgsStep::Wolfe` is the opt-in search, and `set_atom_maxmove`
selects the geometry step only after that opt-in. The cap is 0.2,
the eOn `max_move` and the length ASE publishes as `maxstep`, and it
is not refitted per problem.
`cargo run --release --example lbfgs_capped` repeats each arm
seven times, serially, and the wall time below is the median.
Evaluations do not change across repeats. Wolfe and capped rows
are `Lbfgs` with memory 8 and stop on `norminf(g) < 1e-6`. Their
gradient column is that norm. Session rows use memory 20 and stop
on the largest atomic force, 0.01. Their gradient column is that
force. Wolfe's evaluation counts are the counts already recorded
for `develop`.

| problem | arm | evals | median ms | gradient | value |
|---------+-----+------:|----------:|---------:|------:|
| Rosenbrock 2 | Wolfe | 49 | 0.012 | 1.74e-7 | 8.82e-16 |
| Rosenbrock 2 | capped | 46 | 0.023 | 1.33e-9 | 6.75e-21 |
| Rosenbrock 2 | geometry | 99 | 0.050 | 1.08e-3 | 2.36e-9 |
| Rosenbrock 2 | capped session | 45 | 0.071 | 3.24e-3 | 6.80e-9 |
